It’s going to be a busy Friday and Saturday at the school this summer.

A new curriculum will roll out in two weeks’ time and, because it’s mid-term, children’s teachers will be able to give them the extra attention they need.

And the good news is that, while it’s all going to change, it’s not going to be too disruptive for children and their families.

The Department of Education’s scheme on school meal schemes is going to last until the end of this school year.

Some teachers are still working out how they are going to do it. Some are worried about how to prepare the children to get involved.

So far, it’s been a good start.

The Department of Education is confident it can deliver the extra food and the changes to the curriculum as part of an agreed timetable.

It’s all a bit of a rollercoaster. It depends on the children, and how well they’re taught.

If they don’t get the extra attention they need, the school will be the first to suffer.

It’s the same for parents and for the children.

Teachers are nervous that they will have to adapt their teaching strategies to meet a timetable change.

One of the problems for teachers is that, as soon as the changes are put in place, they will find that they have to adapt their teaching.

A teacher who is struggling to find the right balance between what is important for children’s learning and what’s important for the children’s well-being needs to make a careful assessment of what is best for children’s learning.

If they get the right balance wrong, they will find that their teaching becomes less effective.

That’s what happened to a teacher who, without the right teaching strategy, saw her students struggle in some of their lessons.

Parents will be anxious.

A teacher in a school that uses the meal scheme will have to decide how to use the time during the mid-term break to prepare the children to get involved.

Teachers must also decide how they are going to prepare the children for the extra effort they will have to make in a way that meets the needs of the children.

It is possible for a teacher to look at the children and consider that some of them may not be well-prepared for the extra work they will need to make.

That’s why you have to be aware of how the children are going to react to the change.

Parents will be equally aware.

They may be worried about what will happen during the break.

But they need to be aware of their children.

They need to be aware of their children’s needs and their needs to be able to work effectively.

They need to know what the children need to be able to do at school.

It’s not too late to make changes.

It’s not too late to start making changes and to make changes that work for children and parents.

It’s a long process. But it can be made simpler and easier if teachers and parents start with the right information.

Lehman’s legal team said the court has made a “complete, serious and well thought out decision”.

“The Court of Appeal has now decided that the decision of the High Court was not only appropriate, but essential, in light of the facts and circumstances of the case.

Virus-like treatment to cure the flu

The experimental virus drug HU6 appears to have failed in tests in humans. But experts are sceptical over why the tests took so long.

Experts say the failure is another sign of the difficulty in finding a drug that could be useful in the fight against the flu.

The HU6 vaccine, also known as MERS vaccine, is based on the experimental virus that was developed at the Imperial College in London and by the Pasteur Institute in Paris.

The HU6 vaccine is said to be able to protect against the flu, respiratory disease, hepatitis A and B, meningitis A and B, and even HIV.

The vaccine also has a number of side-effects, including a rash and headaches, which doctors say can be treated with ibuprofen and other medicines.

However, HU6 appears to have failed in tests in humans, according to researchers at the University of Edinburgh and Imperial College London.

Their study, published in the medical journal PLOS Biology, found the vaccine failed in tests in 20 out of 30 volunteers.

Prof Jeremy Collinge, the senior author, said the reason for the failure was a long-running failure to predict which strains of the flu virus would respond.

The researchers said: “Despite the fact that our model has not been refined, and that the ability to predict future epidemics and viral evolution is limited, we are convinced that we can now predict that MERS-CoV is unlikely to be the virus responsible for the outbreak in the Middle East.”

However, the study was just a first indication of a potential vaccine.

Prof Collinge said: “Given the difficulties in producing new vaccines and the rapid development of new flu viruses, this is a significant setback.”

However, the researchers said the failure of the vaccine was not directly related to the problems in getting HU6 to work in the laboratory.

“We are confident that the failure of the MERS vaccine is a result of other potential issues, not a consequence of the MERS strain itself,” said Prof Collinge.

The study comes at a time when researchers are trying to find new ways to tackle the flu, but the current best-known approach is antiviral drugs.

The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases in Maryland, for example, is looking at different approaches.

It is also looking at a virus called vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV).

Experts say that VSV has been developed in a lab, and it may be able to take on the flu in the future.

Prof Collinge said that researchers had not been able to get VSV to work in humans, so it was difficult to assess the effectiveness of the new approach.

“If it was successful, it could revolutionise the approach to combat flu in general,” he said.

“It is not obvious that it is a good way to go about this.”

Another potential alternative approach, the one being developed by the University of Edinburgh and Imperial College, is to try a flu vaccine based on a live version of the H1N1 virus, a strain that has been circulating in parts of Asia.
headline: Experimental virus drug fails in human trials

A French climber, Noel Hanna, died on the first day of a two-week climb to the world’s tallest peak, Mount Everest, last week.

Noel, the son of an Irish mother and American father, has climbed to the top of the world’s highest peak three times, in 2012, 2013 and in 2015.

Last week he was killed on the first day of the second Himalayan summit at the summit of Mount Everest.

He was a member of an elite team at the highest altitude camp in Nepal, which is at 5,700 metres.

Hanna, 24, was travelling from Kathmandu to the camp at the summit when he died.

His death comes just days after a fellow French climber and a team from the US set a new record for the highest climbers in the world.

That was in 2015 when US climbers Brian Smith and Jason Dye, both 35, reached an altitude of 5,500 metres.

Hanna was on the mountain when his partner, Belgian climber Simon Beyster, died last Friday.

Hanna’s death has brought to the forefront a debate about climbing at the summit of the world’s highest peaks.

The two, as well as their two deputies, were put under arrest by the National Guard in the capital, Managua.

Muhammad Musa’s brother, Hani Musa, said he received a call from the police “the moment they put my brother in jail”.

The police also arrested another one of the Movement’s leaders, Jose Ramon Alegre.

Another deputy of the movement, Raimundo Guzman, had been detained for questioning at the headquarters of the National Guard on Sunday night.

Police said they were searching for suspected involvement in the assassination of President Daniel Ortega, the ruling party’s candidate for a fifth term in April’s election.
headline: Nicaraguan police arrest two more opposition contenders

A Ukrainian hospital was hit by more than 60 shells on Thursday during Russian-led military operations in the east, causing the death of one person and wounding of another.

In total, three people were killed and four more were injured when the shells landed near the hospital, a hospital official said.

The official added that a soldier was also injured in the incident.

The hospital’s building was damaged by the shells, and parts of the building had to be repaired.

“One person died and four others were injured when the shells landed at the hospital,” the hospital official told RTÉ News.

“We are expecting a big number of casualties from this incident.”

A military official from Ukraine’s National Guard, Viktor Sharyts, said the hospital was hit by shells in a mortar attack and that he was not in control of the situation at the moment.

“I’m not in control of the situation here at the moment,” Sharyts said.

The hospital was hit in the early hours of Thursday after the shelling and the building suffered damage.

“We’re not in control of the situation right now,” he added.

The incident follows a Russian-sponsored offensive in the east on Friday morning that has been escalating since its start earlier in the week.

The shelling of the eastern Ukrainian town of Myohiyiv in mid-January reportedly killed at least two people, injured three others and resulted in over the weekend in two Russian airstrikes on the city’s airport, with Russia blaming Ukrainian forces for the attack.

On Tuesday, Russian forces opened fire on an ammunition dump belonging to pro-Kremlin militia, a rebel commander told the BBC.

On Wednesday, Russia’s defence ministry said that the Russian military had started an operation in south-eastern Ukraine to "liberate" the city of Debaltseve, located in the country’s southwest, and the town of Mariupol, located in the country’s east.

On Thursday, Russia’s Defence Ministry announced that it had launched a new air and ground assault into Ukraine’s Donetsk and Luhansk regions, where Russian forces have been fighting pro-Russian separatists since 2014.

The Russian-backed troops have been fighting the separatists in their own city centres, which have been heavily bombed by pro-Kremlin militias.

This is not the first time that Russia has been involved in armed conflict in Ukraine’s eastern regions.

On July 17, the Russian military was also involved in the air strikes on a pro-Russian military camp in Donetsk, in which at least 15 people died and around 50 were injured.

This was one of the deadliest events during the conflict.

Earlier in February, the Russian military’s special forces claimed to have killed 25 pro-Russian militants in an operation involving air, artillery and a ground offensive.

The military said that they captured three of the dead in the operation in the Luhansk region.

The Ukrainian armed forces have said that Russian soldiers were present in the area as the fighting in the east continued.

The Ukrainian government’s military spokesperson told reporters earlier this month that the armed forces were on high alert following the developments.

Israel's elections next month could give the green light to a new and more significant Palestinian authority. The Palestinian Authority may be on the verge of its biggest change of form since the Oslo accords. The Palestinians could move beyond their two-state solution, which began with the Oslo accords, with a new one that is focused on the creation of a single state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip. This would be the first major shift in the Palestinian Authority since the Oslo era, and could take place alongside a new Palestinian government. But the Palestinian leadership is waiting to see what will happen at this week's elections in Israel.

The Palestinian Authority has held four general elections since 1994 but only two in Israel. The Palestinian Authority is part of the Palestinian National Authority. The Palestinian Authority is a Palestinian government. It is one of the parties to the US-sponsored peace talks.

The elections will take place next month in Israel. They are expected to be a referendum on the future of the Palestinians. But in the weeks leading up to the elections there has been speculation that the Palestinian leadership will shift its position.

In fact, the Palestinian leadership is working on an entirely new vision of the Palestinians. While the Palestinians are still dealing with the aftermath of the Oslo era, they have moved to a much more radical position on the one state solution.

Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in 2008. Photo by AFP

Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas is calling for a Palestinian state in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. He has called for a separate Israeli state and for the creation of an independent Palestinian state on the basis of the 1967 border.

Arafat's call for the creation of a Palestinian state was based on the 1967 borders, but as he got older he stopped supporting the idea. Abbas is now calling for the creation of a Palestinian state based on the 1967 borders.

Abbas says the Palestinian leadership has not accepted the 1967 borders as the basis for a solution because it does not believe it would work. But Abbas believes that the Palestinians have had enough of the Oslo process. He has been calling for the creation of a Palestinian state in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.

Abbas says that the two-state solution will work and it will be the only solution for the Palestinians. He says that the Palestinian leadership is prepared to accept the Oslo accords but that it will not accept any final status agreement that does not recognise the 1967 borders and includes the possibility of a separate Palestinian state.

The 1967 borders have never been the basis of a solution for the Palestinians. They only accept them as the basis for a state for the Palestinians. The Oslo process has not been about the 1967 borders but about a Palestinian state.

Abbas is also working on a new proposal, which he hopes will be supported by the international community, for the creation of a Palestinian state that would be independent of Israel.

The Palestinian leadership is working on a new approach to the Palestinian cause that is based on the 1967 borders. But it has changed its strategy. Abbas has gone from wanting to negotiate with Israel at all costs to having his sights on a single, sovereign Palestinian state based on the 1967 borders. Abbas has been calling for the creation of a separate Palestinian state, based on the 1967 borders, but he has made the Palestinians believe that they cannot achieve a Palestinian state on the 1967 borders.
headline: What's at stake in Israel's elections?

A judge today ordered the separation of the four-year-old boy with his father from the two women who are legally his parents.

The judge ruled that the pair cannot take the boy home with them or give him back to his mother until further orders.

Justice Michael O’Loughlin said the couple’s separation “appears to have been prompted by the boys’ mother’s own actions and not by the children’s welfare or the mother’s own desires”.

The judge did not order that the mother should return the boy to the father.

A statement from the Family Court in London said: “The Family Court is very concerned about the separation of the minor child from his father and the mother in the present circumstances.

“These actions are not in the best interests of the child and the mother and, under the circumstances of this case, he needs to be with his mother.

“There can be no other reason to separate the minor child from the father.

“The father has the right to claim the child, the mother has the right to claim the child, and it is in the child’s best interests to remain with his father.”

The couple, who are the grandparents of a seven-year-old girl and a nine-month-old boy, had been living separately for more than two years.

The father had been trying to take the boy away from his mother after she had been arrested for drug possession and shoplifting a mobile phone.

The judge said he found the couple were in a “very serious” breach of care and custody order and ordered that the parents should pay £1,500 costs and court costs.

He said the father was seeking to take the boy back to Ireland and that “any child taken away from his mother is a serious and irreparable breach of care and custody order.”

The mother had also been arrested and had been bailed to stay away from her son.

The boy was with the mother when he was taken into care in November 2012, the judge said.

He said the mother had left him on the steps of their flat in London with his sister and his other son.

The judge said the father, who had a criminal record, had been seen by a doctor the previous day and had been told he was suffering from alcohol abuse.

He said the father had been in the court “many times” before, and was “a person who would be able to work but his behaviour is very erratic and unpredictable.”

The father had told the judge: “I just have to do the right thing.”

He said his wife had refused him custody of the children but he was “tired of her and tired of her controlling him” and that he wanted to leave her.

The judge said he was “very concerned about the deterioration in the mother-child relationship.”

“The mother is now unwilling to do her part to protect the child from her husband and the court orders the mother to provide for the child by providing a foster home.

“The court orders the mother to provide care and support to the child by providing an extended family.
headline: UK court rules couple are legal parents of adult son

The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has achieved a crucial milestone, opening the first images of a black hole's innermost regions.

Researchers at the space agency's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California, the observatory's prime contractor, had already released three pictures of the black hole's supermassive central region, but now the Euclid team have taken the final images of the black hole, known as the Galactic Center (GC), the site of a massive star cluster.

As the researchers explain, the data are key evidence for how the black hole formed in the early days of the universe and how it remains at the heart of the GC for as long as it does. They will use the data to test theories of how black holes form and why they act the way they do.

The images were taken at the end of February. They were taken in an effort to provide "observational proof" for the theory that black holes form when a star explodes, a theory also being supported by the latest results from the Planck satellite.

The images were taken using a new generation of cameras on the telescope. That means that the team have been able to build up a much deeper understanding of the GC in unprecedented detail.

A black hole's gravity pulls everything within the event horizon, the space between the star and the black hole, towards the black hole. That means that even if you're sitting right next to the black hole, you will feel a tug on your body.

A black hole's density of mass is greater than that of a planet's atmosphere. That makes it harder for photons to escape from the black hole and light from stars to escape. The researchers say this means the black hole must have an enormous power source to maintain such a huge gravitational pull.

The team will use the new data to test theories of how the black hole formed and why it acts as it does.

This is the first time that the Euclid team have taken the images. The team plans to send the images to researchers on other space agencies in the future.

Image credit: ESO

The study of black holes is extremely complex and involves a number of disciplines, from astrophysics to cosmology. This study will attempt to explain how black holes form in the first place, using the new data.

The image was taken using two different sets of instruments, the two most powerful ones being a pair of telescopes on the Euclid telescope. The telescopes can detect light as far as 100 million light years away. That is a distance well beyond the furthest star and galaxy known.

The team's analysis of the images is expected to reveal the structure of the black hole, including the distribution of objects that have a black hole-like gravitational effect on them.

The images were taken over several months in 2016. Researchers say it's possible to use a super telescope, such as Euclid, to take pictures of the GC for a longer period of time than they were able to with their current instruments.

There are other ways to study the GC with space telescopes. NASA's Kepler space telescope uses three instruments to detect and study planets around other stars. Using this telescope would allow researchers to see the GC in more detail than they can now.
headline: Europe's Euclid space telescope releases first images

A fire at the Turkey-based ski resort of Aydin on Sunday killed 76 people after it began engulfing the building in flames.

“At least 76 people have died in Aydin,” said Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu in the aftermath of the fire, adding that there were “many injured and homeless people.”

The Turkish Red Crescent said that two helicopters carried out the rescue operation and two ambulances arrived on the scene within a minute after it started.

The Turkish Red Crescent said that the rescue operation was “difficult and delicate” and that there was no doubt about the safety of the people who were trapped in the building.

Aydin is the largest ski resort in Turkey, and hosts around 1,200 skiers and snowboarders each season. Its ski area covers more than 50,000 acres of land.

RTÉ News has been told that a helicopter carried out the rescue operation after it started. Two ambulances and a firefighting team arrived on the scene shortly after.

Aydin is the second largest ski resort in Turkey and is known for the Aydin Kale ski runs. The resort is renowned for its pristine powder snow.

“It’s difficult to determine what exactly happened, but this is one of the worst fires we’ve seen in Aydin this season,” a spokesman for the Turkish Red Crescent told RTÉ News.

Turkey’s prime minister said that the incident had affected families and communities across the country and asked the Turkish government to do more to help the victims.

“The most important thing is that the Turkish people pay attention to the situation in Aydin and the fact that the Turkish ski resort has the highest casualty rate this season. That is a serious situation and we ask for the Turkish government to take action,” he said.

According to the Turkish Red Crescent, a fire broke out at around 12.30pm on Sunday, when the building was engulfed in flames. The fire broke out in the kitchen area of the building.

“The fire broke out at the entrance to the hotel,” the spokesman said.

There were also reports that people inside the hotel and the kitchen area had been left unguarded.

RTÉ News has been told that there are three children at the hotel, all aged between four and seven, and the families of those children and those injured in the fire are demanding answers from the owners and employees of Aydin.

“The hotel has a number of children who are all under 12 years old,” the spokesman said. “It would be very wrong to say that there are no children staying there.”

Aydin is known for its pristine powder snow and the ski runs are easy to access.

Aydin has a reputation for the best skiing in Turkey and is popular with skiers and snowboarders from all over the world.

The Turkish government has pledged to make sure that the ski resort is rebuilt and fully operational in time for the 2016 ski season.

The fire has left many skiers stranded in Aydin, with the main resort having around 15,000 skiers and the smaller Aydin Aksaray having around 10,000 skiers.
headline: Death toll in Turkish ski resort fire jumps to 76 people

TURKEY – As Turkey looks to finalise details of its government's Housing
Plan for 2017, a key question is whether the government will be
committed to deliver the planned growth of housing in key areas
across the country.

In his speech to the nation in Ankara today, Prime Minister
Bulent Gül said that the government will allocate 1.8 billion
Turkish liras ($320.4 million) for a programme to build 10
million new housing units. The programme will also include the
purchase of new land for those units.

"This year we will allocate 1.8 billion liras to building housing. This
will include 1,000 housing units for each of the next four years.
With this we will achieve the target of building 10 million housing
units," he said.

"With this, we will be able to address one of the biggest concerns of
the Turkish people in the housing sector," he added.

"We expect these new housing units to be built in Turkey's
major cities and to be completed in a reasonable period of time
for these areas.

"Turkey's housing sector, according to the latest assessment, is
suffering from structural problems due to a lack of adequate
housing supply. We need to provide more housing in Turkey's major
cities in order to correct this and to ensure that the country can
become a country which creates jobs and economic growth."

The prime minister said that he would continue to seek
support for the Housing Plan, which he launched in late 2016, by
pressuring politicians and businesses.

"Turkey's housing supply is very important for the future of the
country, we are the biggest exporter of housing in the world," he
said.

The prime minister added that the housing supply
included new home developments as well as small homes for rental
and business owners.

"In order to achieve our goals, we need to support housing
investment, ensure that we provide good quality housing units to
people at the right price and create new housing sites in Turkey.
This is all part of our overall strategy," he added.

The prime minister said that he hoped the housing
plan would be finalized in the next few months.

The prime minister said that the Housing Plan will be the
largest ever programme in the history of the country.

"We will implement it in one year with the aim of completing the
housing supply in the country in the next year. This will be the
first step in a long-term strategy," he added.

The prime minister announced that the budget for the Housing Plan will
amount to 1.9 billion Turkish liras ($345 million) for 2017.

"We expect a large amount of funding for the Housing Plan in the
budget for the next year," he said.

On the issue of the housing supply, he said that the number of
housing units was declining in the country because of the increase
of population.

"We expect the number of housing units to increase by approximately
1 million this year," he said.

The prime minister said that the government has an important
responsibility to ensure that the country's housing supply is
sufficient for the growth of the population and the increase of
employment opportunities.
headline: 5 takeaways from Government's housing plan

TikTok spokesperson Ben Bowne told RTÉ News: "TikTok is a platform and its own responsibility. We have not been asked to take down our accounts, we have never been asked to do that."

Ms Hanafin also told RTÉ News that she would like to see legislation introduced into the next Dáil, likely to be the next budget, requiring social media platforms to take down the app if children are using it.

Ms Hanafin said that while social media companies have been reluctant to take down the app, in some cases they have been unwilling to remove the offending content.

Ms Hanafin said that she was confident the issue had to be addressed in the Dáil, which is likely to be in place at the next Budget due in the new year.

"There's no doubt that social media platforms need to be in control of the platforms but social media companies should not be allowed to be in control of the content that goes on in social media," she said.

TikTok has recently removed an advert from its app for a "sportswear" line which contained a "slim-cutie" girl wearing a swimsuit and singing a popular song.

A spokesman for the company said: "We apologise for any offence caused by the advert. We take the safety of our customers and their children extremely seriously and have removed the ad as soon as we became aware of it."

A spokesperson for the app said: "TikTok is committed to the safety of its users and the safety of our users' children, and has removed all the ads for the ‘SkinnyTikToki’ swimwear line."

Earlier this month, the Taoiseach responded to a recent video which was shared by TikTok user and former Miss Ireland Olivia Whelan.

She posted a video which showed two young girls wearing swimsuits, singing a song and making out with another girl while posing for a selfie.

A number of internet users took issue with the way the girls dressed and posed in the video.

The Taoiseach's spokesperson said that the video was "inappropriate" and the girls should not be involved in such activity.

Sean Quinn pledges not to trespass on Fermanagh quarry

Sean Quinn has pledged not to trespass on the Fermanagh quarry when the company plans to expand its quarry, reports the BBC.

The Taoiseach said he would ensure that no one was trespassing on the site.

“I want to assure the people of Fermanagh that I am committed to ensuring that no one is trespassing on the site of the quarry when it is developed,” he said.

“I will work with the company to ensure the environment and the safety of the people of the area are protected.”

Mr Quinn said Fermanagh had been a long term quarry site in the region, and said it was important the company’s operations did not interfere with that.

“The site is in such good condition that it should not become an eyesore or an issue for anyone,” he said.

He said he had “no problem” with people being able to get on the site and that the site had been used for “a long time”.

“I think people take it for granted. The site is in such good condition that it should not become an eyesore or an issue for anyone,” he said.

“As far as I’m concerned, there are people who work there and they are just doing their work and making a profit and I wouldn’t like to see that.”

He said people who worked at the quarry and who lived nearby had told him they did not have any problems.

The Fermanagh site is operated by the Fermanagh Development Limited (FDL), and will be operated by a joint venture between FDL and the Sullom Voe quarry owner, who have agreed to transfer the site to the joint venture.

Mr Quinn said the joint venture would have staff and contractors on site, “to make sure nothing untoward happens”.

He said the joint venture was “making sure it has what it needs”, and said that was a “great benefit to the community”.

FDL said the joint venture was “entirely independent”, and said it was “the people who built this quarry and they were doing their job”.

Fermanagh Development Limited said it was “the owner and operator of the quarry”.

It said the FDL site is the “main source of employment in Fermanagh”, adding that “we are committed to ensuring the welfare of all those who work on site”.

The joint venture has a contract for the supply of a series of stone slabs, which is due to be in place by the end of 2020.

“The purpose of the joint venture is to make sure that nothing untoward happens to the people of Fermanagh and surrounding areas,” said a spokesman.

Irish teacher in US to face trial over 'unruly' pupils

by John O’Shea

The Irish teacher arrested after a raid on his school was detained for three months and then released.

Dermot Keogh, 33, is in US custody after an FBI raid at his school, Kilkenny GAA, last week.

The school was searched by US police and Keogh, a teacher with the school for five years, was arrested at the scene.

Keogh has been charged with multiple counts of criminal mistreatment and abuse.

He was released from custody on Saturday afternoon but the US Department of Justice has been unable to put the charges down.

The US charges stem from the raid on the school on Friday.

The following are some excerpts from the arrest warrant for Keogh, obtained by RTÉ News:

“The defendants, along with others, were arrested for conspiring and committing certain acts, including illegal entry into the school building, illegal surveillance of school personnel and illegal entry of school property, by an agent or employee of the United States government.”

“The defendants were also arrested for unlawful entry into the school by an agent or employee of the United States government on November 18, 2012 and for unlawfully entering the school with the intent to commit a felony, specifically assault in the fourth degree.”

“The defendants, along with others, were arrested for conspiring and committing certain acts, including illegal entry into the school, by an agent or employee of the United States government.”

Inquiries into the alleged actions of a US agent in the operation have not yet been completed and therefore the US charges remain unproven.

The charges relate to the arrest warrant against Keogh and the charges are that he conspired with others to commit abuse and neglect of a child in the school and also to commit other crimes.

The accused is not accused of intentionally causing harm to a child.

During the raid on the school Keogh was seen screaming at and swearing at agents who were questioning the school staff, and he was seen threatening a school staff member and breaking a window with a sledge hammer.

The arrested teacher was released from custody on Sunday morning but the US Department of Justice have not commented on the charges.

RTÉ has been told by sources that the charges are serious and have the potential to cause the US to deport the teacher back to Ireland.

Irish Republic officials have said they will do everything they can to stop the teacher and are in touch with the EU, which could intervene to halt his deportation.

A source close to the Irish Government has confirmed that there are calls from EU authorities and the European Commission for the Irish Government to bring the teacher back home.

Irish Deputy Prime Minister for Foreign Affairs, Charlie Flanagan, has been asked by EU foreign ministers to speak to the Irish Government about the case.

The source said: “I would be very surprised if the government didn’t intervene, to stop the deportation.”

Keogh’s mother said: “He was treated well, but we have a complaint.”

A source in the Department of Education said that the allegations had been referred to the US attorney’s office.

MOSCOW (RIA Novosti) - Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko vowed on Wednesday to take measures against the threat from Russian nuclear-armed ballistic missiles.

The statement comes after President Vladimir Putin called for “a full-scale military confrontation” between Moscow and Belarus.

“The Belarusian army is in the process of building a system with a high-precision air defense system,” Lukashenko said in a speech in Moscow, adding that “it is necessary to be prepared for any eventuality.”

Lukashenko told Russian President Vladimir Putin that “we should use any means necessary to ensure our security.”

“We will have no problem in ensuring our security,” he said.

President Putin accused Belarus of trying to “strangle Russia”. He did not comment on the military nature of the missile system being developed by Belarus.

The development of the new missile system is likely to be a major political event in Belarus, where a former Soviet republic has long been a key target for Moscow.

The Russian Federation said last week it had deployed a new anti-ballistic missile system to Belarus. The system has been built by the Russian company SSC, an ally of the Kremlin.

The country is also a member of the European Union, which also has developed a missile system that can intercept ballistic missiles.

Belarus has already deployed two anti-ballistic missile systems to defend against potential threats from Russia.

Earlier this week, Lukashenko said Russia must take measures to stop the threat of weapons from Belarus.

“It is up to Russia to prove that it is not able to pose a threat to us and that is a task that they should take up,” he said.

“They cannot hide and will be forced to do so,” he added.

Lukashenko also said the country has a “strong and stable military.” He said Belarus will not back down from the fight.

“We will continue to do what we have to do to defend our security,” he said.

Russian President Putin said he was disappointed by the Belarusian decision to build the new missile system.

“These weapons and plans, if you wish, are not really in line with the Belarusian-Russian relations and there is nothing for us to do other than to try and solve the problem peacefully,” he said.

“These are weapons of war for the people of Belarus,” he said.

“It is not an improvement of the Belarusian armed forces. They are only putting them into a defensive position.”

The system will be able to target cruise missiles, he said, adding that it would make the country “safe for the first time.”

Belarus has also tested a new medium-range missile system in the past. Lukashenko said that in the event of a missile attack on Belarus, the country would be ready for retaliation.

“We can protect ourselves if and when the time comes to react to such an attack,” Lukashenko said.

“We are ready for anything,” he added.
headline: Belarus to hold Russian nuclear arms after 'pressure'

Judge Brian Hickey QC denies bail to a man who has been charged with assault after he attacked a woman in the early hours of Tuesday morning in Dublin.

The man, who cannot be named, will appear in court on Wednesday.

The assault, the third in four days in the centre of the capital, happened outside the home of one of the woman's friends.

The victim has been left with a torn retina, and it is feared she could lose the sight in her right eye.

The victim is understood to be in intensive care.

Mr Justice Hickey, in his judgment, described the attack as "unnecessarily violent and cruel".

It was a "callous" assault. "She is in a lot of pain and will be in a lot of pain for the rest of her life," he said.

"We know that from the witness statement we have received. We accept it," he said.

"I was concerned that at the end of the day, the alleged offence had not been completely cleared up by a court but there were very serious questions around the man's identity."

"If the charges are not heard in time, there is an implication of a miscarriage of justice," he said.

"I can't say that that would be acceptable in our court system," he said.

"The public interest is not served by a delay in the charges being heard," he said.

The judge said the alleged offence must be heard in the interests of the "public safety".

If the alleged offence was not heard by the end of next week, it will affect a number of other people in the city.

"I am concerned that if the charges are not heard in time they will affect the public safety in terms of the security of the city, and I am not saying that this is something that is acceptable to me," he said.

The man has been charged with common assault and two counts of gross indecency.

The victim was in the company of the man's sister when he went into the house.

He said he had a "bad feeling" as he walked into the house.

He went into the front room, with the sister and the woman who lived there.

The victim saw the man approaching, and she went to the front room and told her friend to call the police.

She then saw the man walking towards the room.

"I said 'you're not allowed to be in here," the victim said.

The man then took her by the arm and pushed her towards the front door.

He pushed her, and at one point he put his hand over her mouth.

"I don't know what happened after I left the room," she said.

"I can't hear the phone. I just heard the door close."

She says she was in shock, and didn't know what to do.

"I don't know what to do about it. I just stood there and I was in shock," she said.

"I got up and I was going to call the police and go. And I saw him come up and I saw his face and I just couldn't believe it. It was something out of a cartoon."

The woman is understood to be in her 30s.

The court heard the sister had a boyfriend who was a witness for the prosecution. He had said that she was with the victim for a couple of weeks at the time the mother went missing.

The jury was told the sister had gone with her boyfriend to visit her sister who was ill. The jury was told this was some time before the mother went missing.

The court heard that the boyfriend did not have any contact with the mother.

The court also heard how the victim had been with a woman for some time and was “very close” to her.

The court also heard how the sister had no idea her mother was in the car park.

The court also heard how the sister had come back with her boyfriend “very late”.

“One sister had the opportunity to come to the police and say she was not involved in the disappearance of the mother and was in no way involved,” said Judge Desmond.

He said “the fact that the sister had come back and said she was not involved” was “conclusive” that the sister had not been involved in the mother’s disappearance.

The judge told the jury it was the sister’s statement that was “not proof that the sister was involved”.

The judge said the sister had not wanted to come forward because she didn’t want to get involved.
headline: Sister didn't want to report mother missing, court told

Irish Independent, 10:30pm Tuesday September 9, 2017

The Government has allocated €6.4 million for a new “defective blocks” scheme, which will provide support to a further 1,100 households in Dublin and Cork.

The move was made after a report by the Government’s own adviser, a project director at the Department of Housing, Planning and Local Government, which revealed that almost half of the households were in “defective blocks” and that they were at risk of being demolished.

The scheme’s architect, Dr Michael Cahill, said: “The new programme will enable local authorities to help tenants on the lowest-priority lists to improve their housing stock.”

Dr Cahill also said that the scheme would have the support of a national infrastructure bank that would finance new and existing projects, to help fund the scheme.

The scheme is the biggest ever to be set up in the country.

Dr Cahill said: “When we have an Irish housing crisis we need to work together to build the next generation of homes.”

The architect added that the Irish Government were in a “unique position” to help with the scheme, as it had the “best system of housing finance in the world”.

Cllr Joe Byrne, Sinn Féin’s housing spokesman, called for the scheme to be cancelled, saying: “It’s not right that the Irish Government are putting a scheme out there for the benefit of the 1,100 families who can least afford to buy new homes.”

Cllr Byrne said: “The current government cannot be seen as championing the poor as it has done with this scheme.”

Cllr Byrne has also called for more investment in housing.

He said: “It’s time for the new government to invest in building more homes and stop throwing the poor under the bus.”

The new housing scheme will provide “housing for a significant number of Irish households who do not have sufficient equity or sufficient income to buy a new home and have not made a payment in three years.”

The Irish Independent has also contacted the Department of Housing, Planning and Local Government for confirmation that €6.4 million has been allocated for the scheme.

The Government has also confirmed that €6 million of funding for the scheme is coming from the Department of Social Protection, but it has not been disclosed in the budget papers.

“The Irish Government is working with Irish State Housing Institutions to identify, coordinate and support those most in need with regard to their housing needs.”

Cllr Byrne said: “This is an Irish Government housing scheme that has been designed in a foreign fashion and with a foreign contractor, the Irish Government has put it out there for the benefit of the 1,100 families who can least afford to buy new homes.”

“This scheme is not fair. It is designed to benefit the few over the many, and that is wrong.”

Cllr Byrne is also calling for the Irish Government to provide more investment in housing.
headline: Half of homes in defective blocks scheme need more work

EU citizens living in the UK can receive official documentation from the European Union

Over three million EU citizens living in the UK can receive official documentation from the European Union.

The EU is expected to announce today that more than 3.1 million citizens who were born in the UK have applied to stay in the EU.

More than half of the applications are for permanent residents who are living in the UK for more than three years.

However, there are also applications for foreign nationals who are studying or have been approved for jobs by the UK and would like to stay in the country.

The EU has approved new rules to ensure the applications are valid and to speed up the approval process.

“In some cases applicants have made the mistake of applying for the wrong EU nationality,” said the European Union’s spokesman, Paolo Martino.

“But since the system of application was introduced in January 2016, many mistakes have been prevented.”

The spokesman said the EU was now expecting that the number of applications will rise.

The spokesman added that some EU countries were now also applying to speed up the process for applicants.

The spokesman said: “Our current rate of approval for EU nationals living in the UK is currently about 4,000 per month, and we expect this to increase.”

As a result of the increased number of applications, the EU is launching an EU-wide online portal to give all of the EU’s citizens access to the system.

The spokesman said: “For the first time, all EU nationals who have access to our online portal will be able to apply to stay in the UK, to study in the UK or to work in the UK, as well as to be able to receive official documents from the UK.”

The spokesperson added that the number of applications for EU nationals who are working or studying in the UK would increase to about 3.2 million within the next three months.

“The majority of these applicants will be British-born or British-citizen nationals who would like to stay in the UK but have not yet been approved,” he said.

“We are expecting these first applications to continue rising in the coming weeks.”

The spokesperson said a new procedure that allows the European Parliament to approve applications for EU citizens who have had a period of residence in the UK and have been working or studying in the UK would also be introduced.

He said: “As of today, we expect that a small number of EU citizens living in the UK will be able to get access to the application and approval system via the new online portal.”

The spokesperson said the change would allow the EU to take back responsibility for the approval of EU citizens.

“The European Parliament will have the possibility to review, by way of an amendment, the status of applications made before it,” he said.

The spokesman added that it was a good time to allow people to apply for the first time.

“We expect that most people will have had their applications already approved already, so there is no need for the new process of review,” he said.
headline: Over three million EU citizens apply to stay in UK

LONDON - Sea swimmers will head out into the ocean near the south coast of Ireland on Saturday as part of the annual Dublin-Belfast Swim meet.

The event, which attracts around 30 swimmers from Ireland, England, Scotland, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands, will take place at the Port of Dublin.

The event is set to take place at various venues in the area over the coming weeks.

The US Navy has deployed two warships to join a fleet of ships patrolling the eastern coast of Venezuela.

The deployment comes as tensions between President Nicolas Maduro’s government and opposition-led opposition have escalated in the past two months.

The Navy says that it is carrying out a “moves to reassure” in order to prevent a confrontation.

“The US Navy is on station in the waters off the Venezuelan coast to reassure US citizens and to assist in maritime surveillance and safety efforts,” the Navy said in a statement.

The statement added that it is “pursuing” an operation “to increase maritime surveillance around Venezuelan waters to help prevent an escalation of tensions and to support national security.”

The statement went on to say: “The US Navy is working to further expand maritime surveillance capabilities in the waters off the Venezuelan coast,” and that the move was being made “in coordination with our Government and the Government of the United States.”

“We urge the Venezuelan Government to engage with the United States and other world powers to deescalate the situation in Venezuela.”

The deployment comes at a time when tensions between the Maduro government and opposition have been escalating.

The Venezuelan opposition-led opposition has been in a diplomatic standoff with Maduro’s government for more than three weeks over allegations that he and other leading members of his government have been living off the country’s oil wealth.

The US has also backed the opposition, in part, by deploying an ‘anti-terrorism’ force.

The US, however, has repeatedly slammed the Venezuelan government for mismanaging the country’s oil wealth.

READ MORE: US ships in US waters near Venezuela

Read more: US forces take part in joint war games with South Korean forces

The US has also called on the Venezuelan government to release all those detained in the country, who are facing charges related to protests. The US has also urged the Venezuelan government to release its top three political leaders and the former president, Nicolas Maduro, who are currently in US custody.

The US has been involved in the Venezuelan conflict since August 2014, when Washington backed the country’s opposition against then-president Hugo Chavez.

At the time, the US said it was worried about the influence of the government on its own people and accused Chavez of having been “too lenient with those who disagreed with him.”

Chavez was elected president in 1998, and his rule was marked by economic and political liberalization.

Since then, Venezuela has seen unprecedented inflation, food shortages and a sharp drop in the country’s GDP.

The US is the biggest supplier of oil to the country, which imports most of its fuel.

With inflation and food shortages worsening, many Venezuelans have taken to the streets to protest against the economic and political situation they face.

The US has blamed the government of Maduro for Venezuela’s problems.

Chavez himself has said that he blames the US government for the country’s woes.

The country was last in the world economic ranking of the top ten producers of oil, with oil exports decreasing by 12 percent in 2013 to 959,814 barrels per day.
headline: US deploys warships amid fears of Venezuela conflict

A locum GP has said he will “never” serve an order of the Medical Council over his care of a patient who has been diagnosed with a rare form of cancer.

The doctor will “be the first person to have ever stood on the same stage as the Medical Council’s medical adviser”, the GP said.

Dr John O’Neill said he was in the same situation as he was three years ago when a patient with a rare form of breast cancer was referred to him at his surgery.

“I’ve been to the Medical Council’s hearings, I’ve read the judgment, I’ve listened to what they’ve said,” he said.

“I think there are very few situations where a doctor can go against the Medical Council.”

Dr O’Neill was referring to the Medical Council’s decision in 2014 to revoke the doctor’s registration over a minor slipup, which led to a series of apologies from Dr O’Neill and the Medical Council, including one to Dr O’Neill that resulted in his licence being suspended for six months.

“I stand by my previous comments, I’ve never gone against the Medical Council over something like this, and I’m quite surprised and disappointed with the judgment.

“As a result of the judgement the council has suspended my medical registration.”

Dr O’Neill said he expected the council to give him his license back, but insisted he could continue his practice “with impunity”.

“If the medical council is happy with that then it is up to them to restore my licence and then I can be in my surgery,” he said.

He claimed he has had a number of people contact his surgery to apologise for him, and that he has not received any complaints from patients.

In 2014, he was suspended from his practice over a minor slip up, and subsequently lost his medical registration, a fine of £2000 and his licence to practice medicine.

A spokesman for the Medical Council said it was a “tragedy” that Dr O’Neill had lost his registration, and that it was “regrettable that a physician should be making such serious allegations about the judgment”.

“We are pleased that he has withdrawn his comments. He has been suspended from practising and we have apologised to him personally.

“We have no power to intervene in the way that a judge might with regard to the decision of the Medical Council.”

A spokesman for the Medical Council said: “We regret that an individual has expressed such a strong view, and we are disappointed that a decision on the judgment was taken against a doctor who was given a fair hearing and who made a serious mistake.”

“However, we have no power to override the judgment.”

The spokesman said Dr O’Neill should “understand that a medical tribunal will have no power to rescind the medical registration that he has lost, and that no action will be taken against him in any circumstances.”
headline: Locum GP before Medical Council over care of patient

Dublin, Ireland

11th February, 2013

A new wave of protest, and calls for a no-fly zone over Gaza, has spread across the city of Dublin following the recent killings in Gaza.

Protesters gathered at various locations in the city this weekend, including the University of Dublin, where they unfurled a banner that read “Gaza, End” and were joined by a large number of Irish Jews.

The protest, known as the Free Gaza demonstration, follows the murder of an Israeli soldier by a Palestinian gunman on February 17.

Protesters at the University of Dublin, including Irish Jews, have unfurled a banner that reads “Gaza, End”. Photo: Kevin Maguire.

Since the beginning of this month, Dublin has experienced a wave of mass protests and has had several incidents of violence, including riots at the city’s colleges, a police raid on a Jewish neighbourhood and at the Israeli embassy, as well as a number of incidents of looting.

In the wake of the Gaza killings, protesters have called for an end to the Gaza conflict.

The protest was joined by members of the Jewish community, and in particular the Dublin Jewish Community Council, which is based in the city. The Jewish community has also been active in calling for a no-fly zone over Gaza.

In the event that the protest continued into the weekend, a large number of Israeli citizens, both citizens and visitors to the country, were prevented from entering Israel. In addition, there were reports of an attack in the Gaza Strip and reports of a firefight at the Israeli embassy in Dublin.

A member of Dublin’s Jewish community holds up a sign in front of the Israeli embassy, where protests against the killing of an Israeli soldier are taking place, in Dublin, on Saturday. Photo: Kevin Maguire.

Dublin has been a focal point in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict since the beginning of the 1990s, when Israel’s first prime minister, Menachem Begin, was elected. Since then, the two sides have been locked in a dispute over land, refugees and territory.

In addition, many Irish Jews have been killed by either Palestinians or Israelis in the Middle East, a fact that has not been lost on the Jewish community, which has been active in calling for a no-fly zone over Gaza.

The Israeli government has said that it is not opposed to the protest in Dublin, and has stated that the city is welcome to host a protest.

The Israeli Embassy in Ireland has also stated that it welcomes protests in Dublin, and has encouraged protests in other cities throughout the country.

Protesters in front of the Israeli embassy in Dublin, on Saturday. Photo: Kevin Maguire.

As for the Palestinian Authority, which controls the Gaza Strip, the Foreign Minister has called on Israel to “respect the borders of the Palestinian Authority and the Gaza Strip”.

In addition, the Foreign Minister, Tzipi Livni, has stated that Israel should not interfere in the internal affairs of the Palestinian Authority.

In response to the recent protests in Dublin, the Palestinian Authority has stated that it would not be interested in hosting protests.
headline: Dublin protesters call for end to Gaza conflict

A Newry man has died following an accident on Mount Conaghy in west Kerry.

Newry and Kerryman Martin Foyle, 40, was a member of the Mountain Rescue Corps (MRC) and part of a team trying to reach the summit of Mount Conaghy when he was forced to make an emergency descent after falling from a cliff face on Saturday, the MRC said.

“He died on impact with the ground below,” MRC spokesman John Sheahan said.

“He did not have a harness on and was unable to descend from the descent to the point of impact. He was wearing an oxygen mask and had a medical condition. He fell 200 metres to the ground.”

Foyle died at about 4.30pm on Sunday. His body was recovered by a MRC colleague at about 5pm.

“It is with a heavy heart that the MRC is sharing with the families the tragic news of the death of Martin Foyle. His family has requested a period of reflection, in the hope of finding some comfort in the knowledge that he had an excellent life and will be sorely missed,” said the MRC.

Foyle was born in the village of Ballygaleen in County Antrim and grew up there. He was a member of the Mountain Rescue Corps (MRC) in the area since 2006.

On Saturday he was taking part in the Mountain Rescue Corps' Operation Mountain Rescue in Co Kerry when he fell from a cliff face on Mount Conaghy.

He was a member of the Mountain Rescue Corps for about three years, he worked on the mountain rescue service for about ten years, and was a member of the Rescue Squad in 2008.

“He was a member of the rescue squad for about 10 years, he was with the rescue squad for about ten years and he was a member of the MRC in the area for about three years," Ms Sheahan said.

"When he died, that is a total loss. His family will be sad, the funeral will be a huge loss and the people of Newry will be very sad.

"It is also a total loss because he was an exceptional person who, even at the age of 40, had a very good character and was very reliable and that was why he was a good member of the Mountain Rescue Corps.

“The MRC is very disappointed. The family will be upset and the community will be very upset with their loss.”

The Mountain Rescue Corps has two teams: an Operations team and a Rescue team.

The Operations team is responsible for the safety of the Mountain Rescue Corps' members and the Rescue team for the rescue of Mountain Rescue Corps' members.

Mount Conaghy is a rock, about 120 metres high and a little more than 2km in length, and is one of the most difficult mountain routes in the world to reach by foot.

Mount Conaghy is one of four highest mountain routes in Ireland and the highest peak in the western part of the country.

On Saturday Foyle, a member of the Mountain Rescue Corps, was part of a team trying to reach the summit of Mount Conaghy.

Foyle died on impact with the ground below. He was wearing an oxygen mask and had a medical condition.
headline: Man dies while climbing Kerry mountain

A rare Roman coin was auctioned last night in Geneva in a spectacular bid by one of its most famous owners.

The coin, which has been referred to as the most valuable coin to ever come from the Roman Empire and the third-most valuable coin in the world, was bought by a private collector for $6.5 million.

"In a sense, Brutus has been around for nearly a century. But now, he is to be auctioned in Geneva with all his friends and family present," said a spokesperson for the auction house, BnF, which is representing the buyer, Domenico Luchetti.

The coin is considered a very rare item. Only a handful of such coins, valued at $150 million, have ever been sold.

It is made up of two layers of gold and is valued at $6.5 million. It is dated on the obverse side to the year of its creation, which is known as "The Great Year of Brutus". This year was the year of the murder of Julius Caesar.

The reverse side is also marked "The Great Year of Brutus".

"There is a significant difference between a coin and an object," said Domenico Luchetti, president of BnF. "The thing we are buying is not an object or a work of art. It is a coin."

"It is certainly an object of art, because it is a piece of history, and it is a coin of the Roman empire, which is not a very ancient place," he said. "And that is an important point to consider."

The other side is inscribed "The Great Year of Brutus".

"He (Caesar) was not a man of his time, in terms of ideas and values, so he had many differences with the Romans," said Luchetti.

The coin was sold for $6.5 million, which is the lowest price ever paid for a Roman coin.

The coin was acquired in the auction of the same name, also held last night in Geneva. A small, one-ton coin worth £1 million was sold, as was the same-named coin worth £2.5 million. A small gold piece worth £1,000 was sold.

The auction last night included two more coins, which were sold for $4 million and $4.5 million, respectively.

BnF's Luchetti did not know when he was going to receive the coin.

"I had a lot of hope and a lot of anticipation for it," said Luchetti.

He said he was optimistic about the coin being in the auction for a long time.

"From the moment I saw it, I knew we had a good chance. And from the moment I saw it, I believed it would be in an exceptional place," he said.

"That is why we are going to take it. It is such a rarity.

"And I am confident that the price will reflect that," he said.

BnF was not the only bidder for the coin. One of the other bidders was a private collector who was paid $500,000.

The coin had been purchased by a private collector, who asked not to be named.
headline: Rare Roman coin featuring Brutus up for auction in Geneva

LONGBOATERS preparing to return to the US for the first time in almost two years, after the US government lifted a travel ban on people who were living or working in the country illegally.

But on Saturday, the White House said it was reopening the travel ban for people coming from the Philippines, but only if the person had not been caught using illegal drugs or committing a crime while in the US.

As it stands, anyone with a US green card or visitor’s visa is barred from entering the US without a visa for 90 days.

The change comes as President Donald Trump pushes for comprehensive immigration reform, which some US officials say could create new categories of immigrants that require a visa to enter the country.

The US said it had seen no evidence of such a change in immigration policy.

‘This is a very important step for our nation. It allows a significant number of our citizens who have not been convicted of a crime to return to the country,’ said White House Press Secretary Sarah Sanders.

‘As part of the efforts to build a safer, more modern, more prosperous America, we are taking steps to give back to our citizens who have been affected by past illegal immigration and who have been unfairly separated from their families.’

The US government has been forced to take these steps following widespread protests, with over 1.2 million people signing a petition last week urging the government to lift the ban.

While some Americans were in tears on Saturday, others showed a mix of anger and sadness in the face of the news.

‘We were very sad, but we are very proud of our country,’ said Megan McCaig, who has been staying with her father in Brooklyn, New York. ‘I am very happy to be here, I don’t feel like I’m going to go back to the US just yet.’

A large gathering of people gathered on the streets of New York City to show their support for the people of the Philippines.

A US State Department statement read: ‘It is the US government’s position that travel by those already in the United States is not a security threat and the US government has no interest in preventing further illegal immigration from the Philippines.

‘In a related matter, the US government recognizes that the temporary ban on travel by those already in the United States was not intended to be permanent,’ it added.

‘The U.S. government is not waiving or canceling the travel ban, but will continue to exercise its authority to remove individuals who pose a risk to the security of the United States.’

The temporary ban was issued in January and lifted in June.

‘In the wake of the news that the travel ban was lifted, I was heartened to see a larger and more diverse gathering of the Filipino community,’ said Rosalinde Santamaria, executive director of the American Filipino Council.

‘It was a very moving and heartening moment,’ she said.

US Senator Mazie Hirono said that the travel ban was an ‘example of the type of immigration reforms that are needed’.
headline: Tourists prepare to return to US as travel ban lifted

On Tuesday, the Irish Post Office began issuing fines of €12,000 and €13,000 for non-payment of tax. For the first time, Ireland has introduced a new penalty that affects non-payers of the €8.6 billion in public services provided by the Post Office. It is the first penalty since the law was enacted in 2011.

The new penalty applies to non-payers who cannot be bothered to pay their tax by the due date.

The fines are for “the total amount of interest, penalty, or penalty interest incurred.”

As part of the new law, which is being introduced in the Post Office’s first year of operation, the Post Office must notify the taxpayer of any “non-compliance with a tax payment deadline.”

The Post Office said in a statement that it will make the penalties “more clear to the taxpayer as well as in-court hearings.”

The Post Office’s fines will be applied only if an individual’s tax returns are filed on time for the relevant year.

“The penalties we will impose are the total amount of interest, penalty, or penalty interest incurred by an individual. These penalties are set out in a legal notice and will only be imposed if it is clear to the taxpayer that they have not paid all the tax due,” an Post Office spokesperson said.

The penalties are applicable to tax returns lodged on or after June 1st, 2011.

“In addition to the interest penalty, the Post Office may impose further penalties where the taxpayer has failed to pay the tax due by the due date. The penalty will also be assessed if the taxpayer’s return is not filed for tax due by the due date,” the spokesperson said.

The fines apply for non-payers who do not pay their taxes by the due date but are still in the process of doing so.

“The penalty will be applied to the total amount of interest, penalty or penalty interest incurred,” the spokesperson added.

The Post Office said it is not aware of any other jurisdictions imposing similar penalties.

The new penalties will apply to non-payers who cannot be bothered to pay their tax by the due date.

The Post Office said in a statement that it will make the penalties “more clear to the taxpayer as well as in-court hearings.”

The Post Office said it will apply the penalties “to a maximum amount, determined by the Secretary of State, of €12,000 for a tax year.”

The Post Office will be applying the penalties to individuals who owe €8.6 billion in tax or €12,000 in interest, whichever is the higher.

“The Secretary of State may waive the penalty where an individual’s tax returns are not filed for tax due by the due date, or where the interest penalty is not a reasonable and fair charge on the tax due,” the spokesperson said.

Under the new law, the Post Office will also be applying the penalties to individuals who do not pay their tax by the due date and fail to pay penalty interest.

The Post Office will assess the penalties if an individual’s tax returns are not filed for tax due by the due date.
headline: Postmistress welcomes reports of €12k State subvention

A pet can cure the most serious illnesses, such as cancer and diabetes.

The Kennels, which are run by a former vet with experience working with sick animals, are dedicated to the care and well-being of sick cats, dogs, reptiles and fish. The pet owner visits the animal’s cage on a daily basis, to ensure that the animal is eating and drinking, and has not lost weight. The owner has a pet sitter visit the kennels regularly to ensure the animals are in good health.

When the owner visits the kennels to clean out the cages, the cat or dog receives a small treat in the form of a small piece of kibble with an extra treat for the kibbles (cats and dogs) or a small piece of raw chicken in the form of a piece of chicken.

The treatment, if needed, is given by the owner, on a daily basis, in the form of an injection with a small quantity of sterile saline solution that is needed for the animal to take.

If the animal becomes ill, and the owner’s pet sitter does not visit the kennels, the owner will take the pet home with her and the owner will not have to carry the pet on her back 24 hours a day.

The treatment given to sick animals is not life-saving but is a life-sustaining intervention.

The Kennels website states: “The kennels were built with the purpose of being a ‘home for sick animals’, and the kennel was the first such facility open in Ireland. For more than 20 years the kennels have been able to provide care and support for the ill animals and their owners.”

It is a privilege that the Kennels receive the highest proportion of clients, the highest proportion of clients of any veterinary practice in Ireland, and the highest number of people who visit the kennels every day.

“We have to make sure the kennels are maintained properly and always provide a good service for the animals and their owners,” the Kennels website states.

“If your pet is sick, we will visit the kennels on a regular basis to ensure your pet is healthy and enjoying a good life, and we also encourage owners to take their pets in for treatment.

“If your pet is not sick, we will provide support by visiting the kennels with you to show that our goal is to provide the best possible care and well-being for our clients,” the Kennels website states.

According to RTÉ News, the Kennels have a total of 32 kennels, in total, throughout the year.

“I’m still getting to know these kennels and it has been a pleasure working with the Kennels for the last five years. It’s a privilege to help the Kennels continue to provide the best veterinary service possible,” Dr. Kevin MacRae, of the Kennels, said.

“The Kennels are in the same situation as any other clinic, and although this is not a medical treatment, the vets are really happy to work with the Kennels for the animal’s wellbeing,” Dr. Kevin MacRae, of the Kennels, said.
headline: Cian's Kennels reunites sick children with their pets

On Tuesday, the Australian government said it would go ahead with a new government-sponsored pay equity agreement with the Irish public service, despite legal challenges from the Association of Government Procurement and Supply (AGSI).

The decision follows the disclosure by the Public Service Association (PSA), and its chief executive officer, Mr Paul McGurk, that he had been informed by the minister in charge of pay policy, Shane Ross, that the deal was in jeopardy.

Mr McGurk said he would not attend the next AGSI pay policy conference in Melbourne. The conference is being organised by the Department of Finance.

AGSI said in a statement that, “despite repeated invitations to attend the conference, Mr McGurk has made it clear to PSA officials that he is not attending and he is in agreement with PSA’s chief executive, Mr Paul McGurk.

“Mr McGurk’s absence will result in the loss of another opportunity to discuss the pay issues facing the public service and a loss of crucial information as to what Government officials are considering as part of a proposed new deal for public service pay.”

The conference is being organised by the Department of Finance, and is the first of its kind to have been held.

The Department of Finance is a statutory body under the Public Service Association Act, which deals with issues such as pay issues.

Mr McGurk was appointed chief executive of the association last year. Mr McGurk is also a member of the Department of Finance.

The Department of Finance and the Public Service Association met with Finance Minister Paschal Donohoe in a meeting on Tuesday.

AGSI said it is seeking an adjournment of the Public Service Conference to allow for the outcome of the legal challenges.

“Our legal team is reviewing the issues relating to the AGSI’s legal rights, including our right to a fair hearing, and will provide further advice to our client, PSA, as soon as possible,” the association said.

The Association of Government Procurement and Supply (AGSI) said it was pleased the Department of Finance had allowed for the postponement of the conference to allow for the resolution of the legal matters.

It noted that PSA had not indicated that it had any specific concerns about the pay deal for the public service.

The department said it would not comment on the legal challenges.

The Public Service Association’s pay policy conference, which is being held in Melbourne, will be addressed by the department’s pay chief, Mr John Loughnan.

Researchers have found microplastics in the breath of bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) from Ireland to the Netherlands and Belgium.

Dublin’s Marine Institute (MI) said it detected microplastics in the dolphins' exhaled air from the Irish area of Mullaghadore in Co Clare to the Belgian region of Meuse-Rhine. The dolphins were fitted with metal cages for the purpose of collecting the samples.

Analysing samples from the bottlenose dolphins and other cetaceans, the researchers found that they were likely to have ingested microplastics from the surrounding oceans.

Microplastics are plastics with a size of a tiny fraction of a millimetre. They are considered one of the fastest-growing and most problematic pollutants, as their presence is linked to health problems such as Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s.

The study shows that the Irish area of Mullaghadore is the first one to be affected by the presence of microplastics in the marine environment.

The study suggests that this is the result of a long-term issue with marine debris occurring in the area which has led to accumulation of plastics in the area.

The researcher who led the study, Dr M. R. C. O’Reilly from the Institute of Marine Sciences at UCD, said the result was “very significant”.

He said it was “very encouraging” that the area was being monitored for the presence of plastics and that the discovery of microplastics in the dolphins’ breath was the first of its kind in Ireland.

The Irish Coastguard is also monitoring the area.

Dublin is the world’s leading centre for marine mammals in terms of the number of bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus), and is also the first place in the world where a study has been carried out on the impact of the presence of plastics on marine mammals.

The study was carried out by the Institute of Marine Sciences at UCD.

November 19, 2015

Ebola virus disease (EVD) is one of the world's most devastating diseases, killing an estimated 4,300 people a day in West Africa alone.

The virus is spread by direct contact with blood or other bodily fluids from an infected person or from an infected person's body fluids such as blood, saliva, semen or vomit.

The virus is extremely infectious and can be spread through the air by coughing and sneezing.

The virus can also be spread through the blood of infected individuals or through the body of an infected individual if they are not screened or have been exposed to an infected individual.

The virus is spread by contact with the blood of an infected person or with bodily fluids that have come in contact with infected people, such as vomit.

The virus can also be spread by aerosolised particles.

This can occur when the virus enters the blood stream through the nose.

The virus can also be spread by infected individuals touching objects such as bedding, curtains or equipment.

If an infected person coughs or sneezes, or touches a person's mouth, nose or eyes, the virus can be transferred by the contact.

The virus is also spread through the air when a person breathes in contaminated air. This can occur if a person's airways become blocked, such as by illness or surgery.

This also happens when an infected person is exposed to other people.

This can happen for example when an infected person coughs or sneezes and they breathe in contaminated air.

The virus can also be spread by contact with infected patients' clothing, bedding or objects.

The virus can also be transmitted from a contaminated person's bed or living quarters.

If an infected person coughs or sneezes, or touches a person's mouth, nose or eyes, they can also transmit the virus to that person's body.

A number of things can reduce the risk of the virus spreading from person to person. These include:

not sharing living spaces;

cleaning and storing items that have come into contact with infected people;

washing hands with soap and water after having come into contact with infected people;

not touching the eyes or mouth of a person with the virus; and

using a facial mask.

Screening for the disease is one of the most important things that can reduce the risk of the spread of the disease.

Screening for the disease involves:

having the healthcare worker complete a questionnaire about the medical history of the person they are caring for,

following the questionnaire with a second question about symptoms, and

having the healthcare worker record their results in a form that can be used to inform the person concerned.

In the West African country of Guinea the healthcare worker was trained to recognise patients with Ebola and patients with other diseases and was then asked to make an immediate assessment.

"We were instructed to refer patients to the relevant health facilities for further investigation, and then send them home with the message 'don't come in here, don't come in there' to all the staff," the woman who attended the training told RTÉ News.
headline: Explained: WHO's high-risk Ebola emergency
