text:
A Dublin man has launched legal action against EirBord Stáit (EBS) and Ulster Bank, alleging a systemic failure on the part of both entities to forward payments made to a former business partner. The man, who wishes to remain anonymous, claims he has been the victim of a complex financial malfeasance that has led to significant financial loss.

According to court documents, the plaintiff made several payments to his former business associate through EBS and Ulster Bank between 2017 and 2020. He alleges that despite these payments being processed successfully, the recipient never received any funds, leading to a protracted legal battle to recover his losses.

The plaintiff contends that both EBS and Ulster Bank failed to adequately investigate and resolve the issue when initially reported, leading to a protracted and frustrating experience. “I paid out thousands of euros in good faith,” the man stated in an interview, “and it’s taken years just to get justice.”

Legal representation for the plaintiff maintains that the banks and the post office service provider have a duty to ensure that all transactions are accurately processed and that recipients receive their rightful funds. They argue that the lack of accountability and timely resolution of this matter constitutes negligence and breach of contract.

The case has been assigned to the District Court, where the plaintiff hopes to establish the extent of financial damage incurred and seek appropriate compensation from both organisations. A spokesperson for EBS declined to comment on the specific case while Ulster Bank stated that they would defend themselves vigorously, citing internal procedures and protocols that were followed during the transactions.

This case highlights ongoing concerns about the integrity and reliability of financial systems in Ireland, particularly regarding electronic and postal payments. Legal experts suggest that such issues may be indicative of broader challenges within the financial sector, prompting calls for enhanced regulation and oversight to prevent similar occurrences in the future.

The plaintiff remains hopeful that justice will be served, but acknowledges the uncertainty and stress involved in the legal process. “I just want my money back and some kind of closure,” he said.
headline: Man sues EBS and Ulster Bank over alleged failure to forward payments to former partner

text:
The Health Protection Surveillance Centre (HPSC) has confirmed 4,141 new cases of coronavirus in Ireland today, bringing the total number of cases since the start of the pandemic to over 865,000. This figure represents a significant increase from yesterday's tally of 2,873 new cases, with health officials warning that the Omicron variant's rapid spread continues unabated.

The majority of these new cases have been reported in Dublin (1,353), followed closely by Cork (595), and Limerick (213). The HSE is urging the public to remain vigilant and adhere to current public health advice, particularly regarding social distancing and wearing face coverings.

Health Minister Stephen Donnelly stated in the Dáil that while the healthcare system remains robust, it faces growing pressure due to the surge in infections. He called on citizens to prioritise vaccination and boosters, noting that they remain the most effective way to combat the virus and its variants.

The Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, also addressed the nation, stressing the importance of following public health guidelines and highlighting the need for booster programmes to continue. "While we continue to face challenges, our healthcare professionals are working tirelessly to support those who fall ill," he said, adding that the Government stands ready to introduce further measures to control the spread if necessary.

Meanwhile, the Gardaí are increasing patrols in areas where large gatherings may be occurring, particularly at nightclubs and other venues known to attract younger crowds. Superintendent Ciarán O'Mahony stated that the safety of the public remains their top priority and that they will take action against any breaches of public health regulations.

Health service staff are being advised to take extra precautions, especially those working in high-risk areas such as hospitals and care homes. The Health Service Executive (HSE) has activated additional contingency plans to ensure adequate staffing levels and patient care can be maintained despite the rising numbers.

The spread of Omicron has raised concerns among health experts about potential surges in hospital admissions and ICU occupancy. Public health officials are closely monitoring trends and adjusting strategies as needed to mitigate the impact on the healthcare system.
headline: 4,141 new Covid cases as Omicron spread continues

text:
Dubliner Pat Shortt has long been a champion of Irish music, from traditional to contemporary genres. Born into a family with deep roots in music, Shortt's passion for Irish culture began at a young age. He recalls being mesmerised by his grandfather playing the fiddle and his mother singing Irish ballads.

Shortt’s journey through the cultural landscape of Ireland has seen him work across numerous mediums, including broadcasting, live performances, and educational programmes. A frequent face on RTÉ Radio, he brings a wealth of knowledge and enthusiasm to every interview and feature. His commitment to preserving and promoting Irish music has been evident throughout his career, whether through his contributions to the annual Celtic Connections festival or his work with emerging artists.

A pivotal moment in Shortt’s career came when he was tasked with curating a series of programmes celebrating Irish traditional music for RTÉ. This involved not only highlighting local talent but also ensuring that the music reached a wider audience. “It was about finding new voices while honouring the rich heritage of Irish music,” he explains. “The challenge was to make it accessible and appealing to younger generations.”

Beyond television and radio, Shortt has been a driving force behind several music festivals and events in Ireland. His involvement in the founding of the National Concert Hall’s Celtic Connections in Dublin exemplifies his dedication to fostering a vibrant music scene. The event has since become a cornerstone of the Irish music calendar, attracting both local and international performers.

His influence extends beyond the stage and screen. Shortt has been a mentor to many aspiring musicians, offering them guidance and advice. “I believe in the power of music to bring people together,” he says. “It’s a universal language that can bridge cultural divides and inspire change.”

Pat Shortt continues to be a cultural figurehead, inspiring future generations to embrace their Irish identity and heritage. His legacy is not just in the music itself but in the way he has engaged and educated audiences, ensuring that Irish culture remains a vibrant and evolving part of our national story.
headline: Culture that made me: Pat Shortt

text:
A young baby was rushed to Cork University Hospital after a suspected petrol bomb attack at a local housing estate on the outskirts of the city. This incident marks the second petrol bomb attack in two days within the Cork area.

According to local reports, the attack occurred in the early hours of the morning when a device was thrown near a property in the Ballincollig area, just a few miles from the centre of Cork. Eyewitnesses reported hearing a loud bang and seeing flames before the device exploded, causing minor damage to the property but fortunately no one was injured initially.

However, a nearby house where a baby was sleeping suffered significant heat damage, leading to the child being airlifted to Cork University Hospital as a precautionary measure. The baby’s parents have been kept informed and are currently with their child at the hospital.

The Irish Defence Forces were called to the scene to assist the Gardaí in securing the area while the incident was investigated. The local Garda station has also increased patrols in the area to provide reassurance to residents.

Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin expressed his concern over the attacks and called for swift action from authorities to ensure public safety. "These types of incidents have no place in our communities," he stated in a statement released to the media.

The Office of the Attorney General has launched an immediate investigation into the circumstances surrounding these petrol bomb attacks. Taoiseach's office issued a statement urging citizens to come forward with any information they may have regarding the attacks.

Community leaders have condemned the acts and appealed for calm. "Our community is reeling from such senseless violence," said Mary O'Sullivan, the local mayor, adding that support services are available for those affected.

Local businesses and residents are being advised to remain vigilant and report any suspicious activity to the Gardaí immediately. The National Community Safety Forum has offered its assistance to help coordinate community response efforts.

The Health Service Executive (HSE) has assured that all necessary medical care is being provided to the baby, with specialists on standby to provide any further treatment required.

As investigations continue, residents in the Ballincollig area are left to grapple with the fear and disruption caused by these recent attacks. Authorities are working around the clock to solve the case and bring those responsible to justice.
headline: Baby taken to hospital following second petrol bomb attack in Cork

text:
A striking piece of street art, which may be the work of the elusive British artist Banksy, has recently been discovered at the foot of a prominent London skyscraper. The artwork, located near the O2 Arena in Greenwich, has quickly become the subject of media and public speculation.

The piece features a large rat wearing a balaclava, sitting on a bench, with its hand resting on a small bag of cash. The image is instantly recognisable as a hallmark of Banksy’s distinctive style, with its blend of social commentary and humorous undertones.

Banksy, known for his satirical and political posters and graffiti, has managed to maintain a mysterious identity, evading capture and attribution of many of his works. This new piece has reignited interest in the artist's elusive nature and has attracted both fans and critics of his work.

Local authorities and property owners have been notified of the artwork’s discovery, and officials from the O2 Development Company are currently assessing the situation. While the company has not yet commented publicly, they are likely to face questions about how such a significant piece of graffiti came to be placed near one of their major venues.

The appearance of the artwork has also sparked discussions about the role of street art in urban landscapes and the potential legal issues surrounding unauthorised artworks in public spaces. Advocates for street art argue that it adds vibrancy and character to cities, while opponents highlight concerns about property damage and vandalism.

In the meantime, thousands of people have flocked to take photos and admire the artwork, some even speculating that it could be another masterpiece by the enigmatic artist. The rat balaclava has become a symbol of curiosity and intrigue, drawing attention to the ongoing debate around street art and its place in contemporary society.
headline: Artwork thought to be by Banksy appears at foot of London skyscraper

text:
The accounting examination, which drew thousands of participants, appears to have been particularly well-suited to those students who had engaged in extensive preparatory work. According to many of those who sat the exam, the questions were closely aligned with the material covered in their study programmes, suggesting that those who had put in the most practice were better prepared.

A TD from Cork South-West highlighted the importance of adequate preparation, stating, "It is clear that the exam was designed for candidates who had been diligent in their studies. Those who did not engage in sufficient revision may have found themselves at a disadvantage."

The chief examiner, Professor Michael O'Sullivan of Trinity College Dublin, agreed, noting that the majority of questions were reflective of the syllabus content. He commented, "The examiners aimed to ensure that it was both fair and challenging. It seems that those who adhered closely to their study plans and took the time to thoroughly understand key concepts fared well."

However, some students expressed concerns about the pressure faced during the exam, particularly given its length and complexity. One student from Galway remarked, "While I felt that the questions were within the scope of what we studied, there was a sense among many that the exam demanded a level of detailed knowledge that required significant preparation."

The Health Service Executive (HSE) also monitored the exam day operations across various centres, ensuring that all necessary provisions were in place for candidates. Dr. Sinéad Mulcahy, Director of Health Services Research and Development at the HSE, stated, "Our teams worked diligently to support all candidates, and we received positive feedback regarding the overall environment and facilities provided."

As the results begin to roll in, many are looking forward to seeing how the exam aligns with predictions made by educators and experts in the field. The results will be eagerly anticipated by students and educational institutions alike, serving as a significant milestone in their respective journeys.
headline: Accounting exam suited 'match fit' students who had done 'plenty of practice'

text:
The Greek Prime Minister, Kyriakos Mitsotakis, has extended what he described as a "hand of friendship" to Turkey, in a significant step towards mending relations between the two long-standing rivals. The overture comes at a critical time for both nations, with Greece facing ongoing disputes over maritime borders and energy resources in the Eastern Mediterranean.

Speaking at a press conference in Athens on Wednesday, Mitsotakis stressed the importance of dialogue and mutual respect in resolving outstanding issues. He highlighted that the gesture was not just about easing tensions but also aimed at fostering regional stability and prosperity.

"I believe that by extending our hand of friendship, we can begin a new chapter of cooperation and understanding," Mitsotakis said. The Greek leader indicated that he would be open to discussions on maritime boundaries, exploring economic partnerships, and enhancing cultural exchanges.

Turkey’s President, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, while initially cautious, welcomed the initiative. "We are open to dialogue and cooperation with all our neighbours," Erdoğan stated during a speech in Ankara. However, he added that any engagement would be predicated on respecting Turkey's interests and historical claims.

Analysts suggest that this move could have far-reaching implications for the region, particularly in the context of ongoing negotiations over gas fields in the eastern Aegean Sea. It may also impact Greece's relationship with other countries in the region, including Cyprus, which is a key partner in the natural gas exploration efforts.

Greece and Turkey have been embroiled in a protracted dispute over territorial waters and airspace rights, leading to numerous tensions and conflicts. This latest development marks a shift from previous confrontational approaches, potentially opening the door for more peaceful resolutions.

The offer of friendship is expected to be closely watched by the international community, especially given the strategic importance of the Mediterranean for trade and energy security. Both countries are members of NATO, adding another layer of complexity to their bilateral relations.

As talks progress, observers will be closely monitoring whether this extension of goodwill translates into concrete actions that address the core issues dividing the two nations. For now, both sides appear committed to exploring avenues for improved diplomatic and economic ties.
headline: Greek PM willing to extend ‘hand of friendship’ to long-time rival Turkey

text:
The relief was palpable at a Dublin police station this evening after a 45-year-old woman who had been reported missing was found safe and well following a thorough search operation. The woman, a resident of north Dublin, went missing on Tuesday afternoon and her disappearance caused considerable concern among her family and friends.

Detective Garda Eoghan Ó Cearúl, speaking to journalists outside the Garda Station, confirmed that the search was called off following the woman’s safe recovery. “We are delighted to inform the public that the search has been concluded with a positive outcome,” he stated. “Our officers, supported by colleagues from the HSE and members of the community, conducted a comprehensive search of the areas where she was last seen. We would like to extend our thanks to everyone involved in the search efforts.”

The woman was last seen walking near her home in the early evening on Tuesday. Her family immediately alerted the Gardaí, who began a coordinated search operation. The search included teams from various districts, deploying search dogs and specialist equipment to cover all possible areas.

“I would like to reassure everyone that such incidents can happen to anyone, regardless of their age or circumstances. It is a testament to the hard work and dedication of the Gardaí that we were able to locate her so swiftly,” said the woman’s mother, who remained visibly emotional during the brief statement.

Community leaders also praised the swift action taken by the authorities. “The quick and efficient response from the Gardaí and emergency services was crucial in this situation,” said Councillor Niamh O’Keeffe, a local representative from the area where the woman was found.

While details surrounding the specific location where the woman was found are being kept under wraps pending further investigation, it was confirmed that she was reunited with her family later in the evening.

The incident serves as a stark reminder of the importance of vigilance and the support available from the community and emergency services. The Garda Commissioner, Mr. Denis Casey, expressed his appreciation for the public’s assistance and called for continued cooperation in similar situations.

As the woman’s case continues to be reviewed by the Gardaí, the focus now shifts towards understanding the circumstances leading to her disappearance. Initial inquiries suggest that she may have experienced some form of temporary disorientation, which led to her departure from her usual routine. Further updates on the matter will be provided as they become available.
headline: Woman, 45, missing from Dublin located safe and well

text:
Parents often find themselves racing against time to document every precious moment with their children. From the first smile to the first day at school, every milestone is a fleeting yet crucial part of a child’s journey. In the digital age, where social media and photo apps dominate, capturing these moments can feel more overwhelming than ever.

Photographer and parent, Sarah McCarthy, recently took to Instagram to share her tips on how to mark these milestones and make lasting memories. "The key is to be present," she advises. "It's not about the perfect shot; it's about the emotional connection you share with your child."

McCarthy recommends setting up a small, dedicated space at home for keeping mementos and documenting these milestones. "A photo album or a box of keepsakes can be incredibly sentimental and provide a sense of continuity," she says. "Every item—be it a drawing, a toy, or a handprint—tells a story."

For those looking to commemorate special occasions beyond the usual photos and videos, there are myriad creative options. Personalised children's books, where the child's name and voice are integrated into the narrative, offer a unique way to immortalise a particular moment. "These books become cherished items for the child to revisit as they grow older," explains children's author, Fintan Doyle.

Doyle also suggests creating a family tree or timeline, which can be both educational and emotionally enriching. "It helps the child understand their place in the family and provides context for their life events," he notes. "Plus, it’s a project that everyone in the family can contribute to over the years."

The role of grandparents in this process should not be underestimated. "Grandparents can offer a different perspective and nostalgia, which can enhance the value of these memories," says Dr. Aoife Murphy, a psychologist who specialises in child development. "Involving grandparents in capturing these moments can create a richer, more connected family narrative."

Moreover, parents should be mindful of the impact of technology on children. "While technology can be a wonderful tool, it's important to balance it with real-life experiences," advises Murphy. "Encourage outdoor play, storytelling, and other activities that foster imagination and creativity."

Ultimately, the most valuable gifts are often the experiences shared and the bonds formed. So, the next time your child achieves a milestone, take a moment to pause, connect, and cherish the moment together. After all, it's the quality of the memory, not the quantity of photos, that truly matters.
headline: Marking milestones and making memories

text:
The world of late-night television was plunged into mourning on Monday as it was confirmed that the legendary American talk show host, Larry King, had died at the age of 87. King, whose long-standing career spanned decades and earned him the moniker "the most asked man in America," passed away in Los Angeles after battling complications from Alzheimer's disease.

Larry King hosted his influential talk show, Larry King Live, for more than two and a half decades, during which he interviewed countless high-profile personalities, including world leaders, celebrities, and other public figures. His ability to connect with guests from all walks of life made him a unique and beloved figure in the media landscape.

Irish audiences were among those who tuned in regularly to watch King's show, where he would often feature Irish celebrities and politicians, showcasing the rich tapestry of Irish culture and talent to a global audience. One such guest was former Taoiseach Bertie Ahern, who praised King's work, saying, "Larry was a true gentleman, and his ability to engage with his guests was unparalleled."

King's personal life was marked by tragedy and triumph. He married twelve times throughout his life, often drawing comparison to another famous serial monogamist, Errol Flynn. Despite these challenges, King remained a tireless advocate for various causes, including human rights and HIV/AIDS awareness. In 2006, he founded the Larry King AIDS Foundation, which aimed to support research and education efforts related to the disease.

His death was mourned by many across the globe, including the Irish community. A statement issued by the Irish Embassy in the United States expressed condolences and noted King's significant contribution to international broadcasting. "Larry King’s influence on global television is immeasurable," said the statement. "His dedication to his craft and his unwavering commitment to sharing stories and experiences with a wide audience will be sorely missed."

As news of his passing spread, tributes poured in from colleagues and fans alike, celebrating King's legacy and the indelible mark he left on the media industry. "Larry was one of a kind," said Anderson Cooper, a co-host of CNN who frequently appeared on King's show. "He brought so much warmth and humanity to our screens."

Larry King's funeral arrangements have yet to be announced, but his family has requested privacy during this time. His legacy, however, is secure – a testament to his enduring impact on entertainment and journalism.
headline: Legendary talk show host Larry King dies aged 87

text:
The Northern Ireland Chief Medical Officer has issued a stark warning to the region’s public, urging them to prepare for the possibility of a second lockdown as the threat of a third wave of the coronavirus pandemic looms. Dr Michael McBride made the plea during a televised address, stating that if stringent measures are not adhered to, a return to full lockdown is a real and imminent risk.

“Given the current trajectory of the virus, it is clear that we must remain vigilant and take all necessary precautions,” Dr McBride said. “The situation in Northern Ireland now mirrors the challenges faced by other regions earlier in the year, where a lack of compliance with social distancing and other protective measures led to significant increases in infection rates.”

He highlighted recent trends, noting a worrying rise in cases among younger age groups, who had previously been less affected by the virus. “Our modelling shows that if we continue on this path, we could see hospitalisations and ICU admissions spike again within the next few weeks,” he added.

Dr McBride emphasised the importance of continued adherence to public health guidelines, including the wearing of face masks, frequent hand washing, and maintaining physical distance from people outside one’s household. He also called for increased testing capacity to quickly identify and isolate cases to prevent further spread.

The call for preparedness comes as Northern Ireland grapples with a rising number of cases and hospitalisations. Health Minister Stephen Donnelly has already announced the extension of a regional alert level system that includes restrictions on social gatherings and businesses, but these have not yet reached the most severe levels seen during previous lockdowns.

Speaking on behalf of the public health community, Professor Jonathan Bell, Director of the Public Health Agency, echoed Dr McBride’s concerns. “We need everyone to play their part in stopping the virus from spreading. A second lockdown is not inevitable, but it is a very real possibility if we do not act now,” he stated.

The government has also faced criticism for its slow response to vaccine distribution, with only a small percentage of the population vaccinated so far. Dr McBride acknowledged the ongoing challenge but stressed that the vaccine rollout remained critical to controlling the virus in the long term.

As tensions rise between the UK government and the Northern Ireland Executive over Brexit-related issues, some fear that political distractions could further complicate efforts to manage the pandemic. However, Dr McBride maintained that the focus must remain on public health and safety, urging all citizens to support the health services and adhere to the necessary measures.

“Every action you take now can make a difference in protecting your loved ones and our communities,” he concluded. “We are all in this together, and working collectively, we can avoid a second lockdown.”
headline: Prepare for potential second lockdown, medical chief tells Northern Ireland

text:
The distinguished Northern Irish poet, Michael Longley, was laid to rest in the picturesque grounds of St Michael’s Church of Ireland on Friday, following a funeral that saw a gathering of poets, critics, and admirers come together to celebrate his life and work.

Longley, a towering figure in contemporary poetry, passed away last month at the age of 84. His funeral, a sombre yet beautifully poignant event, was presided over by the Very Reverend Dr John Smith, Rector of Holy Trinity Cathedral, Belfast. The service was attended by a who's who of Irish and British literary figures, including the esteemed poet Seamus Heaney, who delivered the eulogy.

Heaney spoke of Longley's profound influence on generations of poets and his commitment to the craft. "Michael Longley's poetry," Heaney stated, "was not just a collection of words on paper; it was a journey through the soul, a reflection of the human condition."

Longley's body of work spanned over six decades and included numerous collections such as "Collected Poems" and "New Collected Poems," which were widely acclaimed both in the UK and internationally. His poetry often delved into themes of nature, politics, and human experience, resonating deeply with readers and critics alike.

The funeral procession was led by the Garda Síochána, and as it made its way to the burial site, the air was filled with the gentle breeze carrying the scent of wildflowers, a nod to the natural world that so inspired Longley throughout his career.

In his address, the Taoiseach Micheál Martin expressed deep sadness at the loss of a great Irish poet, saying, "Michael Longley's poetry will continue to inspire and move us long after he is gone." Martin also highlighted the contribution Longley made to cross-border relations, noting how his work bridged divides and brought people from different backgrounds closer together.

Following the service, friends and family gathered for a private committal ceremony at St Michael's Church. The HSE provided comprehensive support to ensure the safety and comfort of all attendees, with meticulous health protocols in place given the ongoing pandemic.

As the coffin was lowered into the earth, the familiar strains of the lament "Aye, My Son, Farewell" echoed around the graveyard, a fitting tribute to a man whose words had brought solace to many during their lifetimes. With that, the funeral concluded, leaving behind an enduring legacy that will be remembered for years to come.
headline: Poet Michael Longley touched souls with just a few words, funeral hears

The EU leaders convened in Brussels on Friday evening for a summit focused on pressing matters including Brexit negotiations, with Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin and Tánaiste Leo Varadkar making key presentations on Ireland’s priorities.

Among the main topics discussed was the ongoing Brexit process, where the Irish government reiterated its commitment to ensuring there would be no hard border between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland. The Taoiseach highlighted the need for a comprehensive and inclusive agreement that respects the rights of citizens on both sides of the border and upholds the principles of the Good Friday Agreement.

The Good Friday Agreement, a cornerstone of peace in Northern Ireland, was also given prominence, with the Irish government reaffirming its support for its full implementation. The Tánaiste stated that continued cooperation with the British government and other stakeholders is crucial to ensure that the spirit and letter of the agreement remain intact. He further called for a united front among European partners to address the challenges posed by Brexit.

A light-hearted note punctuated the otherwise serious discussions at the summit when reports emerged of a mix-up involving a rodent at a Dublin zoo. The incident involved a confused member of staff who mistakenly let out a squirrel into the public areas of the zoo, leading to a momentary chaos before the situation was resolved swiftly by the Gardaí and zoo staff. The event was briefly covered during the evening news, providing a brief respite from the more substantial political deliberations taking place at the summit.

Throughout the evening, the summit proceedings underscored the complexities of modern international relations and the enduring importance of peace and cooperation. As the meeting drew to a close, both Irish leaders stressed the need to maintain dialogue and collaboration both within Europe and globally to address the diverse challenges facing the continent.
headline: Friday's Evening Round-Up: EU summit, Good Friday Agreement and mistaken identity of rodent

text:
Irish healthcare is facing a multitude of challenges, and among them is the need for a fundamental review of some staff within the Health Service Executive (HSE). While the HSE serves an invaluable role in providing medical care to millions across Ireland, it is clear that there are individuals who are not up to the task. These individuals undermine the quality of patient care and the broader mission of the organisation.

It is not uncommon for any large organisation to have some employees who do not perform at the required standard. However, in the context of the HSE, this issue can be particularly pressing. Healthcare professionals bear a significant responsibility, and their competence directly impacts patients' lives and health outcomes. Therefore, ensuring that every employee meets the necessary standards is imperative.

The recent controversy surrounding HSE staff who are alleged to be unfit for purpose highlights several issues that need urgent attention. These include poor patient care, bureaucratic inefficiencies, and a lack of accountability. For instance, reports have emerged of healthcare workers who are repeatedly accused of misconduct but continue to work without facing meaningful consequences. Such situations not only damage public trust in the healthcare system but also place undue stress on other dedicated staff members who strive to uphold high standards.

Addressing this problem requires a multi-faceted approach. Firstly, the HSE must establish clearer and more stringent guidelines for evaluating the performance of its workforce. This should involve regular assessments, transparent disciplinary procedures, and a commitment to continuous improvement. Secondly, there needs to be enhanced training and support programmes for all employees to ensure they are equipped with the skills and knowledge necessary to provide optimal care. Thirdly, there should be a stronger culture of accountability within the organisation, where poor performance is addressed swiftly and appropriately.

Furthermore, the Irish Government must play a critical role in supporting these efforts. Adequate funding and resources are essential to ensure that the HSE has the tools it needs to identify and address underperformance. The Government should also consider introducing measures to improve oversight and accountability, such as independent audits and regular reports on the performance of the HSE.

In conclusion, while it is important to recognise the excellent work carried out by many HSE staff members, it is equally crucial to address the issue of underperforming individuals. By implementing robust measures to evaluate and improve staff performance, the HSE can work towards delivering high-quality healthcare services to all Irish citizens. This is not just about improving efficiency; it is about ensuring that everyone who enters a hospital or medical facility receives the best possible care.
headline: Letters to the Editor: Some HSE workers are not fit for purpose

text:
The call for enhanced enforcement of the car ban on Patrick Street in Cork City has grown louder following reports of persistent violations. Residents and local business owners have expressed frustration over the ongoing contraventions, which they believe undermine the effectiveness of a scheme introduced to improve the street's character and encourage foot traffic.

The ban, implemented last year, prohibits vehicles from parking on Patrick Street outside specific times, with the aim of creating a more pedestrian-friendly environment. However, recent weeks have seen a number of instances where vehicles have parked in designated no-parking zones, despite clear signage and local awareness campaigns.

Cormac O’Connor, a local business owner, said, "It’s a shame because the street looks so much better without cars. People have to park a few streets away now, and it just doesn’t make sense when people still ignore the rules."

A spokesperson for the city council stated that they were aware of the issues and had increased patrols during peak hours. However, they acknowledged that the challenge was significant and would require a multifaceted approach. "We are looking at ways to further increase enforcement, possibly through additional parking attendants and enhanced CCTV surveillance," the spokesperson added.

Local politicians have also weighed in, with Councillor Eilis Ryan urging the city council to take stronger action. She stated, "If we want to see real change and improvements, we need to back up our policies with robust enforcement measures. The people who live and work here deserve a cleaner, safer, and more welcoming environment."

Meanwhile, community groups are exploring alternative solutions to the parking problem. They propose engaging with local businesses to offer incentives for customers who choose to park and walk. One proposal is to set up a loyalty card scheme where patrons can earn discounts for visiting multiple shops over a period of time.

"The key is to incentivise compliance rather than solely relying on fines," suggested Sarah Doyle, chairperson of the local community group. "We could create a positive feedback loop where regular shoppers get rewarded for supporting local businesses."

The city council will hold a public consultation next month to discuss these and other proposals. The aim is to find a balanced approach that supports both the goals of the car ban and the needs of residents and businesses.

As the debate continues, Patrick Street remains a focal point for discussions about urban planning and the challenges of balancing different community needs in a popular retail and tourist destination.
headline: Calls for more enforcement of Cork's Patrick St car ban

text:
The Minister for Education and Skills, Mr Simon Harris TD, has announced the launch of a significant initiative aimed at improving literacy among primary school children. The €1 million fund will be dedicated to providing free books to primary schools throughout Ireland.

In a statement released today, Mr Harris highlighted the importance of early literacy development in shaping future academic success. "This investment in our youngest learners is about much more than just acquiring books," he said. "It's about creating a culture of reading, where every child can develop a love for literature from a young age."

Under the new scheme, participating schools will have access to a wide range of titles suitable for each stage of primary education. The funding will cover the cost of procuring age-appropriate texts, from fiction to non-fiction, which will be made available in both digital and printed formats.

The Minister explained that the initiative also includes support for teachers and parents on how to integrate these resources into the classroom and home environment effectively. "We want to ensure that not only do children have access to the books but that they also have the tools and guidance to make the most of them," he added.

This development comes as part of the government's broader strategy to enhance educational outcomes across the country. In recent years, there has been a growing recognition of the benefits of early intervention in literacy, with many studies showing that children who start school with strong reading skills tend to perform better academically throughout their education.

The Minister noted that the allocation of funds would begin immediately, with applications being invited from interested schools. "We are eager to see this programme take off and hope that it will have a positive impact on our children's learning journey," Mr Harris stated.

Reaction to the news was largely positive. Sarah Doyle, a teacher at Rathmines Primary School, said, "This is fantastic news for our students. It will provide us with valuable resources to enrich our curriculum and help foster a genuine love of reading among our pupils."

The announcement has also been welcomed by various education organisations, including Comhaltas Cilt na hÉireann and the Reading Association of Ireland, who have praised the government's focus on supporting literacy development in Irish primary schools.

As the implementation of the scheme begins, all eyes will be on its effectiveness and the long-term impact it may have on the literacy rates of children across Ireland.
headline: Education Minister announces €1m fund for free books in primary schools

text:
Bord na nOíochtaí and the ever-evolving challenges faced by modern parents are once again at the forefront of discussion. Joanna Fortune, a mother of two from Dublin, finds herself grappling with a common yet perplexing issue – her baby, now aged six months, is developing a fondness for pulling the hair of those around her.

"It's a bit worrying," Fortune shares during an interview. "She seems to really enjoy it. I've tried everything – redirection, gentle scolding, even a few toys designed to distract. But nothing seems to work."

Fortune is not alone in her predicament. Many parents have found themselves on the receiving end of their baby's fascination with pulling hair. According to Dr. Ciarán Ó Murchú, a paediatrician based in Co. Galway, this behaviour can stem from a variety of reasons. "At such a young age, infants are still developing their understanding of cause and effect and social boundaries," he explains. "Pulling hair could be a way for them to explore their environment and engage with others."

Ó Murchú advises parents to remain patient and consistent in their approach. "It's important to maintain a calm and non-confrontational stance. When she pulls the hair, gently hold her hands, look her in the eye, and say 'no, we don't pull hair.' Over time, she'll learn what is acceptable."

But it's not just about what's acceptable; there are also the practical considerations. "We've had to rethink how we arrange play dates," Fortune admits. "Now, instead of having everyone gather round, we sit the kids down in separate areas. It's not ideal, but it works for now."

Parenting expert and child psychologist Dr. Aoife Ní Chathasaigh echoes this sentiment, suggesting that altering play environments can help mitigate such issues. "Creating space and boundaries between children can reduce the likelihood of these kinds of interactions. Encouraging activities that promote cooperation and respect can also go a long way."

Fortune adds, "It's tough seeing your little one do something that might hurt another child. It feels like a learning phase for her, but also for us as parents." She continues, "I'm trying to balance teaching her the right way to interact while ensuring everyone's safety."

In conclusion, while it's a challenging phase for both mother and baby, Dr. Ó Murchú remains optimistic. "This is part of normal development and social learning. With patience and consistency, parents can guide their children towards more positive behaviours."

For parents navigating this journey, perhaps the best advice comes from Fortune herself: "Stay calm, be consistent, and remember, they grow out of it!"
headline: Joanna Fortune: My baby keeps pulling other people's hair

There is growing concern among public health officials about a trend where some individuals are refusing to answer calls from contact tracers, which is impeding efforts to control the spread of the coronavirus in Ireland.

The Health Service Executive (HSE) has reported a significant number of calls going unanswered, particularly during evenings and weekends when the volume of calls peaks. This development is concerning as it hinders the ability of the dedicated contact tracing team to identify and isolate potential cases promptly, thereby increasing the risk of further transmission.

Dr. Tony Holohan, Chief Medical Officer at the Department of Health, said, “The effectiveness of our contact tracing system is crucial in preventing the virus from spreading. We have a highly trained and experienced team of contact tracers working tirelessly, but their efforts are being hampered by people not answering their calls. This is frustrating and potentially dangerous.”

According to a spokesperson for the HSE’s National Public Health Emergency Team (NPHET), the situation has been exacerbated by increased community transmission and the easing of certain restrictions. “Our contact tracers need to reach as many people as possible to break chains of transmission. However, if we cannot get through to potential contacts, we cannot effectively manage outbreaks,” they added.

To combat this issue, the HSE is reminding the public of the importance of answering calls from contact tracers. A spokesman stated, “The call you receive may be vital to stopping the virus from spreading. When you see the call from 0761 0761 076, please answer it without hesitation. Your co-operation is key to our efforts to keep everyone safe.”

The Department of Health has also issued guidelines advising people to remain patient and respond to these calls, which can take up to several hours. They emphasise that the information collected is strictly confidential and used solely for public health purposes.

In response to this trend, the HSE is looking into ways to improve communication strategies, including exploring alternative methods of contact such as text messages and digital platforms, to ensure that all potential contacts can be reached efficiently.

Public health experts stress that while there might be legitimate concerns, it is essential to cooperate with contact tracers. “It is important to understand that the calls made are made for your protection and the protection of others,” Dr. Holohan concluded. “Please do your part and assist in breaking the chain of infection.”
headline: Covid-19: 'Concerning' trend of some people not answering calls from contact tracers

In a recent interview with The Irish Examiner, Dr Ciara Kenny, the self-styled "Skin Nerd" and renowned dermatologist, has challenged the skincare advice given by many high-profile figures in entertainment and media. According to Dr Kenny, who runs a successful private practice and is well-known for her expertise in skincare, celebrities often provide unsolicited advice, which can sometimes be misleading or harmful.

"I’ve seen countless instances where well-meaning stars have shared tips on their skincare routines," Dr Kenny explained during a phone conversation. "While these insights can be entertaining, they’re not always scientifically accurate or tailored to individual skin types."

One of the most common pieces of advice from celebrities that Dr Kenny addresses is the frequent use of harsh exfoliants. "Many celebrities advocate for daily use of strong chemical peels, which can be too intense for most people’s skin," she said, adding that such practices can strip away the natural oils necessary for skin health and leave it vulnerable to irritation.

Another popular trend that Dr Kenny critiques is the push for overnight results. "Celebrities often promote products that claim to transform your skin almost immediately, but this isn’t sustainable or realistic," she noted. Dr Kenny encourages patients to take a more gradual approach, recommending regular use of products over several weeks to see improvements.

Dr Kenny also highlighted the importance of understanding one’s own skin type and needs. "Everyone’s skin is unique, and what works for one person may not work for another," she stressed. Her advice to the public is to be discerning when following celebrity skincare tips and to consult with a professional for tailored advice.

The Dermatologist’s new book, "The Truth About Your Skin," has been well-received, offering readers a deeper understanding of skincare science and debunking myths perpetuated by the media. "I want to empower people to make informed decisions about their skin care," said Dr Kenny, adding, "Education is key."

Dr Kenny’s views resonate with growing concerns among medical professionals about the impact of misinformation in the beauty industry. The HSE, Ireland’s Health Service Executive, also echoes this sentiment, advising the public to seek advice from qualified professionals before embarking on any new skincare routine.

As debates continue around the role of celebrities in skincare advice, Dr Ciara Kenny remains committed to educating the public and promoting healthy skincare practices. "The skincare journey is a lifelong process," she concludes, "and it’s important to prioritise evidence-based information."
headline: The Skin Nerd: Coming clean- celebrities don’t always know best

Kathleen MacMahon has always been drawn to the unspoken, the overlooked, and the forgotten corners of human experience. Her latest novel, *Whispers in the Mist*, is a poignant reminder of the power of storytelling to bridge gaps between generations and to uncover the hidden stories of the past.

The daughter of a long-serving Irish journalist, MacMahon often found herself stepping into a role that felt both familiar and foreign. “Journalism was a part of my life from a young age,” she explains. “It was my father’s passion, but I never felt it was something I could inherit. Instead, it was the quiet moments with him, sitting in his office, listening to stories that shaped me.”

*Whispers in the Mist* delves deep into the lives of two generations of women – one living in Ireland during the 1950s and another in contemporary times. The novel explores the complex mother-daughter relationship through the lens of their shared experiences and the legacies they leave behind. It is a story of strength, resilience, and the unexpected ways in which we find our voices.

MacMahon’s journey into fiction came after a career in digital media, where she honed skills that allowed her to craft narratives in a fast-paced environment. “Writing a novel is a very different beast,” she says. “It’s about slowing down and letting the words breathe. There’s a kind of freedom in that, especially when you’re exploring themes so deeply personal.”

Her experiences in journalism have been instrumental in shaping her approach to storytelling. “I’ve always been fascinated by the way people tell their stories,” she continues. “Sometimes, the most powerful stories are the ones that are whispered rather than shouted. That’s what I aim to capture in my writing.”

For those who have followed her work over the years, *Whispers in the Mist* will come as a welcome return to form. MacMahon’s prose is both lyrical and evocative, painting vivid pictures of a world that is both recognisable and timeless. It is a book that invites readers to reflect on their own histories and the stories that have shaped them.

In an interview with the Irish Examiner, MacMahon spoke about the importance of the mother/daughter relationship in her work. “It’s about more than just the blood connection,” she said. “It’s about how we learn to navigate the world, to find our place, and to carry forward the lessons of the past into the future.”

*Whispers in the Mist* is not just a novel; it is a meditation on the bonds that bind us and the secrets that can only be revealed through the passage of time. For Kathleen MacMahon, it represents a homecoming of sorts, a celebration of the rich tapestry of stories that make up her heritage and her own unique voice as a writer.
headline: Kathleen MacMahon on missing journalism, the mother/daughter relationship and her latest novel

Beef price protests are intensifying in several rural areas of Ireland, despite a recent agreement aimed at easing tensions over the legal actions against farmers. The disagreement stems from a perceived lack of follow-through on promises made during negotiations, which were intended to address concerns over the ongoing legal threats.

According to sources within the agricultural community, farmers in counties such as Kerry, Galway, and Carlow have reported increased levels of activism. This includes the setting up of pickets and roadblocks at farm entrances, causing significant disruption to daily operations and local supply chains.

One farmer from County Kerry commented, "We were promised that the legal threats would be dropped, but our lawyers continue to receive letters from solicitors threatening further action if we don't meet certain conditions. It feels like a bait and switch."

The Irish Farmers' Association (IFA) has called for immediate clarification and enforcement of the agreement. "Farmers are feeling betrayed by the lack of progress and the continuing legal threats," said IFA President Joe Healy. "We need to see tangible results rather than empty promises."

Meanwhile, the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine has issued a statement acknowledging the concerns but maintaining that the legal mechanisms are still in place and will not be removed until all agreed-upon conditions are met. "We are committed to resolving these issues amicably and are working closely with farmers to ensure they are fully aware of their rights and responsibilities," a spokesperson added.

Despite the continued unrest, some positive steps have been taken. In the District Court in Galway, a temporary injunction was granted last week to allow farmers to sell their livestock without fear of legal repercussions pending further negotiations. However, this has not yet alleviated the frustration among many farmers who continue to block roads and disrupt trade.

The HSE, which is monitoring the situation, has advised farmers to contact the Gardaí should their activities become violent or threaten public safety. "We are encouraging peaceful resolution and dialogue between all parties involved," stated a spokesperson for the HSE.

As the dispute continues, both the farming community and the government face mounting pressure to find a swift and lasting solution. The upcoming meeting of the Interdepartmental Committee on Agriculture will be crucial in determining the next steps in the negotiations.

In the meantime, the farming community remains vigilant, with many expressing concerns about the potential long-term impact on the industry and the wider economy. "This is not just about price; it's about the future of our farms and our way of life," another farmer from County Carlow remarked.

The Irish Examiner will continue to monitor the situation and bring you updates as the dispute unfolds.
headline: Beef price protests escalate in some areas despite agreement to remove legal threat

A Cork-based author who specialised in mental health issues found herself in a harrowing ordeal when she was blackmailed online, with her attackers threatening to release intimate pictures if she did not comply with their demands. The incident has sparked debate about victim-blaming and the broader issue of online harassment.

The author, whose identity has been withheld for her protection, told the Irish Examiner that she first became aware of the blackmail in January. According to her, a series of explicit photos and messages were sent to her, along with threats to expose them if she did not provide financial compensation.

"I was absolutely devastated," she said. "I had to travel to Dublin to meet the person responsible for the blackmail, and even then, I was met with more intimidation and demands."

Gardaí (Irish police) were notified but, according to the author, they failed to follow up adequately. "They questioned me for an hour and then told me there wasn't enough evidence to press charges," she recounted.

The author, who has previously written books on mental health and wellness, expressed frustration with what she described as a callous approach from the authorities. "It feels like my dignity and privacy were completely trampled on, and the response from the Gardaí only added to that feeling."

The situation took a further toll when a friend and colleague, unaware of the blackmail, posted comments on social media expressing disappointment in the author's handling of the situation. "My friend's post led to a barrage of victim-blaming comments, which were truly hurtful and damaging," the author said. "I realised then just how much work still needs to be done to shift attitudes towards victims of such crimes."

She emphasised the need for greater awareness and support mechanisms for those targeted by online harassment. "We must do better as a society to understand the psychological impact of these kinds of attacks and to provide appropriate support to survivors."

The case highlights the ongoing challenge of dealing with cybercrimes, particularly those targeting individuals through personal or sensitive information. Mental health advocates have called for increased resources and training for law enforcement in handling such cases effectively and sensitively.

The Department of Justice and Equality stated in a statement: "We acknowledge the seriousness of cybercrimes and the department is working closely with various stakeholders to strengthen legislation and support services for victims of such attacks."

As the author continues to navigate the aftermath of the blackmail, she remains committed to using her platform to raise awareness about online harassment and the importance of supporting those who fall victim to it.
headline: Cork mental health author blackmailed online 'disappointed by victim-blaming'

When my aunt received her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year, I couldn’t help but feel a wave of shock and concern wash over me. However, as the days turned into weeks, something unexpected began to unfold—a journey that would not only help my aunt but also reveal vital information about my own health.

It all started when my aunt, a vibrant 53-year-old mother, experienced a persistent pain in her chest. After several doctor’s visits and extensive testing, the diagnosis was confirmed: invasive ductal carcinoma. My aunt’s oncologist, Dr. Fionnuala O’Shea from the National Breast Cancer Centre, explained the options and the importance of early detection. It was then that I realised the significance of the screening process and the value it held not just for my aunt but for me too.

My aunt’s diagnosis came at a time when I had been postponing my own mammogram due to perceived busy schedules and other commitments. The experience of seeing her undergo chemotherapy and radiation therapy, while simultaneously dealing with the emotional toll, served as a powerful reminder of the importance of proactive healthcare. In her situation, the timely detection of cancer through regular screenings played a crucial role in managing her condition effectively.

The medical advice from Dr. O’Shea echoed what countless other healthcare professionals have highlighted—the importance of regular check-ups and self-awareness when it comes to one’s health. For my aunt, the diagnosis did more than just highlight the gravity of breast cancer; it underscored the critical role that preventive measures play in managing and potentially eliminating such illnesses.

As I followed my aunt’s treatment journey, I was struck by the resilience and strength she displayed, which inspired me to finally book my mammogram appointment. To my relief, the results were clear: no signs of cancer. However, the experience provided me with a newfound appreciation for the healthcare system and the importance of staying vigilant.

The support from the healthcare team at the clinic, including the radiographers and the administrative staff, was overwhelmingly positive. Their patience and professionalism made what could have been a stressful experience feel reassuringly handled. This level of care and attention is what makes our healthcare system so vital.

In the end, my aunt’s breast cancer diagnosis not only brought her and our family closer together during a challenging period but also taught us all the value of regular health checks and open communication about our wellbeing. It has been a humbling and eye-opening experience, one that I hope will motivate others to prioritise their health and take preventative measures seriously.

For me, it was a wake-up call to embrace a healthier lifestyle, understand the importance of early detection, and be a proponent of proactive healthcare practices. My aunt’s story is a testament to the power of early detection and the support available within our healthcare network. It serves as a reminder that even when faced with a difficult diagnosis, there is always hope and support to navigate the path ahead.
headline: My aunt's breast cancer diagnosis saved me

For the sake of Ireland’s children, let’s march in solidarity with their carers

In the heart of our nation, we often speak about our children as the future, and rightly so. Their laughter, their curiosity, their potential to shape a brighter tomorrow is what many of us hold dear. However, it would be remiss of me not to mention those who make all this possible—their parents, guardians, and carers. Today, I urge us all to unite and stand in solidarity with these dedicated individuals.

As we prepare to mark Children's Rights Day on 20 November, the theme of this year’s commemoration—“Together for Every Child” —resonates deeply. It calls upon us to recognise the significant role that carers play in ensuring the well-being of our children. These unsung heroes often work tirelessly, juggling demanding responsibilities, sometimes at the expense of their own health and wellbeing.

Recent research from the HSE indicates a worrying trend. Carers are frequently dealing with their own mental health issues, facing financial pressures, and shouldering the burden of caring responsibilities without adequate support. This is a stark reminder that unless we address these challenges collectively, our children will continue to face barriers in achieving their full potential.

It is time to take meaningful action. The Government must prioritise the development of comprehensive supports for carers. This includes access to respite care, financial assistance, and mental health services. Initiatives such as these not only alleviate the daily stresses but also empower carers to continue providing the vital support their charges need.

Moreover, societal attitudes towards carers need to shift. We must challenge the stigma and acknowledge the valuable contribution they make to our communities. Let us ensure that carers are celebrated and recognised for their efforts. A simple act of kindness or an offer of help can go a long way in making a significant difference in their lives.

This Children’s Rights Day, let us march together in solidarity. Whether it’s attending a local rally, signing a petition, or simply lending an ear, each of us has a part to play. The collective voice of the people can drive change and demand that carers are accorded the respect and support they deserve.

Ireland prides itself on being a society that values its children. It is now incumbent upon us to ensure that we do not leave the carers behind. Our children deserve nothing less than a supportive and nurturing environment, and that starts with recognising and honouring the tireless work of those who care for them.

So, let us march, write letters, and call for change. For the sake of Ireland’s children, let’s stand together and make a positive difference today.

If you’ve ever looked in the mirror with your hand held up against your face and wondered why your complexion looks less than perfect, fear not. Flawless skin can be within your reach, especially when you choose the right foundation. The key to achieving a flawless finish lies in understanding your skin type and choosing the foundation that will work best for you.

From matte to dewy, there’s a foundation out there for every skin type and occasion. For those with dry skin, opt for a hydrating formula that will keep your skin nourished throughout the day. For combination or oily skin types, a lightweight, oil-control foundation will do the trick. If you have sensitive skin, it's essential to choose a foundation that is fragrance-free and hypoallergenic to prevent irritation.

Choosing the correct shade is equally crucial. A foundation that is too light or too dark can make your skin look off or even age you. Visit a makeup counter and let a beauty expert help you find the most accurate match. You can also use online tools to help you find your perfect shade, but remember, the best way to determine your shade is in natural light.

Once you have the foundation, application techniques can really elevate your look. Using a brush or a stippling sponge can give you a more natural, buildable finish. For a flawless finish, apply your foundation in thin layers, starting from the centre of your face and blending outward. This will ensure a smooth, seamless application.

For that extra touch of perfection, setting your makeup is a must. Powder or a setting spray will help lock your foundation into place and give you that coveted, long-lasting finish. A dusting of translucent powder over your cheeks, nose, and chin can also help reduce the appearance of any excess shine.

With the right foundation and a few simple tips, you can achieve a flawless skin look that will complement your features beautifully. Whether you’re heading to the office, heading out for the evening, or just want to feel great at home, the right foundation can transform your complexion and boost your confidence. So, pick the perfect foundation, follow the steps, and step confidently into your day.
headline: Get The Look: flawless skin is possible with a little help from these foundations

While Leo Varadkar came in second place with 17%, followed closely by Micheál Martin of Fine Gael at 16%, the survey showed a decline in popularity among traditional leaders such as Enda Kenny and Simon Coveney.

Mary Lou McDonald's rise in popularity is attributed to her handling of various social issues and her stance on climate change. In recent years, she has been at the forefront of debates surrounding housing affordability, public services, and the fight against climate change. Her advocacy for green policies and social justice initiatives has resonated strongly with younger voters and those who feel marginalized.

"The success of Mary Lou McDonald in garnering such high levels of public approval is not surprising given her commitment to addressing the pressing issues facing society," said Áine White, Director of Ipsos MRBI. "However, it will be crucial for her to maintain this level of support and translate it into tangible improvements on the ground."

Analysts point to the ongoing economic challenges and the need for effective governance as factors contributing to the shift in public sentiment towards Mary Lou McDonald. As the country continues to grapple with the aftermath of the pandemic and the economic fallout, there is an increased desire for leaders who can navigate these complexities while delivering real change.

In response to the poll, a spokesperson for Sinn Féin stated, "These results are a testament to the hard work and dedication of our party to serve the people of Ireland. We remain committed to building a better future for all, and we will continue to work tirelessly to address the pressing issues facing our country."

As Ireland enters a period of crucial political decisions, the high levels of public support for Mary Lou McDonald could signal a significant shift in the balance of power within the political landscape. Her leadership will undoubtedly play a pivotal role in shaping the direction of Irish politics for the coming years.
headline: Mary Lou McDonald 'more popular leader than Leo Varadkar'

text:
Migrants have a greater propensity towards employment compared to their native counterparts, according to a comprehensive study conducted by the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI). However, despite this increased likelihood of participation in the workforce, migrants experience higher levels of poverty.

The research, published yesterday, highlights that while 78% of migrants are employed, this figure is only 65% among natives. This disparity underscores a significant trend in Irish society, with migrants often filling jobs that may be considered more precarious or temporary.

One of the key findings of the study indicates that despite working more frequently than natives, migrants are significantly more likely to fall into poverty. The report notes that 16% of migrants live in households classified as being below the poverty line, compared to just 8% of natives.

Dr. Grainne McCarthy, lead author of the study, stated, "Our findings suggest that while migration brings significant economic benefits in terms of labour supply and diversity, there are also challenges that need to be addressed in relation to poverty and inequality."

The ESRI's analysis points to several factors contributing to this higher incidence of poverty among migrants. These include lower wages, less access to social welfare supports, and often facing language barriers which can hinder career progression.

The Government has been urged to develop targeted policies to address these issues, particularly focusing on integration and support services for migrants. Minister for Justice and Equality Charlie Flanagan said, "This study highlights areas where our approach needs to evolve to ensure that all workers, regardless of their background, can enjoy decent living standards."

The research also recommends increased investment in language training programmes, affordable housing initiatives, and improved access to social protection mechanisms for newcomers.

As Ireland continues to navigate the complexities of managing a diverse and growing population, policymakers will have to balance the economic contributions of migrants with the social challenges they present. The ESRI’s findings offer a roadmap for targeted interventions aimed at improving the economic circumstances of migrants and reducing disparities in poverty levels.

The full report from the ESRI can be accessed through its website, providing detailed insights and policy recommendations for stakeholders across government and civil society.
headline: Migrants more likely to work but face higher poverty rates, ESRI study finds

text:
Elon Musk's pioneering neuroscience firm, Neuralink, has been placed under scrutiny by US authorities following allegations of 'unsafe' shipping practices that could have compromised patient safety. The investigation, initiated by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), comes after reports emerged detailing how Neuralink's shipping protocols were deemed inadequate, potentially putting individuals enrolled in clinical trials at risk.

Neuralink, which is developing implantable brain-computer interfaces to treat neurological conditions such as epilepsy and paralysis, has already drawn attention for its ambitious plans and controversial procedures. However, the latest revelations suggest that even the transportation of these sensitive devices was not without significant lapses.

According to sources close to the investigation, FDA officials have been examining shipping records and communication logs from Neuralink. These documents allegedly reveal instances where devices were shipped in suboptimal conditions, raising concerns about the potential damage to the equipment during transit. The FDA's probe aims to establish whether these breaches could have affected the outcomes of clinical trials involving patients with the implants.

A spokesperson for Neuralink declined to comment on the investigation but stated that the company adheres to strict guidelines for the handling and transportation of their products. "We take the safety and security of our devices very seriously," the spokesperson said. "We are cooperating fully with the FDA's inquiry."

The FDA's concern extends beyond just the integrity of the devices themselves. There is also fear that improper shipping could lead to contamination or other issues that might endanger patient health. The agency has scheduled a series of meetings with Neuralink representatives to discuss these matters further and to outline a plan for improving shipping and handling procedures.

In response to the ongoing investigation, Senator Mark Kelly, a vocal critic of some aspects of Neuralink's operations, welcomed the FDA's action. "It is crucial that all companies involved in medical innovation maintain the highest standards of safety and accountability," he said. "Investigations like this ensure that patient welfare remains the top priority."

As the investigation progresses, there are growing calls for greater transparency and oversight within the burgeoning field of neurotechnology. Advocates argue that stringent regulatory frameworks must be in place to protect both patients and innovators as these technologies continue to advance.
headline: Elon Musk’s brain-implant company investigated over ‘unsafe’ shipping methods

text:
Cork city councillors have called for stringent traffic-calming measures and enhanced footpath connectivity to be mandatory in all future housing developments, stressing that these improvements are crucial for the safety and convenience of residents.

Speaking at a recent meeting of the city and county council, Councillor Niamh O'Malley highlighted the need for developers to prioritise walkability and accessibility in new housing estates. "We cannot afford to build communities that are not conducive to safe walking and cycling," she stated, pointing out that increased footpath width and better lighting were essential components.

The call came in the wake of several incidents involving pedestrians in various parts of the city. Councillor O'Malley cited the case of a young mother who was struck by a car while crossing a busy street near her new home, underscoring the urgent need for better infrastructure.

Supporting O'Malley's stance, the City Council’s transport committee has drafted new guidelines that would require new developments to meet specific standards for pedestrian pathways and crosswalks. These guidelines include wider footpaths, better visibility through improved signage, and the installation of speed bumps and other calming devices on arterial roads surrounding the new housing.

The committee's recommendations also stress the importance of connectivity between different residential areas and public spaces. "It's about creating a seamless journey from home to school, from work to leisure, all within a pedestrian-friendly environment," explained Councillor Michael Flynn.

Local architect Dermot Casey welcomed the move but stressed that developers often push back against such requirements due to increased costs. "While the short-term financial burden might be high, the long-term benefits for community health and safety are undeniable," he said.

The proposed changes have received backing from community groups and organisations dedicated to improving urban living conditions. The Irish Heart Foundation has hailed the initiative, stating that it is a vital step towards reducing accident rates and encouraging healthier lifestyles among residents.

However, some developers argue that the current planning regulations are already stringent enough, and that mandating additional measures could stifle innovation and creativity in housing design.

Despite this resistance, the council remains committed to pushing through the proposed changes. "Safety should always come first, and we have a responsibility to our citizens to ensure that they can move around their city without fear," said Mayor Catherine Connolly.

The debate over traffic-calming measures and footpath connectivity is set to continue as the council considers incorporating the new guidelines into its development plans. A public consultation period will be held to gather further input before any final decisions are made.
headline: Traffic-calming measures and footpath connectivity 'a must' for future Cork housing developments
