A postmistress based in rural County Limerick has expressed her delight at reports suggesting that the Government is set to provide an additional €12,000 in annual support for post offices across the country. The development comes as post offices continue to face challenges due to the rise of online shopping and digital communication methods.

The postmistress, speaking on condition of anonymity, stated that the subvention would be a welcome financial boost. "It's good to see the value placed on our community hubs," she said. "Post offices are not just about posting letters and parcels; they're essential services providing postal, banking, and even utility bill payments for many rural residents."

According to sources within the Post Office network, this support is part of a broader strategy aimed at sustaining community-based services in remote areas. The Department of Rural and Community Development and the Post Office are currently finalising the details of the scheme, with a view to rolling it out to all 1,900 post offices nationwide by the end of the year.

The postmistress highlighted the importance of these services, especially during the ongoing pandemic. "In these uncertain times, having a reliable local service where people can get their essential bills paid or even receive important documents from the likes of the HSE, is invaluable," she added.

The HSE, for its part, has welcomed the initiative, noting the critical role post offices play in facilitating access to healthcare services. "This support will undoubtedly enhance the ability of post offices to assist with important health and social welfare transactions," commented a spokesperson.

As negotiations continue, the postmistress remains hopeful about the future of her local post office. "This extra funding could mean the difference between being able to invest in new technology to better serve our community and possibly expanding our range of services," she concluded.

The Department of Rural and Community Development declined to comment on the details of the proposed subvention but confirmed that discussions were ongoing. A spokesperson stated, "We are committed to supporting local communities and ensuring that essential services remain accessible, particularly in rural areas."
headline: Postmistress welcomes reports of €12k State subvention

Cian's Kennels, a Dublin-based animal sanctuary, has become a beacon of hope for children who find solace in the company of their pets during times of illness. In a heartwarming review of the year, the centre has seen an increasing number of families making the journey to Cian's Kennels to reconnect with their furry friends, providing a much-needed respite from the challenges of long-term hospital stays.

Throughout 2022, the sanctuary received numerous requests from families across Ireland whose children were battling various illnesses. These visits provided a moment of normalcy in a world often fraught with uncertainty. "The children light up when they see their pets," said Aoife Murphy, the founder of Cian's Kennels. "It’s a joy to see them interact, play, and just simply be in each other’s company."

Among those whose lives were touched were the young members of the O’Connor family. Six-year-old Jack was diagnosed with cancer early last year and spent several months in hospital undergoing treatment. His visit to Cian's Kennels, where he was reunited with his dog Max, brought immense joy to both the boy and his parents. "Max is Jack's best friend," his mother explained. "Just being around him makes all the difference to Jack’s mood."

Similar stories have played out countless times at Cian's Kennels, with the centre becoming not just a sanctuary for animals but also a place of healing for the children. The organisation has expanded its reach, working closely with healthcare providers such as the HSE and local hospitals to facilitate these visits. 

"The therapeutic benefits of interacting with animals are well-documented, and we’ve seen first-hand the positive impact on the mental health and overall wellbeing of these children," added Mr Murphy. "Our aim is to continue supporting families and ensuring that every child has the chance to experience the comfort and love of their pet."

In recognition of its vital work, Cian's Kennels received commendations and support from various Irish political figures and public figures throughout the year. The Taoiseach, in particular, praised the centre’s efforts, stating, "Cian's Kennels exemplifies the power of compassion and community. It is a shining example of how we can come together to make a difference in people's lives."

As the year draws to a close, it’s clear that Cian's Kennels will continue to be a cornerstone of support for families seeking solace and connection. With plans for further expansion and additional services, the sanctuary remains committed to its mission of bringing joy and healing through the special bond between humans and their pets.
headline: Cian's Kennels reunites sick children with their pets

text:
The Alliance for Good Service Ireland (AGSI) has raised serious concerns over its exclusion from negotiations surrounding a new pay deal for health workers, according to sources close to the organisation. The AGSI, which represents 15,000 healthcare professionals across Ireland, claims that they were not included in discussions that led to a proposed deal, which was finalised late last month.

In a statement, AGSI spokesperson Fiona McVeagh said, "We are deeply disappointed and frustrated by our exclusion from these crucial negotiations. We have consistently highlighted the importance of ensuring that all parties involved in the healthcare workforce are represented in such critical talks."

The Department of Health and the HSE, however, have defended their approach. A spokesperson for the Department stated, "Our primary focus is on ensuring the best possible outcomes for patients and the healthcare system as a whole. These negotiations involved multiple stakeholders, and we believe that the final agreement reflects the needs and concerns of those directly engaged."

The proposed deal includes significant wage increases for front-line staff, with nurses and other allied health professionals seeing an average rise of 4.8% over the next three years. However, the AGSI argues that these improvements should have been made in consultation with them and other union representatives.

"We have always advocated for fair and transparent processes," added McVeagh. "We believe that our representation should be included in discussions, especially given our significant role in delivering frontline healthcare services."

The AGSI has called for an immediate meeting with the Department of Health and the HSE to address their grievances. Meanwhile, it remains to be seen whether the matter will be escalated to the Ombudsman for Public Services or other regulatory bodies.

As the dispute continues, healthcare unions are expected to maintain their efforts to secure a comprehensive agreement that benefits all staff involved in the delivery of healthcare services in Ireland.
headline: AGSI alleges exclusion from pay deal negotiations

text:
Scientists have made a groundbreaking discovery, finding microplastics in the exhaled breath of dolphins for the first time. The findings, presented at a recent marine conservation conference in Dublin, highlight a concerning new dimension to the impact of plastic pollution on marine life.

Dr. Fiona McQuillan, a marine biologist from the National Institute for Water and Atmospheric Research (NIWA) in Ireland, led the study. She and her team collected samples from two bottlenose dolphins living in the Irish Sea. The dolphins were observed off the coast of County Cork, where they often feed and socialise.

Using advanced analytical techniques, the researchers detected microplastics in the dolphins' breath, indicating that these tiny plastic particles are not just ingested but also absorbed into their respiratory systems. This poses significant health risks, as the plastics can cause inflammation and may lead to long-term damage to organs.

"The presence of microplastics in dolphin breath suggests a more pervasive and insidious impact than previously thought," Dr. McQuillan said. "These animals are at the top of the food chain and serve as a crucial indicator of the health of our oceans."

The discovery comes as environmental groups and policymakers in Ireland are grappling with the challenge of reducing plastic pollution. The government has already implemented several measures, including a ban on single-use plastics in 2021 and increased funding for waste management infrastructure.

"Given the sensitive nature of the research, we need to further explore the full scope of the issue and its implications for marine ecosystems," commented Siobhán O'Sullivan, spokesperson for the Department of Environment, Climate and Communications. "This is a critical area of research that requires urgent attention."

Conservationists are calling for stricter regulations and public awareness campaigns to mitigate the spread of microplastics. "We cannot continue to ignore the fact that our oceans are choking on plastic," said Dr. Aoife Nic Mhaolchinn, a marine conservation expert. "Every effort must be made to protect our marine life and ensure a healthier future for our planet."

The researchers plan to conduct further studies to understand the extent of microplastic contamination in marine mammals and to develop strategies to reduce the intake of plastic particles through the food chain.
headline: Microplastics discovered in dolphin breath

The Irish Labour Party has condemned the decision by UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak to use video footage of the Bloody Sunday massacre during his election campaign, describing it as "disgusting" and exploiting a tragic event from Ireland’s past.

In a statement released on Friday, the Labour Party expressed deep regret at the UK Government’s use of the footage from the 1972 incident in Londonderry, where 14 civil rights marchers were shot dead by British paratroopers. The party said it was a violation of the dignity of those affected and the victims’ families.

"The decision by the UK Government to exploit a moment of such pain and sorrow for a political gain is deeply troubling," said Ciara Travers, spokesperson for the Labour Party. "This is not how we should be remembering the innocent lives lost and their families."

Travers highlighted that the footage's release has reignited painful memories for many in Northern Ireland and the wider Irish diaspora, and called on the UK Government to respect the sensitivities surrounding the issue.

"This is an Irish story, with profound resonance in the Republic of Ireland," she added. "It is essential that the UK Government shows a greater level of respect and understanding in its handling of such sensitive material."

The controversy has also drawn criticism from within Northern Ireland, with some local politicians and human rights groups urging the UK Government to withdraw the footage and acknowledge the distress it has caused.

The Irish Government and opposition parties have also condemned the move, with Foreign Affairs Minister Simon Coveney stating that it was "incredibly insensitive" and "unhelpful" for the peace process in Northern Ireland. 

"The footage should never be used to score political points," Coveney said in a statement. "The victims and their families deserve our respect and our solidarity, not further pain and division."

The Labour Party's stance comes as it prepares for elections in the Republic of Ireland next year, with opposition leaders using the incident to highlight potential differences with the ruling Fine Gael party on foreign policy and support for the British Union.

"This is not just about Bloody Sunday; it is about the principles and values that guide us in the treatment of our neighbours and allies," Travers concluded. "We will continue to hold the UK to account for its actions and seek to ensure that such incidents are remembered with the respect they deserve."
headline: Tories' use of Bloody Sunday footage 'disgusting'

Cork boy, Seán Ó Fátharta, 13, has found himself embarking on a fresh literary journey thanks to a recent donation of Roald Dahl books from the Roald Dahl Museum and Story Centre in Great Missenden, Buckinghamshire. The gift has rekindled his passion for reading and opened up a new world of imagination.

Seán, who attends Presentation Brothers College in Cork, was thrilled to receive the collection after his local community centre reached out to the museum about sharing some of their extensive Roald Dahl holdings with local children. "I've always loved Roald Dahl's stories," said Seán, "but I never had access to such a wide range of his books until now."

The donation includes a trove of hard-to-find titles, including early drafts, unpublished works, and rare editions. Seán's favourite so far has been 'Lolla-Roo and the Polka-Dot Chair', a pre-published manuscript that offers a fascinating insight into Dahl's creative process.

"The stories are so vivid and full of surprises," enthused Seán, "especially the way Dahl plays with language and storytelling techniques. It's like he’s creating a new world every time."

Teachers at Presentation Brothers College have also noticed a marked improvement in Seán's reading comprehension and engagement in class since the book donation. Mrs. Deirdre O'Sullivan, Head of English, commented, "Seán has become more expressive in discussions and his essays show a deeper understanding and appreciation of narrative structures. We're delighted to see him so inspired by these new additions to our library."

The Roald Dahl Museum and Story Centre's Director, Dr. Claire Williams, expressed pleasure at seeing her institution's collections reach eager young readers. "We are thrilled to share our unique collection with more children. Roald Dahl's books are not just stories; they are doorways to creativity and imagination, and it's wonderful to see them fostering a love of reading in young people like Seán."

Seán's journey through the worlds of Dahl continues, promising even more adventures and lessons in the power of literature. As he delves deeper into his new chapter, it is clear that Seán has embraced a new level of literary engagement and enthusiasm.
headline: Schoolboy enjoys new chapter reading Roald Dahl books

Student union leader and opposition spokesperson on education, Ciara Bacik, has strongly criticised the Government's budget proposals, describing them as "in disarray" due to a proposed increase in student fees.

Speaking at a press conference in Dublin today, Bacik highlighted that the increase, which is set to affect third-level education in the coming academic year, represents a significant shift from previous commitments made by the Government. She argued that the hike is not only a retrograde step but also undermines the Government’s broader aims of accessibility and social inclusion in higher education.

"The proposed fee hike is deeply concerning and runs counter to the principles of social justice and equality," said Bacik. "We had hoped that this budget would address some of the long-standing issues facing students, such as accommodation costs and support for those from disadvantaged backgrounds."

Bacik also pointed out that the timing of the announcement coincides with the start of the academic year, leaving students and institutions with little time to adapt to the changes. She called on the Minister for Further and Higher Education, Simon Harris, to reconsider the decision, stating that it risks further alienating students from engaging with government policies.

"We need a budget that works for all students, not just those who can afford the increasing costs," she added. "This is not a matter of political rhetoric; it is about the real lives of young people and their ability to pursue their dreams without being burdened by financial constraints."

The National Union of Students (NUS) Ireland echoed Bacik’s sentiments, warning that the proposed fee increase could lead to a significant drop in applications for certain courses, particularly among students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

Meanwhile, the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science stated that they are working closely with universities and colleges to address the implications of the proposed fee increase. They maintained that the measures are aimed at ensuring the sustainability of the higher education system while balancing the needs of both the state and students.

As discussions continue, opposition parties have indicated that they will be closely scrutinising the budget details in the coming days, with a particular focus on the impact on students and the broader education sector. The Labour Party’s spokesperson on higher education, Enda Kenny, called for a comprehensive review of the proposed changes before any final decisions are made.

The debate on student fees and their role in Irish society remains contentious, with stakeholders on all sides highlighting the complex challenges faced by the education system. While the Government argues that the fee increase is necessary to ensure the quality and sustainability of higher education, critics like Bacik contend that it could stifle access and drive up the cost of attending college for generations to come.
headline: Bacik: Student's budget plans in 'disarray' over fee hike

A man has been charged following a significant drugs seizure at Rosslare Europort, with the haul valued at approximately €6.5 million.

The incident unfolded on Friday when officers from An Garda Síochána intercepted a lorry at the port, which was inbound from the United Kingdom. During the search, a substantial quantity of cannabis was discovered hidden within the cargo. The drugs, estimated to be worth over €6.5 million upon importation into the Republic of Ireland, were seized by the authorities.

The 42-year-old man, who was travelling in the lorry, has now been formally charged in connection with the case. He appeared before the District Court yesterday, where he was remanded in custody pending a further hearing. 

Garda Inspector Sean Murphy stated, "This successful operation highlights the ongoing commitment of An Garda Síochána to combat the smuggling of illicit substances through our borders." He added that the force is appealing for information from the public regarding any suspicious activity that may have led to this significant seizure.

The case is currently under investigation by the Garda National Drugs Bureau, with the potential for further charges to be brought against those involved. The Gardaí are also working closely with their counterparts in other European Union member states to trace the source of the drugs and apprehend any individuals responsible for orchestrating the smuggling operation.

Meanwhile, the Health Service Executive (HSE) has reiterated its call for the public to remain vigilant and report any suspicious behaviour to the Gardaí. The HSE’s Director of Public Health, Dr. Fergal O’Rourke, commented, "We continue to see the devastating impact that the illegal drug trade can have on communities and families. Information from members of the public is crucial in helping us to disrupt these operations."

The incident has caused ripples across political circles, with TDs from all parties expressing their support for the Gardaí and calling for increased resources to combat cross-border smuggling activities.

As the case develops, it remains unclear whether the suspect is from the Republic of Ireland or another country. However, the significant value of the drugs seized has once again highlighted the ongoing challenges faced by law enforcement agencies in tackling the transnational nature of drug trafficking.
headline: Man charged over €6.5m drug seizure at Rosslare Europort

An PSNI officer has been hospitalised following a serious assault in County Tyrone on Wednesday evening. The incident occurred around 7:45pm when the officer, who was off duty and travelling home in Omagh, was attacked in the area of Carnavagh.

The victim, a member of the PSNI for several years, suffered multiple injuries as a result of the attack which led to his immediate hospitalisation. A spokesperson for the PSNI stated that the officer was in a stable condition but still required medical attention. The investigation into the incident is ongoing, with local Garda Síochána officers leading the probe.

Local residents expressed shock at the attack, with one resident stating, "It's shocking to think it happened so close to our community, especially to someone who has been protecting us." Calls have been made for greater vigilance and for the public to come forward with any information that could assist with the investigation.

The incident has caused concern among members of the community and has highlighted the vulnerability of law enforcement personnel even outside of duty hours. A spokesperson for the Department of Justice confirmed they were monitoring the situation closely and assured the public of their commitment to supporting the PSNI and investigating such incidents thoroughly.

The Northern Ireland Office has also commented, expressing solidarity with the victim and their family, while reiterating the government's stance against violence and its support for those who serve to uphold the law. The Taoiseach has instructed his office to liaise with their counterparts in Northern Ireland regarding the matter.

The attack has sparked discussions about security for off-duty officers and the need for increased protection measures in areas where attacks on law enforcement are becoming more frequent. As the investigation continues, authorities are appealing to anyone with information on the incident to contact the police.
headline: PSNI officer hospitalised after Tyrone assault

The Eurozone has agreed in principle to activate a mechanism allowing the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) to directly support struggling economies, a development that is expected to ease the financial burden on states such as Ireland grappling with economic challenges exacerbated by the ongoing coronavirus pandemic.

In a meeting held today, Eurozone finance ministers reached a consensus on modifying the ESM to allow it to provide direct lending to national treasuries, bypassing the existing bailout funds which have been used in the past. This change would be particularly significant for countries like Ireland, which continues to navigate through the lingering effects of the pandemic and has seen its economy struggle in recent months.

Finance Minister, Paschal Donohoe, welcomed the agreement, stating that it provided a much-needed tool in the ongoing efforts to stabilise the Irish economy. "This agreement is a positive step forward, especially as we continue to manage the economic fallout from the pandemic," he said, adding that the modification would provide greater flexibility and support to countries facing fiscal pressures.

The decision follows months of negotiations and comes amid rising concerns over public finances in several Eurozone countries. The Irish Government has been working closely with both the European Commission and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to secure additional funding and support, highlighting the importance of this agreement.

The Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, acknowledged the significance of the decision while cautioning that there was still work to be done. "While this is an important step, we must now focus on the practical implementation of these changes and ensure they deliver the necessary relief for our citizens and businesses," he stated.

In the coming weeks, the details of the agreement will be fleshed out, including the precise terms of the direct lending mechanism and how it will be monitored and managed. The HSE and other key state agencies will play a critical role in ensuring that any financial support reaches those who need it most, whether in the form of direct grants or investment in healthcare and other essential services.

The European Central Bank (ECB) will also need to issue guidelines on the operation of the new mechanism, a process that is expected to take several months. Despite the ongoing complexities, the Eurozone agreement represents a crucial development in the ongoing response to the pandemic, offering new tools to help member states recover and rebuild their economies.
headline: Eurozone 'agrees in principle' to use bailout mechanism

Temperatures soared to a staggering 28.6 degrees Celsius at Shannon Airport yesterday, breaking the previous May temperature record set just a week ago. The mercury climbed steadily throughout the day, reaching its peak well before the evening, marking what is being described as an unprecedented heatwave for the month of May.

Met Éireann, Ireland’s national weather service, issued a warning for the south and west of the country as the warm front moved across the region. The high temperatures, which were recorded on Monday afternoon, are expected to remain elevated through Tuesday, prompting public health advice to stay hydrated and seek shade during the hottest parts of the day.

"The recent heatwave is part of a broader trend of increasing temperatures, driven by climate change," stated Dr. Eamonn Meehan, Senior Forecaster with Met Éireann. He added that while records can be broken due to a combination of local factors, the overall trend towards higher temperatures is concerning and highlights the urgent need for action on climate mitigation.

The previous record for the month of May at Shannon was set just seven days prior, on Thursday, 19 May, when the temperature reached 27.4 degrees Celsius. The new record has raised concerns among environmental groups about the long-term impact of such extreme weather events.

Local authorities and health services have been closely monitoring the situation, with special attention given to vulnerable groups, including the elderly and those with pre-existing medical conditions. Public health experts have advised people to check on neighbours and friends who may be affected by the heat.

The unexpected warmth has also disrupted travel plans, with Aer Ríocht na hÉireann, Ireland’s state airport authority, noting an increase in delays and cancellations of flights due to the intense heat affecting runway conditions.

As the heat persists, officials continue to urge caution and highlight the importance of staying informed through local weather bulletins and health advisories. The record-breaking temperatures serve as a stark reminder of the challenges posed by climate change and the critical need for adaptation measures across all sectors of society.
headline: 28.6C reached at Shannon, breaking May temperature record

A significant breakthrough has been achieved in the conservation efforts for the curlew, a bird species that has been in decline across Europe and is particularly affected in Ireland. The National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS) and BirdWatch Ireland have partnered on a €300,000 initiative aimed at preserving the critically endangered wetland birds.

The curlew, known scientifically as Numenius arquata, faces numerous threats including habitat loss, predation, and climate change. The conservation programme, which commenced earlier this year, focuses on creating and enhancing suitable habitats within designated Special Protection Areas (SPAs) throughout the country.

According to Dr. Claire Keane, head of nature conservation with NPWS, the project has shown promising results. "We have identified key areas where curlews are most vulnerable and are working closely with landowners to implement measures such as reduced grazing intensity and controlled burning to maintain open habitats," she explained.

One of the success stories comes from the Midlands, where a small flock of curlews has been observed nesting successfully after habitat improvements were made. This is particularly encouraging given that the Midlands region is one of the last strongholds for the species in Ireland.

The initiative also involves public awareness campaigns and educational programmes aimed at raising awareness among the general public about the importance of these birds and their plight. According to Mark O'Connor, director of policy and research at BirdWatch Ireland, community engagement is crucial. "By involving local communities and farmers, we can create a network of stewards who will play a vital role in the long-term survival of the curlew."

The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine has provided additional funding to support the project, acknowledging the critical role of the curlew in the ecosystem. The Minister of State at the Department, Thomas Byrne, TD, commented on the importance of the conservation work, stating, "The curlew is not just a symbol of our rich natural heritage but a crucial indicator of the health of our environment. This project represents a collaborative effort between government, NGOs, and local communities, and I am encouraged by the progress we have seen so far."

As the project enters its second phase, there are plans to expand the scope to include more SPAs and to utilise innovative technologies like drones to monitor and protect the birds. The hope is that these combined efforts will reverse the decline and secure a brighter future for the curlew in Ireland.

This breakthrough in curlew conservation highlights the potential for successful partnerships and the dedication of organisations and individuals committed to protecting Ireland's wildlife. As the project continues, all eyes are on the curlew, hoping that its numbers will begin to recover and thrive once again.
headline: Curlew conservation scheme makes breakthrough

G20 leaders meeting in Venice this week have reached a significant agreement to increase their commitment to the humanitarian crisis in Afghanistan. The agreement was announced at a special session held yesterday, following discussions among the heads of state and government from across the globe.

The decision comes amid ongoing instability in Afghanistan, where thousands continue to face dire living conditions and a severe shortage of basic resources such as food, water, and medical supplies. According to the United Nations, nearly 23 million people in Afghanistan require humanitarian assistance, with over half of the population facing acute food insecurity.

In their joint statement, the G20 leaders pledged increased financial support to organisations such as the World Food Programme, UNICEF, and the International Committee of the Red Cross, with an emphasis on reaching the most vulnerable groups within Afghan society. These groups include women, children, and internally displaced persons who have been particularly affected by the country’s deteriorating situation.

The G20 also agreed to facilitate access for aid workers and ensure safe passage for humanitarian convoys. This move is expected to enhance the delivery of much-needed assistance to the Afghan population, which has been severely impacted by the withdrawal of international forces and the Taliban takeover last year.

The Irish Minister for Foreign Affairs, Simon Coveney, highlighted Ireland’s support for the initiative, stating that "the humanitarian crisis in Afghanistan requires a coordinated global response. Our commitment to aid and assistance is unwavering, and we call on other nations to join us in ensuring that no one is left behind."

Critics, however, have expressed concerns about the efficacy and accountability of aid distribution, arguing that corruption and mismanagement may hinder the successful implementation of the pledges. They urge the international community to establish robust mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the use of funds allocated to Afghanistan.

As part of their efforts, the G20 leaders also committed to supporting Afghanistan’s transition towards sustainable development and economic stability. This includes working towards the revival of key sectors like agriculture and education, which have been severely disrupted by the ongoing turmoil.

While the agreement marks a step forward in addressing the humanitarian needs of Afghans, many observers caution that more must be done to ensure a lasting impact. They emphasize the importance of sustained international engagement and a focus on rebuilding trust between the Afghan people and those providing assistance.

The full implementation of the G20's commitment will be closely monitored by both domestic and international organisations. As the humanitarian situation in Afghanistan remains fluid, the world's attention continues to be focused on finding viable solutions to alleviate suffering in this war-torn nation.
headline: G20 leaders agree to step up Afghan humanitarian effort

All Government Departments have agreed to adopt a new strategy that will see them accept cash payments up to €20 for small transactions, such as parking fines and other administrative fees. This decision, which was announced at a joint meeting of the Cabinet, aims to streamline the payment process and reduce bureaucracy for citizens.

The new policy is part of a wider plan designed to improve customer service across government departments. A spokesperson for the Department of Public Expenditure and Reform said, "We believe that accepting cash payments up to a certain limit will make it easier for people to pay for services, particularly those who may not have access to electronic payment methods."

The Minister for Public Expenditure and Reform, who attended the meeting, highlighted that the move would benefit both businesses and the public sector. "This initiative will enhance efficiency and convenience for both our staff and the citizens we serve," he stated.

Under the new strategy, departments will be able to accept cash payments of up to €20 for services such as utility bills, registration fees, and minor administrative charges. The move has been welcomed by consumer groups, who argue that it provides an alternative for those who may be unable or unwilling to use digital payment methods.

However, there are concerns among some quarters that this could lead to higher cash circulation and potential issues with counterfeiting. The Minister addressed these concerns, stating, "We have put robust measures in place to ensure that the new policy operates safely and securely. We will continue to work closely with financial and law enforcement agencies to monitor its implementation."

The Taoiseach, addressing the media following the announcement, reiterated the government’s commitment to modernising public services while maintaining a balance with traditional methods. "We want to ensure that all citizens can engage with their government easily and affordably, whether that means using cash or digital platforms," he said.

The new strategy is expected to come into effect next month, subject to final approval from the Oireachtas. The Minister expressed confidence that the policy would be well-received, saying, "We are confident that this move will make a significant difference in the way our citizens interact with their government."

The implementation of the strategy also marks a shift towards a more inclusive approach within the public sector, reflecting the government's broader commitment to accessibility and convenience for all citizens.
headline: All Govt depts to accept cash under new strategy

An Indian gang operated a fake police station in Dublin for an astonishing eight months, according to a major investigation carried out by An Garda Síochána. The operation, which involved multiple arrests and extensive surveillance, has shed light on the extent of fraud and deception perpetrated by the gang.

The gang, comprising members from India, established a fully functional but unauthorised police station in North Dublin, complete with a mock police uniform, equipment, and even an authentic-looking badge. This ruse allowed them to dupe unsuspecting individuals into believing they were dealing with legitimate law enforcement, and they used this cover to carry out their fraudulent activities.

According to sources within An Garda Síochána, the gang targeted a wide range of victims, including vulnerable individuals and businesses, by posing as police officers and conducting elaborate scams. These included fake arrests, bogus warrants, and false promises of legal assistance in exchange for payments and personal details.

A spokesperson for the Garda Commissioner stated, "This is a significant operation that highlights the sophistication and scale of organised crime in Ireland. The cooperation between various Garda divisions was crucial in uncovering and dismantling this network."

The investigation led to the arrest of six individuals and resulted in the recovery of thousands of euros in fraudulent transactions. Authorities are now working to trace additional victims and secure the return of any stolen funds.

The incident has raised concerns among community leaders about the vulnerability of certain sections of society to such deception. A spokesperson from the National Centre for Traveller Equality commented, "It's concerning that people in our communities may have been targeted in such a way. We urge anyone who believes they may have been a victim to come forward."

This case also underscores the importance of public awareness campaigns aimed at educating the public about common fraud tactics. The HSE, in conjunction with local authorities, is planning to launch a new awareness campaign targeting vulnerable groups and encouraging them to report any suspicious activities.

As the case continues to be prosecuted, the Gardaí have emphasised the need for vigilance and caution when engaging with representatives claiming to be from law enforcement agencies. A sombre atmosphere has pervaded the Birmingham Crown Court today as the inquests into the tragic bombing of the city’s pub in 1993 began. The court paused for a minute's silence to pay tribute to the victims before the proceedings commenced.

The inquest, which will examine the circumstances surrounding the explosion at the Admiral Duncan pub on 22 October 1993, has drawn significant attention from both the UK and Ireland. The bombing, which was one of a series carried out by the Provisional IRA, claimed the lives of 5 people and injured over 200 others.

Representatives from the families of the victims have expressed their hope that the inquest will provide some closure and bring to light any unresolved details from that fateful day. Speaking on behalf of the families, Marie Kennedy said, "It is important that we continue to seek justice for those who lost their lives."

Speaking to reporters outside the court, the Tánaiste, Simon Coveney, remarked on the gravity of the event, stating, "This tragedy had a profound impact on the city and the country as a whole. The inquest marks a crucial step in ensuring that the memory of those who died is not forgotten and that justice is served."

The inquest will involve testimony from survivors, eyewitnesses, and experts in forensic science and bomb disposal. The legal team representing the families will also present evidence to highlight the need for a more comprehensive investigation into the bombing, which they believe is still necessary to uncover all the truth behind the events that unfolded.

The proceedings are expected to last several weeks, with the court aiming to provide a thorough account of what led to the explosion and how it affected the lives of those involved. As the inquest progresses, it is hoped that it will contribute to a fuller understanding of this dark period in British and Irish history.

The Irish Government, through its Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, has been closely monitoring the inquest and stands ready to offer any assistance needed by the families and the court. Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade, Simon Coveney, issued a statement saying, "We are committed to supporting those affected by this tragedy and ensuring that every effort is made to understand the full extent of the incident."

As the inquest begins, the eyes of the nation and the international community are once again turned towards this significant historical event, hoping for answers and justice for all those involved.
headline: Birmingham bombing inquests start with minute's silence

text:
The World Health Organisation (WHO) has declared a high-risk emergency for the Ebola virus, a move that highlights the ongoing threat posed by the disease across several African nations. This declaration, which was announced on 10 June, underscores the need for urgent action and mobilisation of resources to combat the virus.

The Ebola outbreak, which has affected multiple countries in West Africa, is characterised by high mortality rates and rapid transmission among populations. The latest data from the WHO indicate that more than 3,000 cases have been reported since the first confirmed case in late 2022. Despite efforts by health organisations and local communities to contain the spread, the virus continues to pose a significant public health challenge.

In response to the declaration, the WHO has called for an increased deployment of healthcare workers, medical supplies, and financial support to affected regions. The organisation has also urged global health partners and governments to contribute to a fund dedicated to the response efforts. This fund will be used to finance various initiatives, including the provision of essential healthcare services, the implementation of infection control measures, and the development of diagnostic tools and treatments.

"The Ebola emergency is a stark reminder of the importance of coordinated international action," stated Dr Margaret Chan, the Director-General of the WHO, during a press conference. "We must act now to prevent a devastating humanitarian crisis."

The Irish Government, through its Department of Foreign Affairs, has expressed solidarity with the affected regions and has pledged its support to the WHO's efforts. A spokesperson for the department stated that Ireland would be contributing financially and through expert personnel to the ongoing response.

Local healthcare providers and NGOs have also stepped up their operations in the region, working alongside national and international health agencies to provide care to those affected by the virus. The Irish Aid programme has been instrumental in providing assistance, focusing on strengthening health systems, supporting community outreach, and ensuring access to safe water and sanitation facilities.

The declaration of a high-risk emergency is part of the WHO's strategic approach to managing public health emergencies of international concern. It is intended to galvanise global attention and resources to address the crisis comprehensively. As the situation remains fluid, the WHO continues to monitor the outbreak closely and will provide regular updates on the progress of containment efforts.

With the threat of Ebola persisting, there is a call for sustained vigilance and collaborative action to ensure that the necessary resources are available to tackle the disease effectively. The international community, including Ireland, is being urged to play its part in mitigating the impact of the virus and protecting vulnerable populations.
headline: Explained: WHO's high-risk Ebola emergency

text:
Hospitals across Ireland welcomed some very special arrivals on New Year’s Day, marking the beginning of a new year with the arrival of the first babies of 2024.

In Cork University Hospital, two tiny but healthy additions to their families made their grand entrances. The hospital, renowned for its obstetric services, saw the birth of a 3.2kg baby boy at 10:45 am and another healthy baby girl, weighing in at 3.1kg, just before midnight. The Dublin Cildir, St. Vincent’s Maternity Hospital, experienced its first birth of the new year around 2:00 am. This was a 3.2kg baby girl born to a second-time mum. Her father, beaming with pride, said he was “overwhelmed with happiness.”

These joyful moments were not isolated incidents. Across the country, healthcare staff reported a steady stream of deliveries, with many more families bringing new life into the world. The HSE’s Director of Public Health, Dr. Caroline McLaughlin, praised the dedication of healthcare professionals during these crucial times.

“The birth of these first babies of 2024 is a symbol of new beginnings and hope,” said Dr. McLaughlin. “We extend our warmest congratulations to all those new parents and wish them all the best in the coming year.”

As the new year began, hospitals continued to operate with heightened vigilance and care, ensuring that all deliveries were handled with the utmost professionalism. The efforts of medical staff, midwives, and support teams were evident in the safety and well-being of both mothers and their newborns.

New Year’s Day has always been marked by a flurry of activity in maternity units, and this year was no exception. As the sun rose over Ireland on the morning of January 1st, it brought with it fresh hope and the promise of a new beginning for countless Irish families.

Two individuals have tragically lost their lives, while ten others were hospitalised following a series of explosions at a steel plant in the United States, local authorities have confirmed. The incident occurred early yesterday morning at a steel manufacturing facility in the town of Millbrook, located in the state of Alabama.

Emergency services were first alerted to the situation shortly after 04:30 local time. Witnesses described a series of loud explosions followed by the release of thick black smoke, visible several kilometres away. The explosions were so powerful they shook nearby buildings, prompting residents to evacuate from their homes.

The steel plant, owned by the multinational corporation Millbrook Metallurgics, has been temporarily shut down pending a full safety inspection. Preliminary investigations suggest that the cause of the explosion could be linked to a chemical reaction during the production process, but further tests are required to confirm this hypothesis.

In the aftermath of the explosions, a coordinated response involving the local fire department, the Alabama Department of Public Safety, and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) was initiated. A large number of personnel and medical teams were dispatched to the scene to provide assistance to those affected.

Among the injured, a number of employees sustained serious burns, while others suffered from smoke inhalation. All of those hospitalised were transferred to nearby medical facilities, including two regional hospitals and a trauma centre. The condition of the victims ranges from critical to stable, according to the latest reports from the hospitals involved.

The incident has raised concerns about workplace safety standards, particularly within the metallurgical sector. Local officials stated that they would work closely with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) to conduct a thorough investigation into the causes of the explosions.

The steel plant’s management released a statement expressing their deepest sympathies to the families of those who lost their lives, and offering support to all those injured. The company has also pledged to cooperate fully with the ongoing investigation and to take necessary steps to prevent similar incidents in the future.

This tragedy has brought the community together in support of the affected individuals and families. Local businesses and organisations have offered their condolences and assistance, providing relief funds and resources to help those impacted by the disaster.

As the investigation continues, authorities are urging anyone with information related to the explosions to come forward. Inquiries can be directed through official channels or anonymously if preferred.

For the affected families, the road to recovery is likely to be long and challenging. As the full extent of the damage and impact becomes clearer, ongoing support will be crucial for the community and the families of the deceased and injured.

Critics have called for a thorough investigation into the reasons behind the increased costs, suggesting that a failure in project planning and oversight could be at play. "Students and educators are already facing financial pressures, and they need a reliable IT system more than ever."

The HSE, which is involved in providing support services through SUSI, has been praised for its efforts to stabilise the system, but concerns remain over the long-term impact on student welfare. "While we understand the difficulties, the focus now must be on ensuring that students can access the support they need without further delay," added HSE spokesperson, Maria McCarthy.

As the debate intensifies, the HEA continues to work towards a comprehensive solution, with plans to enhance the existing platform and address its vulnerabilities. However, the ongoing delays and increased costs have put pressure on both the HEA and the government to provide a clear and transparent explanation of the circumstances surrounding the project.

"We must learn from these experiences and ensure that such issues do not arise in future projects," stated Brian Casey, chairperson of the PAC. "Transparency and accountability are crucial, and we will be holding all parties accountable for the actions taken."

The situation has also drawn attention to the broader challenges facing technology projects in the public sector, with critics arguing that a more robust regulatory framework and improved scrutiny processes are necessary to prevent similar oversights in the future.
headline: Significant overspend in cost for SUSI IT system

text:
The sunken Indonesian submarine NAMRI S-268 has been located off the coast of Ambon Island in Indonesia, confirming the worst fears of the Indonesian Navy and families of those onboard. The vessel, which had been missing since 15 November, was discovered in two distinct sections, with debris spread over a large area, indicating that the sub had suffered catastrophic damage.

The discovery was made by a joint operation involving Indonesian naval vessels and maritime experts. The team employed advanced sonar technology and divers to scour the sea floor before locating what they believe to be the remains of the submarine. The fragments were found at a depth of approximately 400 metres off the coast of Ambon, a key strategic location in eastern Indonesia.

The Indonesian Navy has confirmed that the sub is indeed the NAMRI S-268, which had been carrying 53 personnel when it went missing. The exact cause of the sinking is yet to be determined, but initial assessments suggest that the vessel broke into three parts upon impact with the seafloor.

Grief and shock have been evident among families and friends of the missing crew members. The Indonesian Defence Minister, Dr Rini Soemarno, expressed deep sorrow at the confirmation and announced that a comprehensive investigation would be launched to determine the precise circumstances leading to the tragedy.

"This is a heartbreaking day for all of us," she said during a press conference. "We are deeply saddened by the loss of life and are committed to providing every possible assistance to the families and loved ones of the crew."

The rescue operations have been ongoing, but with limited success. The harsh weather conditions and difficult underwater terrain have complicated efforts to retrieve bodies and salvage equipment from the sunken vessel. The Indonesian Navy continues to work closely with maritime authorities to ensure a thorough and professional investigation into the incident.

The discovery comes as a stark reminder of the challenges faced by naval forces around the world and the importance of ongoing training and safety protocols. The international community has offered support to Indonesia in the wake of the tragedy, with several nations pledging their assistance in search and rescue operations and investigations.

As the search and recovery operations continue, questions remain about the long-term implications for the Indonesian Navy and its capabilities. The incident has already prompted calls for a review of submarine safety measures and operational procedures within the Indonesian military.

The news of the sub's demise has caused widespread distress, particularly among the families of the missing, who had been hoping against hope for news of their loved ones' survival. In the coming days, more details are expected to emerge as the Indonesian authorities work to piece together exactly what transpired on that fateful night.
headline: Sunken Indonesian submarine found broken in three

text:
Following a series of challenges faced by Shannon Airport over recent months, it has been announced that the managing director, Michael Sheridan, will be stepping down from his position with immediate effect. Mr Sheridan, who joined the airport in 2017, has played a significant role in the strategic direction of the facility during a period marked by fluctuating aviation demands and regulatory pressures.

The announcement comes at a critical juncture for the regional airport, which has seen substantial fluctuations in passenger numbers and has been grappling with issues related to operational efficiency and customer service. According to a spokesperson for Shannon Airport, Mr Sheridan's departure follows discussions with the board regarding the airport’s future trajectory and the need to bolster its management team to navigate the evolving landscape of air travel.

"The board and I have decided that now is the right time for a fresh perspective and new leadership to steer the airport into the next phase of its development," stated Catherine Hayes, Chairperson of Shannon Airport. "We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Michael for his dedication and the contributions he has made during his tenure."

In his statement, Mr Sheridan expressed his commitment to the airport and the local economy. "It has been an honour to lead Shannon Airport through a challenging yet rewarding period. I am confident that the airport is well positioned for continued growth and success under new leadership," he said.

The search for a successor is currently underway, with the board committed to finding a candidate who can bring a fresh approach to leadership and address the strategic objectives outlined by the organisation. The appointment will involve a comprehensive evaluation process to ensure that the new managing director aligns with the vision and goals of Shannon Airport.

As Shannon Airport looks ahead, stakeholders across the region are closely monitoring the developments, keen to see how the airport will continue to contribute to Ireland’s transport infrastructure and support economic activity in the area.
headline: Shannon Airport Managing Director is to leave his role

text:
A pipe bomb was successfully defused on Thursday afternoon after it was discovered in a residential area in County Down. The incident occurred in the Ballymena townland, prompting a swift response from local law enforcement.

Gardaí were called to the scene shortly before 2 pm, following reports of a suspicious object near a house. Upon arrival, they secured the area and alerted the National Bomb Disposal Unit. A specialist team arrived on the scene within minutes and began the process of safely defusing the device.

No injuries were reported during the incident. Local residents were evacuated from their homes as a precautionary measure. The operation lasted for several hours, with Garda officers and bomb disposal experts working collaboratively to ensure public safety.

The HSE’s Public Health Agency (PHA) advised residents to remain indoors until further notice due to the presence of hazardous materials at the site. Once the area was deemed safe, the evacuation orders were lifted, and life gradually returned to normal.

The discovery and subsequent defusal of the pipe bomb highlight the ongoing vigilance of the security services in Northern Ireland. The exact nature of the device and the reasons behind its presence are still under investigation. The Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) has launched an inquiry into the matter, seeking to identify any potential motives or individuals responsible.

Local representatives, including the Member of Parliament (MP) for Mid-Ulster, highlighted the importance of community cooperation and the crucial role played by local people in reporting suspicious items promptly. He urged residents to continue to be vigilant and report any unusual activity to the authorities immediately.

The incident, while concerning, did not disrupt essential services in the region. Local businesses and services resumed operations as normal in the evening, with a sense of relief prevailing among the community.

This event serves as a stark reminder of the continued security challenges faced in Northern Ireland and the dedication of law enforcement agencies to protect the public.
headline: Pipe bomb defused after being found in Co Down

text:
In a significant escalation of tensions in the Gaza Strip, Israeli Defence Minister, Mr Bezalel Smotrich, has publicly threatened to annex parts of the territory, a move that has sent shockwaves through regional politics and international diplomatic circles.

Mr Smotrich’s comments were made during a speech at the Knesset, where he called for the immediate inclusion of parts of the Gaza Strip under Israeli jurisdiction. He justified his stance by referencing historical claims and territorial sovereignty arguments. "The people who live there [in Gaza] are our people," Mr Smotrich stated, arguing that it is only natural for them to be included within the Israeli state.

This announcement comes amid ongoing tensions and a series of rocket attacks from Gaza into Israel, which have seen both sides exchange harsh words and threats. The Israeli government has been under increasing domestic and international pressure to de-escalate the situation but has shown little inclination to do so.

The threat of annexation has drawn swift and strong rebukes from Palestinian leaders and their international backers. Palestinian Authority President, Mr Mahmoud Abbas, described the move as "irresponsible" and warned of dire consequences if it proceeds. The European Union, along with the United States, expressed concern over the potential for further instability.

The Israeli government's position on the matter remains firm, backed by a coalition of right-wing parties that support the annexation bid. However, legal experts and human rights organisations argue that such a move would violate international law, including the Fourth Geneva Convention, which prohibits the transfer of populations from the occupying power to the occupied territory.

Analysts are warning that Mr Smotrich's threat could lead to a prolonged period of heightened conflict and could further undermine the already fragile ceasefire agreements between Israel and Hamas, the militant group controlling Gaza.

The situation remains volatile, with the international community closely watching developments and urging all sides to pursue a path of de-escalation and dialogue. As the region continues to face intense pressure, the possibility of a military confrontation looms large, raising concerns about the safety and security of civilians on both sides of the conflict.
headline: Israeli defence minister threatens to annex parts of Gaza

text:
The District Court in Belfast heard on Tuesday that 27 individuals have been sentenced in what is being described as the biggest tax fraud case in Northern Ireland (NI). The case, which spanned several years, saw the accused charged with attempting to defraud the Inland Revenue of significant amounts through various fraudulent means.

Among those sentenced were 14 men and 13 women ranging from their mid-30s to late 60s, all of whom pleaded guilty to charges related to tax evasion and other financial crimes. The maximum sentence handed down was five years in prison, with many of those convicted given shorter terms depending on the severity of their involvement in the fraud.

District Judge Paul McCague presided over the cases and noted the substantial financial impact these actions had on the Northern Ireland economy, stating, "These individuals engaged in a concerted effort to evade tax obligations that would have provided essential funding for public services."

Gardaí from the Criminal Justice Branch and Revenue Investigations Unit worked closely with their counterparts in the Irish Revenue Commissioners and HMRC in the UK to gather evidence, leading to the successful prosecution of the defendants. The investigation began after a tip-off in 2019 and resulted in a comprehensive trial where testimonies from key witnesses played a crucial role.

Following the sentencing, the Chief Crown Prosecutor in Northern Ireland commented, "Today’s sentences send a clear message that those who attempt to undermine the tax system will face the full force of the law." He added, "It is vital that such actions are deterred and that fair contributions are made towards our essential public services."

The HSE and local authorities in Northern Ireland have expressed relief at the outcome, highlighting the importance of such prosecutions in maintaining the integrity of the tax system and ensuring resources are available for healthcare and social welfare services.

As the community and authorities in Northern Ireland continue to assess the implications of this major tax fraud conviction, discussions around tax reform and enforcement are likely to be at the forefront of future policy debates.
headline: 27 people sentenced in biggest tax fraud case in NI

text:
Sixty-one migrants have drowned after their ship capsized off the coast of Libya, according to official reports from the Libyan coast guard. The incident took place on 24 October near Zuwara, about 170 kilometres east of the capital, Tripoli.

Eyewitnesses reported seeing a vessel filled with people struggling in rough seas before it suddenly capsized. The Libyan coast guard was among the first responders, but the challenging conditions hampered their efforts to rescue those aboard. By the time search and rescue operations were concluded, bodies were recovered from the waters.

The victims included people from various countries such as Eritrea, Nigeria, and Gambia, highlighting the dangerous journey many undertake in pursuit of a better life in Europe. Aid workers expressed deep concern over the loss of life and called for increased international support to address the root causes of such tragedies.

Irish authorities and organisations working with refugees and migrants have condemned the incident, urging greater action from the international community to improve conditions and provide safe routes for asylum seekers. The Irish Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade has vowed to step up diplomatic efforts to ensure safer maritime migration policies are put in place.

In response to the tragedy, the European Union announced an urgent meeting of member states to discuss immediate measures to prevent further such incidents, while also reiterating its commitment to ongoing support for Libya in addressing the crisis. The EU Commissioner for Migration, Home Affairs and Citizenship stated, "This is yet another tragic reminder of the human cost of irregular migration and the urgent need for a comprehensive approach to managing migration flows."

The incident has also raised new questions about the effectiveness of current rescue operations and the broader Mediterranean migration crisis. Human rights groups are calling for increased funding and resources dedicated to search and rescue missions, alongside efforts to tackle the root causes of displacement.

The families of the deceased are seeking answers and justice. Irish diplomatic channels are assisting in coordinating consular support and providing assistance to relatives who wish to come to Ireland for the burial of their loved ones.

This tragedy serves as a stark reminder of the ongoing humanitarian challenges and underscores the global responsibility to address the complex issues surrounding migration.
headline: 61 migrants drown after shipwreck off Libya

text:
An appeal has been issued across the Leinster region to trace a man who has been missing from his home in Dundalk for over two weeks. The man, whose name has not yet been released pending notification of family members, was last seen on 15 March at his residence on Westview Avenue.

The local community is concerned following the prolonged absence of the individual. Neighbours reported that they have not seen or heard from him since the day he was last spotted walking his dog in the early evening. Local gardaí confirmed that a thorough search of the area has been conducted but no leads have emerged.

Det Supt Eoin McHugh, who is leading the investigation, stated, "We are appealing to anyone with any information, no matter how insignificant it may seem, to come forward. The urgency of this case cannot be overstated."

The man, described as being in his mid-40s and of medium build, was last seen wearing a dark jacket, jeans, and brown boots. Authorities have expressed concern for his safety and wellbeing given the passage of time without contact.

The family of the missing man, now being assisted by the Health Service Executive (HSE) crisis team, is also urging anyone with information to come forward. They asked the public to be vigilant and report any sightings or relevant details to gardaí immediately.

The incident has drawn attention from the local media and political representatives, with both the Dáil and Seanad expressing solidarity with the family. A statement from the office of the Tánaiste, Cian Ó Fádhail, has been issued, offering support to the investigation and appealing for public assistance.

Residents in the neighbourhood have rallied together, organising a community vigil in memory of the missing man and in support of his loved ones. Organisers hope that the gathering will help bring comfort and perhaps even lead to new clues in the search for the man.

As the search continues, gardaí have advised local residents to remain alert for any suspicious activity in the area and to maintain their vigilance. The appeal to the public to provide information remains ongoing, with a strong emphasis on the potential risks associated with prolonged unexplained absences.
headline: Appeal issued to trace man missing from Dundalk

text:
In a significant U-turn, Attorney General Jeremy Starmer has admitted he made a mistake in his decision to appoint former Irish politician Peter Mandelson as the UK's new envoy to the United States. Mr Starmer made the admission in a statement to the House of Commons on Thursday.

In his remarks, Mr Starmer stated, "I acknowledge that I erred in my judgement in naming Mr Mandelson for the position. It is clear that his appointment did not fully consider the broader political implications and public reaction." The statement comes after widespread criticism from Conservative MPs and the public following the controversial appointment.

Mr Mandelson, who served as European Commissioner, Chief of Staff to Tony Blair, and European Commissioner, was chosen to replace Sir Ivan Rogers as the UK’s ambassador to the US. The move was intended to leverage his diplomatic experience and connections. However, it quickly became contentious due to Mr Mandelson's past involvement in the controversial beef crisis during his time as EU trade commissioner, which led to the imposition of a tariff on British beef exports.

The admission by Mr Starmer signals a shift in tone from the initial defiant stance taken by Downing Street regarding the appointment. The statement also hints at potential changes in the selection process for future diplomatic positions.

Reacting to Starmer's admission, Conservative Party Leader Liz Truss said, "It is good to see some honesty from the government. The public needed to hear this. Now, we must focus on ensuring that the right person is appointed and one who can effectively represent the UK’s interests abroad."

Meanwhile, Labour MPs welcomed Starmer’s acknowledgment but expressed reservations about whether the change was enough. A spokesperson for the Opposition stated, "Jeremy Starmer’s admission is a step in the right direction, but Labour members of parliament hope it will lead to a more transparent and fair process moving forward."

The controversy over Mr Mandelson’s appointment underscores the delicate balance between leveraging experienced political figures and navigating the complex landscape of international relations and domestic politics. As the fallout continues, the incident highlights the challenges faced by the UK government in making high-profile appointments while maintaining public support.
headline: Starmer says he was wrong to name Mandelson as US envoy

text:
The Government has announced an expansion of the free contraception scheme, aiming to provide more comprehensive sexual health services to all eligible individuals nationwide. This move is part of a broader strategy to enhance access to healthcare, particularly among younger demographics.

Under the new arrangements, which come into effect from next month, a wider range of contraceptive methods will be made available at no cost to those between 16 and 26 years of age, with certain conditions. The scheme now includes long-acting reversible contraceptives such as intrauterine devices (IUDs) and implants, which were previously not covered. The Department of Health stated that these additions would provide users with longer-term options without the need for constant attention.

Speaking on the announcement, the Minister for Health, Simon Harris, TD, emphasised the importance of accessible healthcare services. "This expansion of our free contraception scheme is a significant step towards ensuring that every individual can make informed decisions about their reproductive health," he said. "We believe that providing a variety of choices will empower young people to take control of their health and plan their future."

Health professionals have welcomed the changes, citing higher uptake rates for certain forms of contraception as a key benefit. "Having a greater selection of options makes it easier for young people to find a method that suits them," explained Dr. Sarah O'Sullivan, a leading gynaecologist. "This can lead to more consistent use, which in turn reduces unwanted pregnancies and related health issues."

The HSE, which manages the scheme, plans to increase funding to ensure all participating clinics and pharmacies are adequately equipped to provide these new services. A spokesperson for the HSE added, "We are working closely with partners across the healthcare sector to roll out these enhancements smoothly and ensure that there are no disruptions to current services."

While the scheme remains free for those within the age range, it's important to note that additional costs may apply if a service is provided outside standard clinic hours or if special equipment is required. The Department of Health is also exploring further expansions, including potential coverage for non-medicated forms of contraception.

In a statement, the Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, acknowledged the significance of this initiative. "Improving access to sexual and reproductive healthcare is a cornerstone of public health policy," he said. "By supporting our young people in making informed choices, we can foster a healthier, more inclusive society."

The expanded free contraception scheme is expected to reach thousands of young adults, contributing to both individual wellbeing and societal benefits. As Ireland continues to prioritise health and social welfare, this move is seen as a positive step forward in providing accessible and modern healthcare services.
headline: Government expands free contraception scheme

text:
Gardaí are appealing to the public for information following the death of a 54-year-old man in Dublin city centre on Tuesday evening.

The man was found deceased at approximately 6:30 pm near O’Connell Bridge, Dublin 1. An Garda Síochána attended the scene shortly after the report came through and began a formal investigation. The deceased has yet to be formally identified, and his family have been informed.

Det Insp Niamh O'Sullivan of the Garda National Homicide Investigation Unit said, "We are treating this matter as unexplained at this stage and are appealing to anyone who may have witnessed the incident or has any relevant information to contact us immediately."

Eyewitnesses reported seeing a male in distress moments before his body was discovered. "I saw him walking along the bridge and then suddenly fall," said local resident, who wished to remain anonymous. "It looked like he might have had some kind of seizure but it was very quick."

The incident took place during rush hour traffic in one of Dublin’s busiest areas, prompting concern from local residents. "It's shocking really, to see something like that happen so close to where we live and work," said Ciarán McManus, a shopkeeper nearby. "There should be more security around such areas during peak times."

Dublin City Council has called for a review of safety measures in the vicinity of key bridges and public spaces. "Our priority is ensuring the safety of our citizens and visitors," said a spokesperson for the council. "We are in discussions with the Gardaí about additional surveillance and emergency response protocols in these areas."

The HSE, meanwhile, has advised members of the public to stay alert and report any unusual activity in public spaces. Dr. Aoife Mac Gabhann, Consultant in Public Health Medicine, stated, "Our teams are here to support anyone affected by this tragic event and to help ensure that similar incidents can be prevented in the future."

The Gardaí have asked that members of the public who were in the area around O’Connell Bridge on Tuesday evening come forward with any details they may have. They also appealed for anyone with CCTV footage of the time to contact them.

As the investigation continues, the Gardaí are keen to piece together what led to the man’s death and to rule out any suspicious circumstances. "We will leave no stone unturned in our efforts to establish exactly what transpired," concluded Det Insp O'Sullivan.
headline: Gardaí appeal for witnesses following death of man

text:
The Minister for Children and Youth Affairs, along with housing and welfare advocates, expressed major concerns today over the rapid increase in child homelessness, citing a significant rise in the number of families with children seeking emergency accommodation.

According to the latest figures from the HSE’s National Accommodation Register, there has been a 20% increase in the number of children in emergency accommodation in the past year alone. This surge in numbers has left many parents and activists deeply worried about the well-being and future prospects of these young people.

"Child homelessness is not just an issue of finding a roof over their heads; it has profound impacts on education, health, and overall development," stated Marie Conway, a TD representing an area with high rates of homelessness. "We need immediate action and a comprehensive strategy to address the root causes."

The government acknowledged these concerns, announcing additional funding of €15 million to support emergency shelters and transitional housing schemes across the country. However, critics argue that while increased funding is necessary, it must be accompanied by systemic changes to prevent future occurrences of child homelessness.

"We need to focus on long-term solutions, such as affordable housing, better mental health services, and stronger family supports," said Councillor John O'Connor, chairman of the Local Government and Community Development Committee. "Policymakers must work collaboratively to ensure that every child has the opportunity to thrive in a safe and stable environment."

The Minister for Children and Youth Affairs, speaking on the floor of the Dáil, called for greater inter-departmental cooperation to tackle this crisis. "It is crucial that we take a holistic approach to addressing child homelessness, involving all relevant stakeholders, including local authorities, community organisations, and non-governmental bodies," she stated.

Garda spokespersons have also highlighted the increased strain on emergency services, noting a corresponding rise in calls related to homelessness. "Our officers are frequently called to assist families in crisis, often under very challenging circumstances," said Superintendent Eoin McCarthy. "More resources and coordination between agencies will be essential to meet the growing demand for our services."

As the debate continues, advocates for vulnerable children remain optimistic that collaborative efforts can yield positive outcomes. "The challenge is immense, but with sustained commitment and action, we can make a real difference in the lives of these children," concluded Dr. Aoife MacDermott, a spokesperson for the Childcare Ireland network.

The Irish public and policymakers alike are being urged to consider the long-term implications of child homelessness and the urgent need to implement effective, sustainable measures to protect the most vulnerable members of society.
headline: Major concern over pace of child homelessness

text:
Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across Ireland have collectively lost billions of euros over the past year due to stringent public health measures aimed at curbing the spread of the coronavirus, according to a new report released today by the Chambers of Commerce Ireland (CCI).

The report, entitled "The Economic Impact of Pandemic Restrictions on SMEs," details the financial toll of repeated lockdowns, border closures, and strict social distancing guidelines on businesses of all sizes. The findings indicate that SMEs, which account for approximately 99% of all Irish businesses and employ nearly half of the country’s workforce, have been disproportionately affected by the economic fallout.

Speaking at the launch of the report, Fiona Barry, President of CCI, expressed grave concern about the state of Irish SMEs. "We are seeing a staggering €3.2 billion in lost sales and €1.5 billion in unrealised profits due to the various restrictions implemented since the onset of the pandemic," she said. "These figures do not capture the emotional and mental strain our members are experiencing."

The report highlights several key areas of impact. One significant challenge is the closure of physical premises, particularly in sectors like hospitality, retail, and tourism. The report notes that over 80% of SMEs had to close temporarily at some point during the pandemic, with many forced to operate online, which has proven challenging for small firms without established e-commerce platforms.

Furthermore, the report cites the cost of compliance with public health guidelines, including hygiene measures, PPE provision, and staff training, as contributing factors to financial strain. "While these measures were necessary for public health, they also added significantly to operational costs," said Mr Barry.
