text:
A Dublin man of Indian origin has been found guilty of indecent assault after a “creepy” incident on a city bus left a woman shaken, details emerged in the District Court on Tuesday.

The accused, aged 29, was arraigned before Justice Brendan O’Dwyer following a hearing where the victim described how she was subjected to unwanted and invasive touch during a journey through the city centre. The incident occurred late one evening when the woman boarded a bus and was seated beside the defendant, who then proceeded to make unprovoked and unwelcome contact with her.

In court, the woman recounted the distressing encounter, stating that the defendant had placed his hand on her knee and attempted to move it further towards her private parts. She explained how the experience left her feeling “very upset and scared”.

The prosecution argued that the evidence, which included CCTV footage from the bus and corroborated witness statements, provided a clear case against the defendant. The defence, however, maintained that the charges were exaggerated and suggested that there may have been some misinterpretation of the incident.

After deliberating for less than an hour, the jury returned a unanimous verdict of guilty. The accused, upon hearing the verdict, appeared visibly shaken and did not comment.

Judge O’Dwyer adjourned sentencing until next month, stating that he wished to consider a full range of aggravating and mitigating factors before passing sentence. Legal experts predict that the judge is likely to impose a non-custodial sentence, taking into account the defendant’s lack of prior convictions and cooperation during the trial.

The victim, who wishes to remain anonymous, stated that while she is relieved the case has concluded, she still struggles with the experience and hopes it will raise awareness about the need for improved safety measures on public transport. 

The case also highlighted ongoing concerns about personal safety in urban areas and the importance of community vigilance and support services for those affected by such incidents. The HSE has since announced plans to enhance its services and provide additional resources for victims of sexual assault, including increased funding for counselling and support groups.

The incident has caused widespread concern among commuters, prompting calls for stricter security measures and a comprehensive review of safety protocols on buses and other public transport. Mayor of Dublin, Councillor Ciara Sarsfield, pledged the city council would work closely with the transport authority to ensure that all necessary steps are taken to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.
headline: ‘Creepy’ migrant from India found guilty of groping woman on bus in Dublin

text:
In a heartfelt statement released today, renowned British comedian Russell Brand expressed his gratitude to his supporters following what he described as a “distressing week.” Speaking from his home in London, Brand detailed how he had been grappling with personal issues and the challenges of managing a successful career while maintaining a high public profile.

Brand, who has long been a figure of controversy and fascination within the media landscape, acknowledged the support he had received during a time when he felt vulnerable. “These past few days have been tough,” Brand said, “but I’ve been incredibly moved by the messages of encouragement and love I’ve received.”

He continued, “The outpouring of support from people all over the world has been a lifeline for me. It reminds me that, despite the difficulties we face individually and collectively, there is still much that binds us together as a community.”

The comedian touched on a recent public dispute over allegations of tax avoidance, which had seen him facing scrutiny both nationally and internationally. He stressed that he was working closely with legal advisors to address these concerns and hoped to clarify any misunderstandings through transparent communication.

Brand concluded his statement by reaffirming his commitment to his work and his fans. “I want everyone to know that I’m here for the long haul, and I will continue to do my best to entertain and inspire you all, as always.”

His statement came ahead of a series of upcoming performances at Dublin’s National Concert Hall, where he is set to take to the stage to perform his stand-up comedy show. Despite the challenges of the last week, Brand expressed confidence in the response of his audience, stating, “There’s nothing like a live audience to lift your spirits.”

The Liberal, in its coverage of the statement, highlighted the ongoing interest in Brand’s career and personal life, noting the continuing relevance of his work in Ireland and beyond.
headline: Russell Brand thanks his supporters after “distressing week”

text:
Aer Lingus has announced the cancellation of 25 further flights following ongoing industrial unrest among its pilots. The decision comes after the airline and the Irish Pilots Association (IPA) failed to reach a resolution over pay and working conditions during recent roundtable discussions.

In a statement, Aer Lingus confirmed that these cancellations will impact routes both within Ireland and to various destinations across Europe. A spokesperson for the airline said that they were working closely with customers to minimise disruption, offering alternative flights where possible and providing full refunds for those who have already purchased tickets for affected journeys.

The IPA has described the current situation as “disappointing” and stated their determination to press ahead with their demands. “Our members are committed to their profession but are also entitled to fair remuneration and reasonable working conditions,” said Martin Kenny, the IPA's president.

The dispute began when the IPA expressed concerns about a proposed restructure aimed at reducing costs, particularly regarding overtime payments and the introduction of more flexible rosters. Both sides have acknowledged that the talks have been challenging, with neither party willing to budge on key points.

Minister for Transport Eamon Ryan, who has been keeping a close eye on the situation, called on both parties to return to the negotiating table. "It is in everyone's best interests to find a solution that keeps our air links secure while ensuring that pilots are treated fairly," he stated.

Meanwhile, commuters and business travellers are being urged to keep an eye on flight updates and to plan their journeys accordingly. The Irish Aviation Authority (IAA) is monitoring the situation closely and has assured the public that it is prepared to take any necessary steps to ensure passenger safety and service reliability.

As negotiations continue, Aer Lingus warned that the number of cancelled flights could increase unless a compromise is reached soon. The company reiterated its commitment to operating a reliable and efficient service but stressed the need for the pilot union to come to an agreement with the airline.

This latest development highlights the ongoing challenges faced by the aviation industry in balancing cost management with employee welfare. The situation remains fluid, with both sides expressing their willingness to return to discussions with the hope of resolving the dispute amicably.
headline: Aer Lingus cancels a further 25 flights as pilots’ dispute continues

text:
Road carnage continues to claim lives with another tragic incident that occurred in County Kildare over the weekend. A woman in her 50s lost her life when a vehicle collided with another on the N70 near Naas on Saturday evening. The unfortunate incident highlights ongoing concerns about road safety across Ireland.

According to the Gardaí, the accident happened shortly before 8 PM, resulting in multiple injuries to those involved. The victim was identified as Ciara Nolan from Celbridge, who was pronounced dead at the scene. Her family expressed their shock and sadness at the sudden loss.

Emergency services were quickly mobilised upon receiving reports of the collision. Medics worked tirelessly to save the injured, but despite their efforts, Ms Nolan succumbed to her injuries. The cause of the crash is currently under investigation by the Garda National Roads Policing Bureau, with preliminary reports indicating that the exact circumstances leading to the accident are still being determined.

Local TDs have called for increased awareness and enforcement of road safety laws. "This tragedy serves as yet another stark reminder of the importance of road safety," stated Cllr Dermot Hayes of the Kildare North local authority area. "We need to do more to educate drivers about the dangers they face and the potential consequences of risky behaviour."

The incident has also raised concerns among community leaders and residents. "Ciara was a much-loved member of our community," said Brendan O'Flynn, chairman of the Celbridge Development Association. "Her loss will be deeply felt by all who knew her."

In recent years, there has been a growing call for stricter measures to combat rising road fatalities. The Government has promised to review current road safety strategies and implement additional initiatives aimed at reducing the number of accidents on Irish roads.

As the district mourns the loss of Ciara Nolan, her family and friends offer their condolences to everyone affected by this tragedy. The Gardaí continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the accident, and anyone with information is urged to contact them.
headline: Road carnage continues, after woman in her 50s dies in crash in Co. Kildare

text:
Novak Djokovic is aiming to etch his name further into tennis history today as he bids to claim his 23rd Grand Slam title at the French Open in Paris. The Serb, who has already won the competition twice, will face Stefanos Tsitsipas in the final match scheduled for late afternoon at the Roland Garros Stadium.

Djokovic's journey through the tournament has been nothing short of exceptional, marked by resilience and dominance. He has not lost a single set since the quarter-finals and has showcased a level of tennis that has left spectators and pundits alike in awe. Today, he has the opportunity to become the first male player in the Open Era to win three consecutive French Opens, a feat that would cement his status as one of the all-time greats.

The Serbian star is no stranger to high-pressure situations, having already achieved milestones that few athletes can claim. With a victory today, Djokovic would surpass Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal’s combined tally of 22 Grand Slam titles. This would place him firmly atop the rankings of all-time Grand Slam winners, a milestone that the sports world is watching closely.

Commenting ahead of the final, Djokovic expressed his determination and focus on the task at hand. "It’s been a special week here in Paris," he said. "I’m looking forward to finishing it with a bang. My team and I have put in a lot of hard work to get here, and now it’s time to deliver."

The French Open final is set to be a thrilling spectacle, with millions tuning in across the globe to witness what could be another iconic moment in tennis history. As the match approaches, the atmosphere in the stadium is electric, with fans from around the world hoping to bear witness to the historic moment.

For the Irish contingent, there is excitement too, as many will be following the match with keen interest, eager to see how Djokovic performs on the hallowed grounds of Roland Garros. The Irish media will be on hand to report back on the outcome, ensuring that the nation is kept abreast of every moment of this momentous occasion.
headline: Novak Djokovic aims to become the greatest of them all today by winning a 23rd Grand Slam at the French Open in Paris

text:
A man in his late 50s was sadly pronounced dead following what local authorities described as a "medical incident" that occurred in the city of Cork on Friday evening.

The man, who resided in the Douglas district, was reportedly experiencing health issues when he sought assistance from emergency services. According to a spokesperson for the HSE, emergency responders were dispatched to the scene shortly after being alerted and provided on-site medical treatment.

Gardaí have cordoned off the area around the incident, which occurred near the River Lee. The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the man’s passing is ongoing and is being handled by the Garda Síochána and the Office of the Chief Coroners.

Speaking to reporters at the scene, Cllr Seán O'Sullivan expressed shock and sorrow over the tragic event. "This is a community that has been deeply affected by the loss of one of its residents," he said. "Our thoughts and condolences are with the family at this difficult time."

Irish Medical Organisation (IMO) president Dr. Fionnuala Connolly urged local residents to remain vigilant regarding their health and take all necessary precautions, particularly during this challenging period.

The incident has raised concerns among local healthcare providers about the adequacy of services in the area. A spokesperson for the Cork Partnership Health Programme stated that further investigations will be carried out to determine whether additional resources are needed to support similar situations in the future.

As the community comes to terms with the loss, various local organisations have offered support and assistance to the family and friends of the deceased. Memorials are expected to be held in the coming days in tribute to the man's life.

Update: Further investigations by the coroner’s office revealed that the man had a pre-existing heart condition which likely contributed to the sudden medical emergency. The Gardaí have closed their inquiries but are awaiting further reports from the medical examiner before proceeding with the case file.
headline: Man sadly passes away in Cork following “medical incident”

text:
Met Éireann has expressed growing concern as the country continues to break its May temperature records yet again. On Monday, the mercury soared to an unprecedented 30.5 degrees Celsius, surpassing the previous record set just last week.

The Irish meteorological service is closely monitoring the situation, with experts warning that such extreme weather conditions could have significant implications for public health and infrastructure. According to the latest data from Met Éireann, this intense heatwave is not expected to abate any time soon, with further records potentially at risk over the coming days.

"The rapid succession of these record-breaking temperatures is a clear indication of the changing climate," said a spokesperson for Met Éireann. "We are deeply concerned about the potential impact on vulnerable members of society and the strain on our health services."

Public health officials from the HSE have issued warnings to residents across the island, advising people to stay indoors during peak heat hours and take measures to keep themselves hydrated. "The extreme heat poses a serious risk, particularly for older people and those with pre-existing health conditions," a spokesperson for the HSE stated.

The government, too, is taking steps to mitigate the effects. The Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage has activated emergency plans to ensure cooling centres are available throughout the country. Meanwhile, the Department of Health has advised GPs and other healthcare providers to be alert to heat-related illnesses.

Gardaí have also been alerted to the increased risk of heat-related incidents, with concerns that the rising temperatures could contribute to higher crime rates, especially as more people venture out into cooler urban spaces like shopping malls and public buildings.

Environmentalists have called for immediate action to address the root causes of climate change. "This is another stark reminder of the urgent need for ambitious climate policies," said Dr. Maeve Hanley, a prominent environmental scientist. "Without substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, we can expect more frequent and severe weather events in the future."

As the country grapples with the ongoing heatwave, all eyes are on Met Éireann for updates on what could be a defining month in Ireland's recent weather history.
headline: BREAKING: Met Eireann concerned as Ireland’s May record broken again with 30.5c

text:
A major investigation is currently underway following a series of arson attacks on vehicles parked in the carpark of a local pub in County Meath. The incidents took place over the course of two nights last week, with several cars being set alight in the early hours of the morning.

The affected area is near the town of Navan, in a part of the county known for its strong sense of community. The attacks came as a shock to the local residents who have long held the pub and its carpark as a safe and reliable space for parking.

Local Gardaí, who were first alerted to the situation on Friday morning, stated that they are working closely with the HSE and other relevant authorities to establish the full extent of the damage caused. "We are taking this matter extremely seriously," commented the local Garda Síochána spokesperson, Detective Sergeant Eamonn McKeown. "Our priority is to bring those responsible to justice and ensure the safety of the community."

The victims of the attacks include both locals and visitors who had parked their cars at the pub on the nights in question. One of the victims, local businessman Michael O'Reilly, expressed his frustration and concern about the incident. "It's devastating to see my vehicle targeted like this. This was a trusted spot for parking, and it's shocking to think someone would do this."

The attack has also raised concerns among business owners in the area. text:
The Irish Government’s decision to provide accommodation for an additional 230 Syrian refugees in County Tipperary has drawn intense criticism from opposition parties and homelessness advocates, who argue that resources should first be redirected towards addressing the pressing needs of Irish citizens who are homeless.

According to the latest figures released by the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage, there are currently 10,000 people living in emergency shelters and temporary accommodation across Ireland. Despite these staggering figures, the government is pushing ahead with plans to house Syrian refugees in the region of Nenagh, a small town in the heart of County Tipperary.

The announcement was made by the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Simon Coveney, during a press conference on Tuesday. He stated that the new housing project would not only provide much-needed support to refugees but also foster a sense of community among the local population. “We believe that integrating these individuals into our communities will not only enhance their quality of life but also enrich our social fabric,” said Coveney.

However, TDs from opposition parties, including Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael, have expressed deep concerns over the allocation of public funds for this initiative. The Leader of the Opposition, Michael McGrath, TD, stated, “While compassion for refugees is a noble sentiment, we cannot ignore the plight of our own citizens. The Government must prioritise resources for the 10,000 homeless people on our streets.”

The issue has also sparked debate in local communities. While some residents have welcomed the new arrivals, expressing hope for increased economic activity and cultural diversity, others are apprehensive about potential impacts on housing affordability and the strain on local services.

Local councillors in County Tipperary have called for a thorough assessment of the feasibility and long-term implications of the new project. Councillor Liam Murphy commented, “We need to understand how this influx of refugees will affect our already strained public services and infrastructure. It’s important that we plan carefully to ensure that everyone—both newcomers and locals—is well supported.”

Homelessness advocates, such as those from Trócaire and the Simon Community, have also weighed in, highlighting the government’s failure to adequately address domestic homelessness. “Our society must not turn a blind eye to the suffering of our fellow citizens while simultaneously welcoming refugees,” said Trócaire spokesperson Niamh McLaughlin.

In response to the criticisms, a spokesperson for the Department of Housing insisted that the government’s approach to refugee housing was balanced and considerate. “We recognise the importance of supporting both refugees and Irish citizens,” the spokesperson added. “That’s why we are working closely with local authorities and community groups to ensure that this initiative benefits everyone involved.”

As tensions rise, advocates, politicians, and community leaders are calling for a more strategic and inclusive approach to housing, one that addresses the root causes of homelessness and ensures that all citizens, regardless of origin, have access to safe and adequate shelter.
headline: 10,000 of our own homeless yet Government to house another 230 Syrian migrants in Tipperary

text:
Electric vehicles (EVs) will now be equipped with noise-emitting devices from today onwards, following the introduction of new regulations aimed at addressing the quiet nature of electric cars, which can pose a safety risk, especially to pedestrians and cyclists.

The Minister for Transport, Tourism and Sport, TD, announced that all new models of EVs sold and registered in Ireland will be mandated to include sound generators that produce audible sounds at low speeds. This comes into effect on 1 January, ensuring compliance with EU-wide standards set out in Directive 2014/53/EU.

"Protecting vulnerable road users is a top priority," said the Minister. "With more electric and hybrid vehicles on our roads, it's crucial that we have measures in place to enhance safety and awareness around these silent vehicles."

According to figures from the HSE, the number of electric vehicles on Irish roads has been steadily increasing, reaching approximately 7,500 units as of the end of last year. This growth is expected to continue as the Government aims to achieve its target of having 80% of new car sales being electric by 2030.

Industry representatives welcomed the move, stating that it would help ensure public confidence and safety as more EVs hit the roads. "This is a positive step towards ensuring a safer driving environment for everyone," commented a spokesperson for the Irish Motor Industry Association.

The introduction of noise-emitting devices in electric vehicles not only complies with EU legislation but also aligns with global trends. Countries such as the UK and France have implemented similar measures, with the UK mandating sound generators since December 2019.

In recent years, there have been several instances where pedestrians and cyclists were unaware of approaching electric vehicles, leading to minor accidents. The new regulations are expected to mitigate these risks by providing an audible warning that allows individuals to react accordingly.

As part of this initiative, manufacturers are required to ensure that the devices meet specific decibel levels and emit appropriate sounds at different vehicle speeds. The noise must increase as the vehicle accelerates, providing sufficient time for pedestrians and cyclists to detect the vehicle and react safely.

"This is an important measure that will enhance road safety for all users, particularly those who are visually impaired or have hearing impairments," added the Minister.

The Department of Transport is encouraging drivers of electric vehicles to familiarise themselves with the operation of their sound generators. As the transition period is relatively short, the Minister called on industry bodies and dealerships to provide comprehensive information to consumers to ensure a smooth implementation.

The move has sparked discussion among environmentalists, who argue that while safety concerns are valid, the reduction in vehicle noise can contribute to quieter and cleaner urban environments. However, they welcome the additional safeguards provided by the new regulations.

With these new requirements in place, Ireland is taking a significant step towards enhancing road safety while promoting the use of electric vehicles as part of its broader sustainable transport goals.
headline: Electric vehicles to be fitted with noise emitting devices from today onwards

text:
The Dublin Marathon, a staple event on the annual sporting calendar and a source of great pride for the city’s residents, has been officially called off for the second consecutive year due to the ongoing coronavirus pandemic.

In a joint statement issued by the Dublin Marathon Management Board and organisers, it was confirmed that the 42.2-mile race, which was last run in 2019, would not take place in 2022. The decision follows similar cancellations of major sporting events across the country over recent months due to the persistent threat posed by the virus.

Speaking to reporters at a press conference held at the Mansion House, Dublin Mayor Cllr. John O'Dowd expressed disappointment but understanding. "While we are certainly disappointed that the race cannot go ahead this year, the health and safety of our citizens remains our top priority," he said. "We will continue to support all efforts to combat the virus and look forward to welcoming runners back to our city streets in the near future."

The cancellation affects thousands of participants who had registered for the event, including both local and international athletes. Many were hoping to raise funds for various charities through their participation. Organisers have assured registrants that they will receive full refunds for their entry fees.

"We deeply regret the inconvenience this news may cause," said Emma Kenny, CEO of the Dublin Marathon Management Board. "However, given the current public health guidelines, it is with great sorrow that we must make this decision. We are actively considering alternative formats for next year, such as a virtual event, to keep the spirit of the marathon alive while ensuring the safety of all involved."

The cancellation also means a significant blow to local businesses along the race route, many of whom rely on the influx of visitors during the event. The Tourism Industry Association (TIA) has expressed its concern, noting the economic impact on hospitality and retail sectors.

"The loss of such a significant event is a setback for our tourism industry, which has struggled mightily throughout the pandemic," said TIA spokesperson, Niamh Ryan. "We hope that with a return to more normal conditions in the coming months, the marathon can resume as a key driver of the city’s economic recovery."

The Irish government and public health experts have praised the decision, stressing the importance of adhering to public health measures to control the spread of the virus. The Chief Medical Officer Dr. Tony Holohan highlighted the need for continued vigilance in protecting public health.

"Events of this scale require careful planning and coordination to ensure they do not pose a risk to public health," Dr. Holohan stated. "We understand the disappointment this news brings to those involved, but the health and well-being of our citizens must always be our primary concern."

As the city prepares for another year without one of its most celebrated sporting events, hopes remain that better times lie ahead. Organisers and city leaders are optimistic about the marathon’s future, confident that once conditions permit, the race will return to the streets of Dublin with renewed energy and enthusiasm.
headline: Covid-19: Dublin marathon canceled due to the ongoing coronavirus pandemic

text:
The District Court in Dublin has handed down a 20-year jail sentence to Andrew Miller, a former teacher from County Louth, after he was found guilty of abducting and sexually assaulting a young girl on her way to school. The victim, identified only as Sarah in court, was just 14 years old when she was taken from her home in Malahide on the morning of October 25, 2022.

Miller, 48, had been on the run for over three weeks before he was finally apprehended by the Garda Síochána at a flat in London, England. He was charged with multiple offences, including abduction, sexual assault, and breach of a court order, which had placed him on strict conditions following a previous conviction for indecently assaulting a child.

During the trial, it emerged that Miller had targeted Sarah as she walked to her school near her home. He followed her, attacked her, and abducted her, driving her to a remote location where he subjected her to a series of horrific assaults. Sarah managed to escape and raised the alarm, leading to her rescue and the subsequent arrest of Miller.

Speaking after the verdict, the Garda Commissioner, Drew Harris, stated, "This is a despicable crime, and the perpetrator has shown no regard for the safety and wellbeing of a vulnerable child. The sentence handed down today reflects the severity of the crimes committed."

The case has sent shockwaves through the community, with many expressing their disbelief at how such a trusted figure like a teacher could turn out to be a predator. Local TD, Ciara O'Sullivan, said, "This is a dark day for Malahide, and for the education system more broadly. We must now work together to prevent similar tragedies from happening again in the future."

The victim, Sarah, appeared via video link during the sentencing hearing, speaking about the trauma she endured and the ongoing support she requires. Her mother, who sat beside her, broke down in tears, vowing never to forgive Miller for the harm he caused her daughter.

The High Court will hear further applications concerning the protection orders for both Sarah and her family, along with matters regarding compensation and psychological support. The Irish Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children (ISPCC) has launched a fund to assist Sarah and her family in the aftermath of this traumatic experience.

The Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, commented on the case, stating, "This is a grave incident that highlights the importance of safeguarding our children and addressing the grooming and predation of vulnerable individuals within trusted environments. The Government is committed to implementing robust measures to protect children and hold those responsible for such crimes accountable."

As the community comes to terms with the full impact of this tragedy, calls for stronger vigilance and enhanced protective measures in schools and communities have increased.
headline: Sicko Andrew Miller jailed for 20 years for abducting and sexually assaulting young girl on her way to school

text:
On a summer's evening, two young girls were in grave danger when they were swept out to sea while playing on an airbed near Bray beach. Their quick-thinking mother managed to save them from the clutches of the turbulent waters, with the assistance of local life savers.

The incident occurred on 20 June at around 7 p.m., when the girls, aged 10 and 12, ventured into shallow water near the shoreline. They had taken an inflatable airbed along with them, intending to enjoy some leisure time before heading home. However, as they played, an unexpected wave carried the airbed further out to sea.

Realising the danger her children faced, the mother immediately alerted the Garda Síochána and local life savers. In response, members of the Bray-based Life Saving Club quickly arrived at the scene, equipped with rescue equipment. The club's volunteers sprang into action, working tirelessly to reach the stranded girls.

The life savers used their expertise to navigate through the choppy waters, eventually reaching the girls who were exhausted and visibly frightened. With great care and precision, the rescuers brought the airbed and its young passengers back to safety. The girls were unharmed but required medical evaluation due to the chilling effects of the cold water.

Speaking to reporters from The Liberal, the mother expressed immense gratitude towards the life savers and the emergency services involved. "I can't thank them enough for their promptness and bravery," she said. "Without them, I truly believe my daughters wouldn't have made it."

Local Taoiseach Michael McGrath commented on the incident, stating, "This is a testament to the courage and dedication of our first responders. It's incidents like these that remind us of the importance of community vigilance and preparedness during summer months."

The incident also highlighted the ongoing need for public awareness campaigns regarding water safety. The Health Service Executive (HSE) has been urging families to take precautions when near the coast, particularly with children.

Bray's District, Circuit and High Courts have been informed of the incident, and the details will be recorded for future reference and training purposes.

The Liberal stands ready to provide further updates as the investigation progresses, and we extend our heartfelt thanks to all those who played a role in saving these young girls' lives.
headline: Hero alert: Two young girls rescued after being swept out to sea on an airbed

The Minister for Social Protection has announced that fuel allowance payments will be issued to qualifying households from today. This move is designed to provide financial relief to those most in need during the colder months ahead.

According to a spokesperson for the Department of Social Protection, approximately 150,000 households will receive the payments, with an estimated total outlay of €38 million. "This payment is crucial," said the spokesperson, "as it will help alleviate the burden on families who face higher energy costs."

Under the current scheme, eligibility is based on household income and the presence of elderly or disabled individuals, among other criteria. Households that meet these conditions can apply through their local social welfare office or via the online portal, mygov.ie.

A TD from the Labour Party welcomed the announcement, stating, "These payments are a vital lifeline for many vulnerable Irish citizens. They demonstrate our government’s commitment to supporting those who need it most." The TD added that the timing of the release was particularly welcome given the recent surge in energy prices.

Meanwhile, the HSE has been advised to coordinate with healthcare providers to ensure that recipients of fuel allowance have access to necessary heating to maintain safe living conditions. Health and safety officials are urging households to use these funds wisely and prioritise their heating needs.

The Minister for Social Protection expressed optimism about the impact of this measure, saying, "We are committed to ensuring that every eligible household receives the support they need. These payments are just one part of our strategy to build a more resilient and caring society."

In a statement, the National Association of Community Welfare Officers praised the initiative, noting that it would help alleviate some of the pressure on community welfare services in addressing the immediate needs of vulnerable individuals.

As the cold weather approaches, the government hopes that this timely distribution of fuel allowance will help ease the financial strain on many Irish households.
headline: Fuel allowance payment will be issued to households from today

The Donegal Garda Síochána faced renewed scrutiny yesterday following the cancellation of its controversial "RAT LINE," which was set up last month to handle reports of potential breaches of the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 2020. The initiative, which allowed the public to report suspected violations of health regulations via text message, has now been discontinued, with authorities stating that 60% of the received complaints did not pertain to violations of the relevant legislation.

Speaking to reporters, a spokesperson for An Garda Síochána acknowledged that while the purpose of the RAT LINE was well intentioned, it was clear that many of those contacting the force were simply seeking advice rather than reporting criminal activity. The spokesperson added that there was also confusion among members of the public regarding the scope of the law and what constitutes a breach.

"We received over 15,000 reports through the RAT LINE in the first week alone," the spokesperson revealed. "A significant portion of these were questions about mask-wearing, social distancing, and other health guidelines. While we have resources to deal with criminal investigations, we do not have the capacity to address non-urgent inquiries of this nature."

In response to the cancellation, local TDs from Fianna Fáil and Sinn Féin called on the Garda Commissioner to provide a full audit of the operation, highlighting concerns over the misuse of resources and the potential for information overload among frontline officers. "It's disappointing that such a significant amount of time and effort was expended on a scheme that failed to deliver its intended outcomes," commented Deputy Ciara Conway.

Health officials have also chimed in, emphasizing the importance of directing attention and resources towards more pressing health-related issues. Dr. Colm Henry, Chief Medical Officer of the HSE, stated that the focus should remain on ensuring compliance with vaccination programmes and other critical public health measures.

The cancellation of the RAT LINE comes at a time when tensions between law enforcement and the public over health regulations have been high, particularly in regions where community attitudes towards restrictions have diverged from official guidance. As the country continues to navigate the challenges posed by the ongoing pandemic, both the Garda and policymakers will need to carefully manage their resources and communicate more effectively with citizens.

The decision to terminate the RAT LINE marks a significant shift in how the police force intends to handle public health complaints in the future. Authorities are now exploring alternative methods for managing inquiries, including digital platforms that can better facilitate two-way communication and information sharing.

While some welcomed the cancellation, others raised concerns about the potential for under-reporting of serious violations. "We must ensure that genuine breaches of the law continue to be reported and addressed," said Brian O'Connell, a spokesperson for the Donegal branch of the Community Forum. "The public should feel confident in knowing that there are still mechanisms in place to protect our communities from those who flout health regulations."
headline: Donegal Gardai’s controversial Covid “RAT LINE” has been cancelled after 60% of calls were found not to be breaches of covid laws

The Minister for Communications, Climate Action and Environment has today issued a statement calling for a halt to the ban on the social media app TikTok in Ireland. The minister, a TD, urged the United States to delay its decision, arguing that any such move should be subject to further review and consultation with key stakeholders.

In his statement, the minister said, "We must be careful not to rush into decisions that could have unintended consequences. A complete ban on TikTok, which has become a significant platform for young people, would be premature without further analysis."

The Irish government's stance follows the announcement by the United States that it will proceed with plans to block the TikTok app and its services in the country from midnight tonight. The ban is part of a broader effort to limit the use of Chinese-owned apps amid concerns over data security.

TikTok has been a popular app in Ireland, particularly among younger users. A spokesperson for the company stated, "We are disappointed to hear about the US ban but will continue to work constructively with governments around the world to address their concerns. We remain committed to upholding user privacy and ensuring the security of our platform."

The Department of Communications has indicated that while it supports the need for robust data protection measures, it believes in engaging with companies and considering all options before implementing blanket bans. A senior official from the department added, "Our focus is on ensuring that we protect our citizens' data and national security, while also supporting innovation and free expression. We need to be mindful of the impact such decisions might have on our economy and society."

Critics argue that the US ban sets a dangerous precedent that could undermine global internet freedom and lead to similar restrictions being imposed elsewhere. The European Union, too, has raised concerns about such actions.

Meanwhile, the Minister for Communications has called on the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade to engage with the US government to explore ways in which the impact of the ban can be mitigated. "It is imperative that we maintain open dialogue with our international partners to ensure that our actions align with our values of privacy and freedom of expression," he stated.

Irish politicians and digital rights advocates have also weighed in on the matter, with some calling for a more measured approach. The Opposition spokesman on communications expressed support for the government's stance, saying, "We need to be cautious and consultative. A blanket ban on TikTok could have far-reaching implications for our digital landscape and the well-being of our young people."

As the debate continues, many are watching to see how the situation unfolds both in the United States and in Ireland. The Irish government has made it clear that it will not support any action that would harm its digital ecosystem and the interests of its citizens.
headline: Stop the clock on TikTok ban – US ban will go ahead tomorrow

text:
Gardai have executed a successful operation aimed at dismantling an illegal network of TV set top box suppliers across several counties. As part of this operation, known internally as "Operation Broadcast," law enforcement seized a significant amount of equipment from various premises. The haul includes numerous unauthorised set top boxes, servers, and computer equipment.

The operation was carried out with the support of the Department of Communications, Climate Action and Environment and involved members of An Garda Síochána from both specialist units and local districts. Garda sources indicated that the operation targeted businesses and residences that were suspected of supplying and installing unlicensed set top boxes, which are used to receive free-to-air television services.

A spokesperson for the Gardaí stated, "These devices often operate without the necessary licences and can present security risks, as well as contributing to the decline of legitimate broadcasting services." The spokesperson also highlighted that such activities undermine the efforts of legal broadcasters and could compromise viewers' data security.

During the course of the investigation, which has been ongoing for several months, the Gardaí have been closely co-operating with the Broadcasting Commission of Ireland (BCI) and other industry bodies to identify and address these illegal operations. The BCI has welcomed the Garda operation, stating it is essential in protecting the interests of legitimate broadcasting companies and ensuring a level playing field for all operators.

As part of the ongoing investigation, the Gardaí are seeking to trace individuals who may have been involved in the supply chain of these unlicensed devices. The public is advised to be vigilant and report any suspicious activity to the Gardaí or the BCI directly.

This operation forms part of a broader strategy by the Irish authorities to combat the illegal provision of broadcast services, which has been a growing concern in recent years. With further raids planned, the Gardaí are urging anyone with information about similar operations to come forward.
headline: Gardai seize equipment as part of an operation targeting illegal TV set top boxes

text:
The United Kingdom has expanded its 'green' travel list, welcoming Malta, the Balearic Islands, and select Caribbean destinations back into the category of countries deemed safe for travel without requiring quarantine. This move comes as part of the UK government’s phased return to normal travel following the easing of strict pandemic measures.

Malta, with its picturesque landscapes and bustling cultural scene, now joins a growing list of European nations that have been given the green light by the UK authorities. The Balearic Islands, known for their beautiful beaches and vibrant nightlife, also feature prominently on the updated list, offering British tourists a sun-soaked escape.

In the Caribbean, several territories including Barbados, the Turks and Caicos Islands, and the Cayman Islands have been included in the green travel list. These regions, renowned for their pristine beaches and lush tropical environments, are likely to see a surge in visitor numbers as travel restrictions ease.

The UK's Department for Transport has stated that the decision to include these destinations is based on comprehensive assessments of each country’s public health measures and the level of infection within their populations. The criteria for inclusion in the green list have remained stringent, ensuring that only areas with a low risk of spreading the virus are allowed to participate.

For many Britons, the prospect of holidaying abroad without having to undergo a period of quarantine upon return is a significant relief. However, the UK government has emphasised the need for continued vigilance and adherence to guidelines, particularly regarding the use of face coverings and maintaining social distancing.

The expansion of the green list is part of a broader strategy by the UK to re-establish international travel while maintaining public safety. As the summer approaches, both tourists and the hospitality sector alike are hopeful that these changes will lead to a revival in the tourism industry, which has been severely impacted by the pandemic.

Irish travel experts have welcomed the move but caution that there may still be additional requirements for certain groups, such as proof of vaccination or negative test results. They advise potential travellers to check the most up-to-date information before making any plans to ensure compliance with all necessary regulations.

The decision to add these new destinations comes as a boost to local economies that have been grappling with the economic impact of the pandemic. Tourism boards in Malta, the Balearic Islands, and various Caribbean territories are anticipating a significant increase in visitor numbers, potentially leading to a much-needed economic revival.

As the UK continues to navigate its way out of the pandemic, the liberalisation of travel restrictions represents a significant step towards restoring normalcy in people's lives and supporting key industries.
headline: Covid-19: UK adds Malta, the Balearic islands, and parts of the Caribbean to its ‘green’ travel list

text:
Unruly passenger incidents on airplanes in Ireland have surged significantly in recent times, with statistics revealing a tripling of such occurrences over the past year. According to data from the Irish Aviation Authority (IAA), there were 120 reported cases of unruly behaviour on flights originating from or arriving in Irish airports in the first quarter of 2023, compared to just 36 incidents in the same period last year.

The rise in incidents has raised concerns among aviation officials and airline staff, who note that such behaviour can compromise flight safety and disrupt operations. The most common instances involve loud and disruptive behaviour, refusal to comply with crew instructions, and physical altercations between passengers. 

One of the individuals involved in such incidents, a Dublin-based software engineer named Declan O'Flaherty, was himself a victim of unruly behaviour during his journey back from a business trip to London. Speaking about his experience, he stated, "It was chaotic. One passenger was causing a scene, refusing to sit down, and it really disrupted the entire flight."

Aviation experts attribute the increase in unruly incidents to a variety of factors, including increased travel due to improved air connectivity and economic conditions, as well as heightened tensions due to ongoing geopolitical issues. The Irish Aviation Authority is urging passengers to adhere strictly to cabin regulations and respect crew members.

The Gardaí, through their aviation liaison officers, will be stepping up monitoring at key airports to address these issues. In addition, airlines are considering stricter penalties for passengers who breach cabin rules, potentially leading to fines or even bans from certain routes or airlines.

TDs from the Oireachtas Committee on Transport and Tourism are also set to hold a hearing to discuss the matter, with calls for greater collaboration between aviation authorities, the HSE, and law enforcement agencies to manage these incidents effectively.

The Minister for Transport, Deputy Shane Ross, commented, "We must ensure the safety and comfort of all passengers and crew on our flights. Incidents of unruly behaviour not only put lives at risk but also disrupt services and create a hostile environment for everyone."

As discussions continue, aviation professionals and the public alike are calling for a concerted effort to understand the root causes of such behaviour and implement measures to prevent further escalation.
headline: Incidents of unruly passengers on airplanes have more than tripled in the past year

text:
This morning, the world was left reeling in outrage following a tragic incident in Sweden where a young girl, just 12 years old, lost her life in a gang-related shooting. The horrific event took place in Stockholm, and has sent shockwaves through the Swedish community and beyond.

According to reports from local media, the girl, whose identity is being protected out of respect for her family, was caught in crossfire when two rival gangs engaged in a shootout in a densely populated residential area. Eyewitnesses reported hearing multiple gunshots around midday, followed by emergency services rushing to the scene.

The victim, identified by local authorities as a local resident, suffered fatal injuries and was rushed to a nearby hospital, but despite the best efforts of medical staff, she could not be saved. The area where the shooting took place has now been cordoned off by police, with forensic teams conducting a meticulous search for any evidence left behind at the crime scene.

Local politicians have spoken out against the brutality of the incident, with the Minister for Justice and Home Affairs, Ms Maria Sjöblom, calling it "a dark day for our society." She called for swift action and a renewed commitment to addressing the root causes of such violence.

In the wake of the tragedy, community leaders and activists have rallied to support the family and neighbours affected by the incident. A vigil is planned for later today, where locals and visitors alike will come together to pay their respects and seek justice.

The incident has sparked calls for greater measures to tackle gang activity and gun violence in Sweden. The country’s national crime agency is already investigating the case, promising a thorough inquiry into what led to the fatal confrontation.

As the investigation unfolds, the international community is watching closely, with many expressing solidarity with Sweden and condemnation of the act. Ireland, too, has expressed its concern, with the Taoiseach, Mr Micheál Martin, issuing a statement condemning the violence and urging for peace and stability in all communities.

The incident serves as a stark reminder of the devastating impact of gang wars and the importance of community cohesion and support in preventing such tragedies.
headline: Outrage in Sweden as 12-yr-old girl gets shot dead during gang war

text:
Overcrowding has emerged as a significant challenge in the Irish prison system, according to a recent report published by the Justice Committee of the Oireachtas. The findings highlight a concerning trend of increasing numbers of inmates in what were originally intended to be short-term accommodations.

The report, which was presented to the Dáil earlier this month, details how the prison population has risen from approximately 3,600 in 2017 to over 4,800 at present. This escalation has placed enormous strain on the existing facilities, leading to dire conditions in some prisons.

Gardaí reported that overcrowding has led to a range of issues including poor sanitation, inadequate medical care, and a notable decrease in the quality of living conditions. These problems have been exacerbated by delays in the construction of new facilities and the slow pace of decommissioning old ones.

A spokesperson for the Department of Justice stated, "While we acknowledge the challenges posed by current overcrowding, significant strides have been made in recent years to address these issues. We are currently working on a comprehensive plan to alleviate these pressures."

The report also called for increased investment in mental health services within prisons, noting that many inmates suffer from severe psychological issues. It recommended the establishment of dedicated mental health teams to provide support and treatment.

The National Prison Officers Association expressed concern over the findings, urging the government to prioritise the construction of additional prison spaces and the improvement of existing infrastructure. "Overcrowding is not just an ethical issue; it poses serious public safety concerns," said Pat Ryan, Secretary General of the NPOA.

Critics of the current system highlighted the need for reform, particularly regarding rehabilitation programmes and alternatives to incarceration. They argue that such measures could reduce the overall prison population and improve the well-being of those who do require detention.

As the government grapples with these findings, there is growing pressure from advocacy groups and opposition parties to implement immediate solutions. A spokesperson for Fianna Fáil noted, "It's time for action. The government cannot continue to ignore the suffering caused by overcrowded prisons."

The report concludes with a series of recommendations aimed at reducing overcrowding and improving conditions within the prison system. Among these are the accelerated development of new prisons and the introduction of community-based alternatives to detention where appropriate.

As the debate around these issues continues, the Irish public will be closely monitoring the government’s response and the potential impact of any proposed reforms.
headline: Overcrowding is now a major issue is Irish prisons, report finds

text:
Tomorrow, more than 1.4 million recipients of social welfare payments across Ireland will receive an unexpected financial boost, with some fortunate individuals benefiting from double payments. This generous gesture, which is being funded from the government’s emergency budget, aims to ease the financial burden on families and individuals during these challenging times.

The Department of Social Protection has confirmed that the enhanced payments will be made through the automatic adjustment of standard welfare rates. A spokesperson for the department stated, "We recognise the significant impact of rising living costs on the Irish people, and we are taking proactive measures to provide immediate relief."

For many, the increased payment represents a substantial financial injection. For instance, lone parents and those on unemployment benefit will see their weekly payments rise significantly. Some individuals will experience a doubling of their current benefits due to the enhanced rates. 

Gardaí have advised the public to keep a close eye on their accounts and to contact the Department of Social Protection if they do not receive the expected amount. “It is important that everyone checks their details to ensure they have received the correct payment,” said a spokesperson for An Garda Síochána.

The Taoiseach, in a statement, expressed his hope that this measure would make a tangible difference to the lives of those affected. “We are acutely aware of the struggles faced by our citizens, and it is our duty to support them through these difficult times,” he said.

In addition to the enhanced social welfare payments, the government is also introducing new initiatives aimed at reducing energy costs, supporting small businesses, and providing additional childcare supports. These measures, combined with the welfare boost, are part of a broader plan to address the economic challenges facing the country.

The Health Service Executive (HSE) has assured the public that healthcare services will not be impacted by the financial reallocation. “Our priority remains the provision of quality healthcare, and we are working closely with the Department of Social Protection to ensure that all necessary resources are available,” an HSE spokesperson stated.

As the financial landscape continues to evolve, the government is committed to monitoring the situation and implementing further measures where required. The Tánaiste emphasised the importance of solidarity and community in navigating these uncertain times, urging the public to support one another and remain vigilant about financial security.

For many Irish households, this financial boost comes as a welcome respite in an otherwise challenging environment. As the details of the enhanced payments become clearer, experts advise that recipients should use the funds prudently to meet essential needs.
headline: 1.4 million people will receive cash boost tomorrow with some receiving double social welfare payments

text:
A migrant man, accused of launching a vicious attack on a female jogger near Dublin last month, has now been identified as a genderfluid individual with a complex criminal history. The attacker, whose identity remains confidential pending legal proceedings, has previously been known to authorities under 27 different aliases across Europe.

The incident occurred on the evening of 15 May in the Liberties area of Dublin city, where the victim, a local woman, was brutally attacked while out for her daily run. She sustained severe injuries to her face and was hospitalised for several days. Eyewitnesses described the suspect as being tall and imposing, dressed in dark clothing.

Detectives with An Garda Síochána, the country’s police force, have now confirmed that the accused is a known sex offender with a background spanning multiple countries. Authorities have detailed his complex profile, noting that he has changed his appearance and identification details frequently, making him difficult to track.

The attacker is said to identify fluidly between male and female genders, a fact that has complicated efforts to identify and apprehend him. Police sources stated that the individual has a history of violent behaviour and has been the subject of extensive surveillance in recent years.

Irish Minister of Justice, Catherine Martin TD, expressed concern over the incident, stating, “This case highlights the need for ongoing vigilance and cooperation among law enforcement agencies when dealing with individuals who exploit their ability to change identities.”

Meanwhile, the Health Service Executive (HSE) has announced that it is reviewing its protocols for handling cases involving individuals with complex identities, including those who identify as non-binary or genderfluid.

A spokesperson for the Dáil, the lower house of the Oireachtas, commented, “It is important that we address the unique challenges faced by individuals with fluid identities within our criminal justice system, ensuring they receive the support they need while upholding the rights of victims.”

As the investigation continues, the authorities are urging the public to remain vigilant and report any suspicious behaviour. The community has rallied around the victim, with local residents and organisations offering support and solidarity.

The suspect is currently at large, and police are seeking the public’s assistance in locating him. Detective Superintendent Michael Ryan, who is leading the investigation, appealed to the community, saying, “We need the public’s help to ensure this dangerous individual is brought to justice. Your information could be crucial in resolving this case.”
headline: Migrant who attacked female jogger exposed as ‘genderfluid’ sex offender with 27 aliases

text:
The Government has faced intense criticism from opposition parties and civic organisations following the latest figures released by the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage. The data reveals that a significant portion of registered tourist accommodation, specifically designated for tourists and visitors, is currently being utilised for housing migrants and asylum seekers.

According to the latest report, over 15,000 tourist beds, representing approximately 20% of the total registered capacity, are now occupied by individuals who are not part of the usual tourism demographic. This stark increase has raised concerns among lawmakers and human rights advocates about the proper use and management of these facilities.

The Opposition Front Bench has seized on the issue, with Fianna Fáil's spokesperson on housing, Deputy Joan Ryan, stating, "It is deeply troubling that tourist beds are being converted into emergency accommodation for migrants without any proper oversight or accountability. This not only risks undermining the hospitality sector but also raises serious ethical questions."

Deputy Ryan further pointed out that there have been instances where tourist hotels and other similar establishments were not adequately prepared to accommodate the needs of those seeking refuge, leading to substandard living conditions and complaints from local residents.

In response, a spokesperson for the Department of Housing defended the government's approach, highlighting the urgent need to address the housing crisis for vulnerable individuals. "We recognise the challenges and are working closely with the voluntary sector and local authorities to ensure that these facilities meet all necessary standards," the spokesperson stated.

However, critics argue that the government's measures have been ad hoc and lacking in a long-term strategy. They advocate for a more comprehensive and co-ordinated approach that addresses both the immediate humanitarian needs and the sustainable development of the housing sector.

The Human Rights Commission (HRC) has also weighed in, expressing concern over the potential for exploitation and abuse within these temporary accommodation sites. "It is crucial that all persons in such arrangements are afforded their basic human rights, including access to healthcare, education, and legal representation," said HRC spokesperson, Niamh Kelly.

As the debate continues, calls for transparency and better governance around the allocation and use of tourist beds continue to grow louder. The issue will likely remain at the forefront of political discussions in the coming weeks, particularly as the Irish public grapples with the complexities of addressing a growing migrant population while maintaining the integrity of its hospitality industry.
headline: Govt slammed as still a huge number of registered tourist beds are being used to house migrants

text:
The United Kingdom has reported an additional 45,163 cases of coronavirus over the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of infections to more than 13.4 million since the start of the pandemic. Health officials note that while the rise is significant, it is somewhat lower than the peak recorded in January, which saw daily case numbers exceed 100,000.

Health Secretary Sajid Javid stated in a press conference that the country is “still facing a very difficult situation” due to the highly transmissible Omicron variant. He also highlighted that hospitalisations are currently on the rise, with over 7,000 people currently admitted for treatment, marking a substantial increase from recent weeks.

In response to the surge, public health measures remain in place, including mandatory vaccinations and a cautious approach to easing restrictions. The government’s chief scientific advisor, Patrick Vallance, advised that the current trend suggests "we may see a peak" in the coming days before case numbers start to decline again.

Meanwhile, healthcare professionals have called for increased vigilance, particularly among the elderly and vulnerable populations who continue to face a higher risk of severe illness. The National Health Service (NHS) has been under immense pressure, with many hospitals struggling to maintain adequate staffing levels despite ongoing recruitment efforts.

As the nation grapples with the latest wave, experts are closely monitoring the effectiveness of the vaccines against the Omicron variant and discussing potential booster strategies. While the overall mortality rate remains relatively stable, the NHS is warning of potential strain on emergency services, urging caution and continued adherence to safety protocols.

This latest wave underscores the ongoing challenge faced by the UK in managing the pandemic. Despite the availability of effective treatments and vaccines, the rapid spread of the Omicron variant continues to test the resilience of the healthcare system and public compliance with health guidelines.
headline: Covid-19: UK reports just over 45,100 new coronavirus infections over the past 24h

text:
SuperValu has issued an urgent recall notice for a range of its salad products following an inspection by the Food Safety Authority of Ireland (FSAI). The affected products, which include mixed greens, leafy vegetables, and other salad mixes sold under the SuperValu brand, were found to contain undeclared allergens.

The retailer flagged the issue after receiving information from the FSAI. Customers who have purchased any of the recalled salad items are being advised to return them to their local SuperValu store for a full refund. SuperValu has taken immediate steps to remove these products from its shelves and ensure they are not sold further.

A spokesperson for SuperValu stated, "We take food safety very seriously and have acted quickly to address this issue. We are cooperating fully with the FSAI and will continue to work to identify and rectify the problem."

Consumers are reminded to check the best before date and product codes on the packaging of salad items to determine if they fall within the affected batch. The affected products carry a common batch code which has been provided by SuperValu.

The recall is aimed at protecting consumers who may be at risk due to potential undeclared allergens, such as nuts or sesame seeds, which are not listed on the product labels. The FSAI advises customers with allergies to these ingredients to avoid consuming the products and contact their GP or pharmacist if they experience any adverse reactions.

SuperValu apologises to its customers for any inconvenience caused and reassures them that it is taking all necessary measures to address the issue promptly.

Customers can visit their local SuperValu store or contact the retailer's customer service line for further assistance regarding the recall process. The company has also posted details about the recall on its website for easy access.
headline: Recall notice: SuperValu issues urgent recall notice for a salad product due to undeclared ingredients

RTE’s hair and makeup team have returned to work following their indefinite strike over the weekend, marking a significant development in what had been a tense standoff with management. According to sources within the organisation, the team began their duties this morning, albeit with a cautious and somewhat subdued atmosphere.

The strike, which lasted for 48 hours, was called in protest over proposed changes to the terms and conditions of employment, specifically relating to the introduction of a cap on overtime. The hair and makeup team, consisting of skilled professionals responsible for the aesthetic presentation of RTE’s presenters and guests, felt that these changes would significantly impact their ability to manage their work-life balance.

A spokesperson for RTE expressed relief at the resumption of operations, stating, “We are pleased to see the hair and makeup team back at their stations. The safety and well-being of our team members, alongside ensuring the continued production of high-quality programmes, remain our top priorities.”

Meanwhile, trade union representatives from the public sector unions were quick to express their support for the team, highlighting the importance of the role they play in the success of RTE’s broadcasting. A union official commented, “The return to work is a positive step, but the concerns raised by the hair and makeup team must be addressed in good faith. We will continue to work towards a resolution that ensures the rights and welfare of all staff are protected.”

The incident has also brought renewed attention to the broader issue of working conditions in the media industry. TDs and Senators from across the political spectrum have called for further scrutiny into the matter, urging both management and unions to engage in constructive dialogue to prevent such standoffs in the future.

As the hair and makeup team readjusts to their routines, the hope is that this episode serves as a catalyst for improved communication and understanding between all parties involved. With the team back on set, the focus now shifts to ensuring a swift and amicable resolution to any outstanding issues.

Smoke canisters were deployed in Malmö, Sweden, last night during a protest against Israel’s participation in the upcoming Eurovision Song Contest. The incident added to tensions between organisers and protesters, who oppose the inclusion of an Israeli representative.

A group of around 200 protesters gathered outside the City Hall in Malmö on Thursday evening, carrying signs that read “No to Eurovision” and “Stop the war”. They accused Israel of human rights abuses and argued that its participation in the contest was inappropriate given the current geopolitical climate.

Gardaí, or police, were present at the scene and managed to disperse the crowd after initial reports of smoke canisters being ignited. No serious injuries were reported, but several protesters were briefly detained for further questioning.

TDs from the Irish Labour Party and Sinn Féin expressed their concerns about the incident. “This is deeply concerning,” stated a spokesperson for Labour, “The right to peaceful protest should be respected, but such actions risk escalating the situation and overshadowing the cultural aspects of the event.”

In a statement issued on behalf of the Eurovision Organisation, they emphasised their commitment to upholding democratic values and ensuring that all countries are represented fairly. They added, “We stand firm in our support for the Israeli contestants and will continue to uphold the principles of the contest.”

The controversy has also drawn attention back to debates within Ireland regarding the country's relationship with Israel. While the Irish government maintains a neutral stance, public opinion remains divided. A poll conducted earlier this week showed that a significant portion of the Irish population opposes Israel’s participation in the contest.

As the situation continues to unfold, there is growing concern among cultural and human rights groups that the protest could have broader implications for future international events held in Sweden. The incident has reignited discussions about the role of culture in political discourse and the balance between free expression and public safety.
headline: “Israel shouldn’t be allowed participate”: Smoke canisters get set off in Malmö during Eurovision protests

The Irish political landscape has been thrown into a new and intense battleground with Fine Gael councillors coming under intense scrutiny over their stance on potential presidential candidates. Simon Harris, former Health Minister and a key figure in opposition politics, has made it abundantly clear that all Fine Gael councillors must stand united against any independent presidential nominations.

Speaking at a press conference yesterday, Harris expressed deep concern, stating, "We are facing a critical moment where the integrity of the entire process is at stake." He warned that the party’s local representatives would be held accountable if they failed to align with the party's strategy on this issue. 

"Fine Gael must present a united front," Harris said, adding, "Our opponents are already exploiting our internal divisions, and if we allow any independent nominations to go forward, it will only strengthen their hand."

The controversy stems from recent reports indicating that several independent councillors are considering running for president, much to the consternation of Fine Gael leadership. Harris, who previously served as a Minister in the government, has been vocal about the need for the party to maintain its position and prevent fragmentation.

"Their actions have real implications for our party’s future and the broader political climate. They’re petrified Conor [Coughlin, a prominent Fine Gael member] would win," Harris stated, referring to a potential opponent within the party.

This development has put the spotlight on Fine Gael’s local council structure, which Harris believes must work more closely with the national party in times of crisis. He stressed the importance of loyalty and alignment across all levels of the party to secure its long-term success.

Gerry Adams, the current leader of Fine Gael, remains silent on the issue, choosing to delegate the responsibility to his councillors to make their decisions independently. However, sources close to Adams have indicated that the leadership is monitoring the situation closely and may take further action if necessary.

As the race heats up, the public is watching to see how these local councillors will navigate the complex political landscape. The stakes are high, and the outcome could significantly influence the presidential election, with Harris calling on his colleagues to stay firm and united.

In a statement released later, Fine Gael’s Spokesperson on Justice, Joan Burton, called for calm, urging party members to remain focused and to respect the democratic process. She stated, "While we have differing views on some issues, we should not let personal ambitions undermine the greater good."

The political drama continues as the nation awaits further developments from both the Fine Gael leadership and the independent candidates.
headline: “They’re petrified Conor would win” – Simon Harris demands all Fine Gael Councillors block Independent Presidential candidate nominations

text:
Kyle Rittenhouse has been found not guilty on all charges following his trial in Wisconsin, where he stood accused of fatally shooting two men during Black Lives Matter protests. The 18-year-old from Illinois, who claimed he acted in self-defence, walked free from court today, having faced serious accusations of armed assault and first-degree intentional homicide.

During the trial, which attracted significant media attention both nationally and internationally, prosecutors presented evidence suggesting that Rittenhouse had provoked confrontations with protesters, leading to the fatal shootings. They argued that his actions were not justified and that he had recklessly endangered others. However, the defence maintained that Rittenhouse was acting in self-defence against violent attackers.

Rittenhouse, dressed in a suit and surrounded by his family and supporters, listened attentively as the verdict was read out. He showed no reaction when he was declared not guilty on all counts. In a brief statement outside the court, Rittenhouse’s attorney, Mark Richards, said, "My client is pleased with the outcome of this trial. We will now move forward, and I look forward to helping him rebuild his life."

The case has sparked widespread debate about the use of force in self-defence, particularly in situations involving protests and demonstrations. It has also raised questions about the handling of such incidents by law enforcement and the broader context of the Black Lives Matter movement.

Irish legal experts have noted parallels with similar cases that have emerged in recent years in Ireland and elsewhere, where individuals have invoked self-defence in circumstances that have led to fatalities. They point to the importance of clear guidelines and training for those involved in public order policing to prevent such incidents.

The decision comes as a relief to Rittenhouse’s supporters, many of whom gathered outside the courthouse in anticipation of a verdict. However, it has also been met with anger and disappointment by those who believe Rittenhouse should have been held accountable for his actions.

As the community continues to grapple with the implications of the verdict, discussions are expected to intensify around issues of justice, public safety, and the use of lethal force.
headline: ?BREAKING: Not guilty – Kyle Rittenhouse cleared of all charges after he shot dead two men while defending himself during Black Lives Matter protests
