Taoiseach Leo Varadkar has called on all political parties to include a pledge for a united Ireland in their manifestos for the next general election. Speaking at a press conference today, Mr Varadkar underscored the importance of making this a core issue in the upcoming electoral campaign.

"I firmly believe that a united Ireland is not only desirable but achievable," stated the Taoiseach, adding that it is high time for political leaders across the board to commit themselves to the cause. "This is a message that must resonate with every electorate, regardless of their current affiliations."

The Taoiseach highlighted that the concept of a united Ireland has gained traction over recent years and is no longer seen as just a pipe dream. "We have seen progress in various areas, and it is only logical that we now move towards a comprehensive and inclusive approach that brings us closer to our goal," he explained.

Varadkar acknowledged that there would be significant challenges to overcome, particularly regarding the Northern Ireland Executive, the role of the British Government, and the complexities of cross-border cooperation. However, he remained optimistic about the prospects of achieving a united Ireland through dialogue and mutual understanding.

The call for a unified stance on this issue has been welcomed by some political figures but has also met with resistance from others who maintain the status quo. Sinn Féin’s leader, Mary Lou McDonald, praised the Taoiseach for taking a bold step forward, stating that it is crucial to have this debate openly and honestly. However, unionist representatives have expressed concern, highlighting the potential risks associated with any moves towards unification without addressing the underlying issues in Northern Ireland.

The Taoiseach also outlined plans to facilitate discussions and forums where people from all backgrounds could engage in meaningful conversations about the future of the island of Ireland. He stressed that these dialogues would be essential in charting a path towards a united Ireland.

In conclusion, Taoiseach Varadkar’s call for an inclusive manifesto commitment on Irish unity is set to be a pivotal issue in the upcoming election. It remains to be seen whether other parties will follow his lead and how the public will respond to this rallying cry for a more united Ireland.
headline: Leo Varadkar wants Irish unity manifesto pledge by all parties in next election

text:
Engineers in Miami have begun the delicate process of demolishing the remaining debris of the Champlain Tower South block following its catastrophic collapse earlier this year. The incident, which occurred on 24 June, has left a significant mark on the Miami skyline and raised critical questions about building safety regulations.

The structure, a 12-storey residential building, fell into the sea after a severe storm hit the area, killing at least 9 people and leaving several others missing. According to preliminary findings, the collapse was attributed to deteriorating concrete and a lack of proper maintenance over the years.

In a scene reminiscent of disaster recovery efforts, heavy machinery and safety personnel were on site today as they prepared to dismantle what remained of the collapsed tower. The operation is expected to take several weeks and will involve extensive coordination between engineers, construction workers, and emergency services.

Speaking to reporters at the site, a spokesperson for the Miami-Dade County Department of Building Safety stated, "Our primary focus is ensuring public safety throughout this operation. We will be working closely with the community to manage any potential impacts and address concerns."

Residents from neighbouring buildings who lost loved ones in the collapse have expressed a mix of emotions, ranging from anger to relief at seeing progress being made. "It's hard to watch them tear down what once belonged to us," said Mary Connolly, a local resident and survivor. "But it's important that we move forward."

The incident has led to increased scrutiny of building safety regulations across Florida, with calls for stricter inspection protocols and more rigorous maintenance standards. A special task force has been established to review the current building codes and make recommendations for improvement.

As the demolition work progresses, officials are also considering the long-term impact on the surrounding area, particularly on the tourism industry which has been significantly affected by the negative publicity surrounding the event. Local authorities are working with hoteliers and business owners to mitigate any adverse effects on the region's economy.

The demolition of Champlain Tower South marks a critical step in the recovery process for the affected community and serves as a stark reminder of the importance of vigilance in maintaining the integrity of our built environment.
headline: Miami tower block collapse: Engineers demolish the remains of the Champlain Tower South block

text:
A migrant who had been trying to enter Europe from North Africa has been discovered alive but exhausted after being found hidden in the cramped car glove box. Emergency services were alerted to the discovery near the border of Italy and Slovenia after a routine check following reports of suspicious vehicles.

The 32-year-old man, who is of Iraqi origin, said he had been stuck in the vehicle for over 24 hours without water or food. He managed to stay hidden until a patrol car noticed the unusual temperature inside the car during the routine check.

Gardaí arrived on the scene and provided immediate assistance to the man. Paramedics from the Health Service Executive (HSE) were also present to provide medical attention. The man was reportedly dehydrated and in a state of exhaustion but is expected to make a full recovery.

Speaking at a press conference, the Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, condemned the treatment of migrants and called on European countries to work together to address the root causes of such dangerous journeys. "This is not just a humanitarian issue but a matter of human rights," he stated. "We must do more to assist those fleeing war and persecution and ensure they are treated with dignity and respect."

According to officials, this incident highlights the dangers faced by people seeking refuge in Europe. The man was in contact with human smugglers who arranged for him to be transported illegally. He hoped to reach Germany, where he has family members, but his journey took a dire turn when his vehicle broke down.

The incident has led to renewed calls for reform of Europe's migration policies and a strengthening of border security measures. The Minister for Justice, David Stanton, said, "We need to balance our responsibilities towards people in distress with the need to maintain robust border controls." He added, "It is unacceptable for anyone to be put in such perilous situations."

The discovery has prompted the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to call on member states to strengthen cooperation and protection frameworks for migrants. The organisation stated that it is committed to working with European authorities to improve conditions for migrants and refugees along migration routes.

Irish media outlets have been monitoring the situation closely, highlighting the plight of migrants and the challenges faced by both the smugglers and the authorities. The Taoiseach's office has also announced plans to host a summit next month with other EU leaders to discuss how to better manage the continent's migration crisis and ensure the safety of those seeking asylum.
headline: Migrant desperately trying to enter Europe is found hiding in cramped car glove box

text:
Ireland’s young people have long been known to venture abroad in search of better prospects, but the statistics for 2025 paint a stark picture that has left many wondering if the emigration wave is now an unstoppable tide. The latest figures from the Central Statistics Office (CSO) show that a record-breaking 160,000 individuals aged 18 to 34 left the country last year, marking a significant increase from previous years. This unprecedented level of emigration is raising concerns among policymakers and social commentators alike.

The reasons for this exodus are multifaceted, with the high cost of housing taking centre stage. In Dublin, the cost of a three-bedroom apartment has reached €700,000, making it almost impossible for young professionals and graduates to secure a foot on the property ladder. Even those who have managed to find employment in their field often find themselves living in shared accommodations or returning to the family home, delaying the establishment of independent households.

“Homeownership has become a distant dream,” said Cian McCarthy, a software engineer who moved to London to pursue career opportunities. “The prices here are just too steep. It feels like every week I’m priced out further. The irony is that I could make a much higher salary in Dublin, but the cost of living and the cost of housing don’t match up.”

This trend is not limited to just Dublin. Across other cities and towns, the issue of affordability is leading to a brain drain that could severely impact the economy in the future. Small businesses, particularly in tech and creative sectors, are finding it difficult to retain talent due to the inability to offer competitive living conditions for their employees.

The government’s response so far has been largely inadequate, with schemes aimed at alleviating the housing crisis facing criticism for being too slow and insufficient. The National Development Plan (NDP) allocated €5 billion towards the construction of social and affordable housing, but progress has been glacial, with many expecting a more robust and immediate solution.

“While the government talks about long-term plans and targets, young people need solutions today,” stated Aoife Ryan, spokesperson for Young Irelanders United, a youth advocacy group. “We need action now to address the immediate needs of our generation. This isn’t just about homes; it’s about the future of our country.”

Education and training programmes, designed to prepare young people for the workforce, also fall short when they fail to equip graduates with the skills needed for the job market, leaving them struggling to find meaningful employment in Ireland. As a result, many are forced to seek opportunities elsewhere, where the cost of living is more manageable, even if salaries are lower.

The exodus of young people is not only a personal tragedy for those leaving but also a societal one. The loss of talent, energy, and dynamism could have profound effects on Ireland’s economic and social fabric. The country stands at a crossroads, where decisive action is required to halt this exodus and create a sustainable future for its younger generation.

As we move forward, it is imperative that the government listens to the voices of those affected and implements measures that will make Ireland an attractive place to live and work again. Only then can we hope to see a reversal of this worrying trend and ensure that Ireland’s future is built on the foundations of its young people.
headline: Gone for good? Ireland’s youth exodus accelerates as record numbers emigrated in 2025 as homeownership remains a pipe dream

text:
A devastating train collision on Thursday night has claimed at least 36 lives and injured more than 150 others in central Greece, prompting an urgent investigation into the cause of the accident. The crash occurred on the Athens–Thessaloniki railway line near the city of Larissa, about halfway between the two major cities.

Eyewitnesses described the scene as chaotic, with emergency services working tirelessly to extricate trapped passengers from the wreckage. "The impact was massive," said one local resident, who asked not to be named. "Smoke was everywhere, and there was just a terrible noise."

According to initial reports from the Hellenic Railways Organisation (OSE), the collision involved a passenger train and a goods train, which derailed after coming into contact with each other. The exact circumstances of the crash are still being investigated, but preliminary findings suggest possible technical failures as well as human error could have contributed to the tragedy.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis condemned the accident during a press conference held Friday morning. "Our thoughts are with the families of those affected and we will do everything in our power to ensure justice is served," he said.

In the aftermath of the disaster, the Greek government announced plans to provide immediate support to survivors and their families, including financial assistance, psychological support, and relocation services if necessary. Minister for Transport Nikos Hardalias stated that the government would review all safety measures across the national rail network.

The accident has sparked widespread concern among Greek citizens and political leaders alike. Opposition parties called for a full and transparent inquiry to prevent future incidents. "This is a wake-up call for the entire transportation sector," said Maria Georgopoulou, spokesperson for the opposition Syriza party. "Safety must be our top priority."

International solidarity has also been expressed, with neighbouring countries offering condolences and assistance. The European Commission has pledged support, emphasizing the importance of robust safety protocols within the European railway network.

As the nation mourns, the focus now shifts to ensuring that those responsible are held accountable and that necessary reforms are implemented to prevent similar tragedies in the future.
headline: No fewer than 36 people dead following train collision in Greece

text:
Health expert Dr Brian Glynn has warned that Ireland now finds itself in a precarious position with the reproduction rate (R number) of the coronavirus hovering between 1.2 and 1.8. Speaking at a press conference today, Dr Glynn highlighted the critical importance of adhering to public health measures as the country continues to navigate the pandemic.

"The current R number indicates that each infected person is infecting, on average, more than one other person," Dr Glynn explained. "While this might sound like a small increase, it can quickly lead to a significant rise in cases if not properly controlled."

The National Public Health Emergency Team (NPHET) has been closely monitoring the situation and has advised that sustained adherence to existing guidelines is essential. These include wearing masks in public indoor settings, maintaining physical distancing, and ensuring good hygiene practices.

"Given the current figures, we must remain vigilant," stated the Tánaiste and Minister for Health, Leo Varadkar. "We cannot afford any complacency; every individual’s actions play a crucial role in preventing the spread of the virus."

Dr Glynn also urged the public to be mindful of the impact their decisions have on the healthcare system. "Our hospitals and healthcare workers have done a phenomenal job thus far, but the continued pressure from a rising case count could strain our resources significantly," he said.

Meanwhile, the Government has indicated its commitment to further support measures to keep the economy afloat, while balancing the need for public health safety. The Minister for Enterprise, Trade and Employment, Simon Coveney, stated that additional financial aid may be on the way for businesses affected by the current conditions.

As the country grapples with the latest data, experts emphasise the necessity of collective responsibility. "This is not just about individuals' rights or freedoms, but about protecting the lives and livelihoods of everyone in society," Dr Glynn concluded.

The Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, has called for a unity of purpose among the nation in responding to these challenges. "We stand together stronger in times of adversity, and this is certainly a time when we must all pull together," he remarked.

With the festive season approaching, public health officials are particularly concerned about potential super-spreader events, urging people to avoid large gatherings where social distancing may be difficult to maintain. "Let’s make the right choices this holiday season to ensure that our progress so far is not wasted," Dr Glynn implored the public.
headline: Dr Glynn says Ireland is in a precarious position as R number is between 1.2 and 1.8

Fianna Gearmánaíochta's (Irish Freedom Party) leader, Cian Ó Fágla TD, is leading an impassioned campaign in the European Parliament to resist the requirement for MEPs, staff, and visitors to present a COVID-19 vaccination certificate.

The Irish politician has been at the forefront of challenging the recently introduced mandate, which has sparked controversy among some MEPs who argue it violates individual freedoms and the right to travel without being subjected to health mandates.

In a statement issued last week, Ó Fágla TD expressed strong opposition to the measure, stating, "This is an egregious overreach of authority and a clear violation of our democratic rights. No one should be coerced into accepting a vaccine as a condition of participation in public spaces."

During a recent debate in the European Parliament, Ó Fágla TD highlighted the potential for discrimination and inequality, citing instances where individuals may face barriers to entry due to vaccination status, regardless of their health circumstances.

"The introduction of this requirement is not only unjust but also counterproductive," said Ó Fágla TD. "It sends a message that we value compliance over human dignity and personal choice."

The Irish party's stance has garnered support from various quarters, including local TDs and civic groups across Ireland. However, it has also drawn criticism from pro-vaccination advocates who argue that such measures are necessary to combat the ongoing pandemic.

In a separate development, the Irish Government has stated that while they respect the position of the Irish Freedom Party, they will continue to adhere to public health guidelines set by the European Union. A spokesperson for the Department of Health noted, "Vaccination remains the most effective way to protect against severe illness and help prevent the spread of the virus. We urge all citizens to make informed decisions based on the latest scientific advice."

As the debate continues, the Irish delegation in the European Parliament faces increasing pressure to find common ground in a highly polarized issue. With the Irish Freedom Party's tenacity and commitment to opposing the mandate, it seems clear that this will not be a quick or easy resolution.

In a move that has sparked debate and intrigue across Ireland and beyond, former President Mary Robinson and the renowned musical group U2 have been jointly awarded the prestigious European Order of Merit. This accolade, known for recognising individuals who have made significant contributions to society, culture, or public life in Europe, is seen as a high honour in the European Union.

Mary Robinson, the first female and the second president of Ireland, was sworn into office in 1990 and served until 1997. Her tenure was marked by a focus on human rights and environmental issues, and she has continued to advocate for these causes since leaving the presidency. Despite her efforts, she has faced criticism over recent years regarding her handling of certain aspects of her time in office.

The band U2, whose members have included Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton, and Larry Mullen Jr., has been a global phenomenon since its formation in Dublin in 1976. The group has sold millions of albums worldwide and won numerous awards, including multiple Grammy Awards and the Brit Award for Outstanding Contribution to Music. Their music often addresses themes of social and political activism, making their inclusion in this award particularly noteworthy.

A statement released by the European Commission cited the recipients' "outstanding contributions" to various fields, without providing specific details about how they met the criteria for receiving this honour. The decision to award both a former political figure and a rock band has raised questions about the criteria used for the selection process.

Reacting to the news, a spokesperson for the European Commission stated, "We are pleased to acknowledge the immense impact that both Mary Robinson and U2 have had on their respective domains, and their contributions to European values and culture."

Critics, however, have pointed out that the award may appear somewhat incongruous, given the different backgrounds of the recipients. One critic noted, "While it’s laudable to recognise cultural and public figures, the choice of awarding such a prestigious title to both a former Irish president and a rock band might blur the lines between recognising significant contributions and perhaps pandering to public interest."

The award ceremony for the European Order of Merit is scheduled to take place later this year in Brussels. Both Mary Robinson and U2 have expressed gratitude for the recognition, although details of their responses have not been publicly disclosed at this stage.

As this development continues to unfold, it will be interesting to see how the award is received in Ireland and how it influences public opinion on both recipients.
headline: Two has-beens? Mary Robinson and U2 are being awarded European Order of Merit

The Brexit Withdrawal Agreement has been swiftly approved by both Houses of the British Parliament today, with overwhelming support from members of the House of Commons and a majority in the House of Lords. This development marks a significant step towards the formal departure of the United Kingdom from the European Union, with the date now set for 31st January 2020.

Prime Minister Boris Johnson, who has been at the helm of this process, hailed the passage of the agreement as a "milestone" in the UK’s journey to independence. Speaking to the media after the vote, Johnson expressed his gratitude to lawmakers and said that this is a clear mandate from Parliament to proceed with Brexit as scheduled. 

In the Dáil and Seanad Éireann, Irish political leaders reacted cautiously, acknowledging the importance of the move while urging continued dialogue between the UK and the EU. TDs and Senators were quick to point out the potential implications for Ireland's peace process and economic ties, particularly along the border in Northern Ireland. The Taoiseach, Leo Varadkar, stated, "While we welcome the agreement's passage, there remains much work to be done to ensure a smooth and just transition for all parties involved."

Gardaí and local authorities have prepared contingency plans for potential disruptions, although they hope the new arrangement will prevent any major issues. The Health Service Executive (HSE) is also assessing the agreement's impact on healthcare services, especially cross-border ones.

The European Union's response was swift and supportive. EU institutions welcomed the vote, emphasising their commitment to working closely with the UK during the coming months to finalise the future relationship agreement. President Charles Michel highlighted the EU’s readiness to engage in negotiations with Britain to maintain strong economic and social ties.

The withdrawal agreement itself aims to address several contentious issues, including the Irish border, citizens' rights, and financial settlements. However, key questions remain regarding the implementation of these provisions and the ongoing negotiation of a comprehensive trade deal.

As the clock ticks down to the 31st, all eyes are on Brussels and London as talks continue to solidify the terms of the future relationship between the UK and the EU. While many see today’s vote as a clear indicator of Britain's determination to leave, the road ahead is fraught with challenges that could yet lead to further delays or renegotiations.
headline: Brexit Withdrawal Agreement breezes through Parliament, meaning Britain will likely leave the EU for good on January 31, 2020

The Green Party TD, Roderic O’Gorman, has issued a stark warning to voters across the country, urging them to avoid electing independent candidates who might support a coalition government. Speaking at a press conference in Dublin yesterday, O’Gorman highlighted the potential risks associated with such a move, particularly for environmental policies.

"The Greens stand firm on our commitment to protect the environment and achieve our climate targets," O'Gorman stated. "We cannot afford to see these hard-won goals put at risk through the influence of independent voices who may have different priorities."

O'Gorman stressed that while the Green Party has been open to working with other parties on certain issues, an independent supporting a coalition would jeopardize the party's ability to push for ambitious green policies. He cited recent experiences where independent voices within coalitions have watered down key environmental legislation.

"This is not just about our party," O'Gorman added. "It's about all citizens who care deeply about our planet. We need a government that will commit to real action on climate change and sustainability, and that means we must be united behind a party that shares those values."

Green Party officials expressed concern over the rising support for independents among disillusioned voters, especially in rural areas where the party had previously struggled to make inroads. However, they were keen to point out that their own electoral success in recent years demonstrated a growing appetite for green policies and a desire to see these initiatives prioritised.

The Green Party's position comes as the political landscape remains fluid, with various independents and small parties considering their options ahead of the general election scheduled for May next year. The Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, has indicated that he is open to negotiations with any willing partners, including independents, in the event that his Fianna Fáil–Fine Gael alliance fails to secure a majority.

While the Green Party's call for unity behind its platform is resonating with some, others are calling for a more inclusive approach to governance. A spokesperson for one of the smaller independent candidates said, "Voters want change and they don't want to see political parties dictating which voices can contribute to the debate. We believe our experience and local knowledge are essential assets in forming a strong and effective government."

The debate over the role of independents in the next Irish government continues to shape the political discourse, with the Greens standing firm on their stance. As the election approaches, O'Gorman’s words ring loud: "Do not let independents prop up a coalition that might compromise on the very principles you hold dear."
headline: Please don’t do it! Green’s Roderic O’Gorman warns public against independents propping up coalition

text:
The rise of online casinos has been a significant development in the Irish gambling landscape, with a noticeable impact on the national economy. These digital platforms have become increasingly popular, offering players from Ireland and beyond a myriad of options to engage in gaming, thereby contributing to the country’s economic growth.

According to data from PwC, the Irish online gambling market is estimated to be worth over €160 million annually, with a substantial portion coming from online casino revenues. This sector not only boosts the overall revenue but also provides employment opportunities across various sectors, from software development and customer service to marketing and finance.

One of the key contributions of online casinos to the economy is the creation of jobs. According to the HSE (Health Service Executive), there has been a notable increase in employment in the digital sector, with many roles created specifically for the online casino industry. This includes positions such as game developers, software engineers, and customer support staff, all contributing to Ireland’s growing tech workforce.

Moreover, the presence of online casinos has led to increased foreign direct investment (FDI) into the country. Companies looking to tap into the lucrative Irish market have invested in local talent and infrastructure, leading to further job creation and skill development. This trend is especially evident in regions with established tech hubs, such as Dublin and Cork.

However, the economic benefits of online casinos are not without controversy. Critics argue that these platforms contribute to gambling addiction, which can lead to social and personal issues. The HSE and other health organisations have highlighted the need for stringent regulation to protect consumers and ensure responsible gambling practices.

To address these concerns, the government has taken steps to introduce stricter regulations. The Department of Justice and Equality, in conjunction with the Central Bank of Ireland, has developed guidelines aimed at ensuring the integrity and safety of online gambling operations. This includes measures such as age verification, enhanced security protocols, and the introduction of responsible gambling tools.

Furthermore, the introduction of the Online Gaming Act 2023 is expected to provide a more robust regulatory framework for the industry. This legislation aims to strengthen oversight, protect vulnerable individuals, and ensure fair competition among operators. It is hoped that these measures will help mitigate some of the risks associated with online gambling while still allowing the sector to thrive.

In terms of prospects, the outlook for online casinos remains positive. With the ongoing shift towards digital services and the increasing sophistication of online gambling platforms, the potential for growth is substantial. The global pandemic has accelerated this trend, as people have turned to digital entertainment more than ever before.

Local online gambling operators have been at the forefront of innovation, developing user-friendly platforms that cater to diverse needs and preferences. Many have also invested in marketing campaigns that promote responsible gambling, aligning with the regulatory goals set by the government.

As the industry continues to evolve, it will be crucial for policymakers, regulatory bodies, and industry stakeholders to work together to balance economic benefits with public welfare. By doing so, Ireland can harness the full potential of online casinos to contribute to its economic recovery while safeguarding the well-being of its citizens.
headline: The Impact of Online Casinos on the Irish Economy: Analysis and Prospects

text:
A new recruit to An Garda Síochána has been discovered in a ditch along the M1 motorway following the abandonment of his patrol car. The incident occurred near Portadown, County Armagh, early this morning.

The garda, who is believed to be a trainee, was discovered in critical condition and rushed to a nearby hospital where he remains in a serious but stable condition. According to officials from the Health Service Executive (HSE), the individual had sustained significant injuries.

The car was found parked on the hard shoulder of the M1, with the engine off, and the key left inside. Gardaí confirmed that the door was unlocked, which is standard protocol during training exercises, raising questions about the individual’s state of mind.

The District Court will convene to hear the details of the incident, and a full investigation is ongoing by the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP). The Department of Justice stated that they are closely monitoring the situation and will provide further updates when appropriate.

The Taoiseach and the Tánaiste have both expressed their shock at the incident, calling for a thorough examination of the training procedures in place for new recruits.

Irish Road Safety Authority (IRSA) spokesperson, commenting on the dangerous practice of leaving a vehicle unattended, said, "This is a stark reminder of the importance of road safety and proper protocols."

Local residents have expressed concern over the safety implications of such incidents and called for increased vigilance on Ireland’s roads.

As investigations continue, the Garda Síochána have appealed to the public to remain vigilant and report any suspicious activity involving police cars or officers.
headline: Newbie Garda found in ditch after abandoning car on M1 motorway

text:
Cork Airport has issued a word of caution to passengers and visitors regarding travel arrangements in light of current adverse weather conditions. A spokesperson for the airport has advised all individuals planning to visit the facility to stay informed about the latest developments and to check with the airport directly before making any travel plans.

The spokesperson highlighted that heavy rain and strong winds have caused disruptions and delays at several other airports across the country, and while Cork Airport is currently operating within normal parameters, the situation could change rapidly.

"Passengers are encouraged to monitor the latest updates on our website and social media platforms, where we provide real-time information on flight status and any potential changes," the spokesperson stated. "We appreciate the understanding and patience of all our customers during these challenging times."

The spokesperson also reminded the public that the safety of all travellers remains a top priority for the airport authorities. "We are closely monitoring the weather and will take any necessary steps to ensure the safety and comfort of everyone visiting our premises," they added.

In the meantime, the airport's operations team is on high alert to manage any issues that may arise and to keep the travelling public well-informed. The spokesperson encouraged all those heading to the airport to allow extra time for their journeys and to remain vigilant about changing conditions.
headline: Cork Airport spokesperson advises people to be cautious when traveling to the facility due to adverse weather conditions

text:
The High Court in Dublin has ruled against two women from County Clare in a case involving fraudulent insurance claims, with the presiding judge branding their claims "shocking" and "despicable". The case, which saw the women accuse a Dublin-based taxi driver of serious offences including sexual assault, has now been thrown out.

The claimants, both from rural areas of County Clare, had travelled to Dublin seeking to file insurance claims following alleged incidents with the taxi driver. According to court documents, the women claimed they had been assaulted by the driver on separate occasions over several months, necessitating significant medical and psychological treatment. However, the court heard evidence that cast serious doubt on the veracity of these claims.

The presiding judge, Mr Justice Ó Fearghail, expressed his disapproval during the hearing, stating that the women’s actions amounted to an affront to the judicial process. "This is not a court for such frivolous and baseless allegations," he said, adding that the claims were without merit and represented a significant waste of court resources.

The Gardaí were called in to investigate the claims after concerns were raised about inconsistencies in the accounts provided by the women. Following a thorough investigation, it was determined that the women had knowingly submitted false information to the insurance company and the court.

The Taxi Drivers Association welcomed the judge’s decision, with spokesperson Niamh O’Donovan stating, "This is a clear message to all who might think of making similar claims; the legal system will not tolerate such deception."

The two women involved, who cannot be named due to court proceedings, have not commented publicly on the outcome of the case. Their lawyer issued a statement indicating that the couple had always maintained their innocence and would be appealing the decision.

The High Court’s ruling has drawn condemnation from victims' rights groups, who argue that such cases can take a severe emotional toll and should not be treated so lightly. They urge the justice system to be more sympathetic to genuine victims of crime while also ensuring that those making false claims are held accountable.

The case highlights the importance of integrity within the legal and insurance systems and raises questions about the accuracy of claims made by individuals who may seek financial gains through fraudulent means. It also underscores the commitment of the judicial system to upholding justice and ensuring that the rights of genuine victims are protected.
headline: Angered judge throws out ‘fraudulent’ insurance claims from Co Clare women against Dublin taxi driver

text:
A tragic incident occurred on the morning of 10th June off the coast of Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, where a 26-year-old mother from Ireland met a violent end after being attacked by a shark while swimming with her young daughter. The victim, who has not yet been formally named, was accompanied by her child when they ventured into the ocean.

The incident took place approximately two miles off the beach of Playa Los Muertos, where a large number of tourists and local residents had gathered to enjoy the water activities. Eyewitnesses reported hearing a commotion and screams before rushing to the area. They found the woman’s body near the shoreline, with her daughter clinging to her. Emergency services were immediately alerted, but despite the best efforts of both local lifeguards and paramedics, the mother was pronounced dead at the scene.

Local authorities have stated that a tiger shark is suspected of the attack, given the type of injuries observed. The Gardaí, along with officials from the Mexican authorities, are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident, including whether any safety protocols may have been overlooked.

The victim, described by her family as a beloved mother and sister, had recently returned to Ireland from her holiday in Mexico. Her daughter, who was severely shaken by the experience, is receiving support from the HSE’s Children First team. The family has requested privacy during this difficult time.

Irish Tourism Minister, Simon Coveney, expressed his condolences to the family and the Irish community. “This is a devastating tragedy,” he said, “and our thoughts are very much with the bereaved family. It is important to remember that such incidents are extremely rare, and Irish tourists should continue to enjoy their holidays in Mexico safely.”

The incident has prompted discussions about shark safety measures and the importance of adhering to guidelines provided by local authorities. Beaches in the region have since been closely monitored by lifeguards, and additional warnings have been issued to swimmers.

In a statement, the Irish High Commission in Mexico assured all Irish citizens in the area that appropriate assistance and support are available. They also reminded the public to follow all safety advice and to heed warnings from local authorities.
headline: 26-yr-old mother dies after attack by shark in Mexico while swimming with daughter

text:
Gardaí are conducting a major search operation in a remote wasteland area near Dundalk town following the tragic death of teenager Kyran Durnin. The search, which began this morning and involves a significant number of Garda officers, is centered around an area close to where the Durnin family previously resided.

The incident has been closely followed by the local community and national media, with residents expressing concern and cooperation with the authorities. The search area, described by local residents as a neglected and dangerous region, has become the focus of intense interest due to its proximity to the deceased's former residence.

Kyran Durnin was found deceased on the evening of last Wednesday in circumstances that are still being investigated. The family has been providing support to one another during this difficult time. The Dáil and the Tánaiste have issued statements expressing their condolences to the family and offering any necessary assistance.

Local TDs from the area have also commented on the tragic event, with one TD stating, "This is a deeply troubling and heartbreaking situation for the family and the community. The Gardaí must be given the resources and support they need to uncover the full facts surrounding this case."

As the search continues, local community members have expressed hope for swift resolution and emphasised the importance of maintaining vigilance and cooperation with law enforcement agencies. The community has organised vigils and support groups for the family, as well as those who are grieving the loss of Kyran Durnin.
